Headline: Osaka’s G20 summit likely to impede logistics operations from June 27-30
Details:
Japan will host its first ever Group of Twenty (G20) summit at Osaka’s International Exhibition Center on June 28-29, 2019. The G20 summit is held annually for governments of 20 member nations to discuss a wide range of issues affecting the world’s economy. In light of the high profile event, Japanese authorities have released a statement detailing large-scale traffic and sea restrictions near Osaka Port, Kansai International Airport (KIX), as well as within Osaka city during the summit period. As KIX is the country’s third largest airport and a key logistics hub for engineering and automotive companies from southern and central regions of Japan, heightened security checks and restrictions may significantly affect cargo handling and delivery for industries that rely heavily on this route. 

Organizers of the G20 summit reportedly aim to reduce traffic by 50 percent for four days, during and leading up to the event. To this end, local authorities have set up traffic restrictions in and around Osaka especially for roads connecting to KIX. The airport is built on an artificial island in Osaka Bay; thus the bridge that connects KIX to Rinku town on the main island will be the most impacted route, particularly on June 27 and June 30 during the arrival and departure of head of states. 

From June 27-30, 10 major sections of Hanshin Expressway including No.1 Loop Route and the Gulf Line totaling about 160 kilometers that connects to KIX, hotels, and the summit venue will be closed to traffic from morning until late evening to facilitate movement of delegates and participants of the summit. As a result, traffic will likely be diverted to other expressways such as Meishin Expressway. In Osaka, traffic restrictions will be in effect at 9 locations: Osaka Station, Nakanoshima, Tenma, Osaka Castle, Honcho, Uehoncho, Namba, Tennoji, and Nanko. 

In order to access international cargo and fuel supply areas, authorities have set up a fixed route bus that goes from Kansai Airport Station to these areas. However, the bus may not operate normally due to traffic restrictions and logistics providers have been advised to allow for extra travel time. 

According to official statements by the local authorities, heightened security checks can be expected at three main entry points in Kansai region: Kansai International Airport, Osaka International Airport (also known as Itami Airport), and Kobe Airport. Due to their proximity to the event venue, Kansai and Osaka Airports will be used widely by the participants and both airports have released statements pertaining to cargo inspections. 

While no airlines have publicly announced additional flights during the aforementioned period, both airports have pre-warned about possible flight delays on June 27 and June 30 due to the arrival and departure of aircrafts carrying heads of states and government officials. Both airports also have prohibited flying drones above and around the facilities; KIX in particular has restricted flying drones within 1,000 meters of the airport. 

According to the statement released by authorities, all vessels entering the sea near Osaka Port and KIX from June 24–30 are requested to provide prior notification to Japan’s maritime security department by noon at least the day before the planned navigation date. Failure to do so would result in longer berthing times. Shipping companies can submit earlier notifications to the nearest maritime security department starting from June 3–19. In addition, vessels are also requested to refrain from entering designated restricted areas, referred to as ""voluntary navigation restraint sea area"", around the airport island and the ""exclusive use sea area"" between the two parts of the island.

Traffic restrictions in and out of KIX for 4-days are likely to be the main challenge for Everstream Analytics customers with airfreight as collection service for KIX from major domestic shipping companies and delivery service centered in Osaka are likely to be disrupted, particularly on June 27 and 30. In addition to road restrictions, security spot checks on vehicles and cargo inspections may take longer than usual prior to and during the summit.

It is possible that local freight forwarders may pick up imported air cargo arriving during the G20 summit period from July 1 onwards. Thus, customers are advised to liaise with local contacts to avoid delays for critical cargo, such as perishable or pharmaceutical goods, that may require special handling. Alternatively, customers can also consider rerouting shipments to Tokyo’s Narita Airport to avoid delays. This option was used by manufacturers when KIX was shut down for 3-days due to the destruction caused by Typhoon Jebi in 2018.

Headline: UPDATE - USA, Virginia: Tropical Storm Michael results in fatalities, power outages, and road closures overnight in Virginia
Details: Media sources are confirming at least five storm-related fatalities in Virginia as a result of Tropical Storm Michael overnight. As of this morning, the Virginia Department of Emergency Management released statistics confirming the fatalities as well as indicating that around 520,000 are without power and nearly 1,200 roadways are closed due to flooding and downed trees. Emergency officials are urging motorists to take extra precautions if transiting the area. A Flood Warning remains in effect in the eastern region of Virginia until 10:45 EDT. Travelers are advised to actively monitor weather and media outlets for situational updates. Motorists should keep apprised of ongoing road closures via traffic reports and avoid areas where flood conditions persist.

Clients are advised to avoid all impacted areas and terrain, as the fires remain uncontained and hazardous. Refer to official and media sources for the latest information on the situation. Adhere to all instructions issued by local authorities.

Headline: Hong Kong: Junior Police Officers' Association calls for curfew and tougher emergency powers in SAR
Details: In the aftermath of yesterday's flashpoint unrest in Hong Kong, on the anniversary of China's National Day, the Special Administrative Region's (SAR) largest police group, the Junior Police Officers' Association, has called for curfew and tougher emergency powers. The law would also allow censorship, arrests, detentions and deportations, the control of ports and all transport, the appropriation of property, and authorises the entry and search of premises. The law was last used in 1967.

Headline: COVID-19 Causing Backlog of Cargo at Karachi Port; 180 Trucks Stranded at Libya-Tunisia Border
Details:
On Thursday, Pakistani media sources reported that as of April 15, some 1,900 shipping containers had accumulated at Karachi Port due to a decision by the government to halt trade with neighboring Afghanistan amid the COVID-19 pandemic. However, officials indicated that they expected the backlog to ease in the near future, as while the Pakistani government extended a nationwide shutdown and restrictions on public gatherings for another two weeks on April 14, some so-called “low-risk” industries have been allowed to reopen, including construction, agriculture, e-commerce, paper, and packaging, among others, with export orders to resume soon as well. Meanwhile, Libyan media outlets reported that 180 cargo trucks have been stranded at the country’s border with Tunisia for several weeks due to COVID-19-related travel restrictions. The trucks are reportedly loaded with foodstuffs bound for Libya but have been unable to enter the country or return to Tunisia due to the countries’ respective coronavirus containment efforts, which include the closure of their shared border.



Assessment: The developments highlight how efforts to contain COVID-19 have negatively affected supply chains in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). Indeed, commercial shipping operations largely continue throughout region, as, despite many countries having curbed cross-border travel, air, sea, and overland cargo shipments have generally been exempt from such directives. Still, coronavirus-induced restrictions, notably mandatory quarantines, nightly curfews, and enhanced screening procedures, have reduced the capacities of some service providers, delayed cargo handovers and inspections, and extended lead-times, among other issues, leading to incurring storage and demurrage at ports and delays at borders for customs. With some MENA nations having begun to relax such measures, associated disruptions may soon start to dissipate. That said, residual backlogs and service delivery delays should be anticipated.

Headline: 40 miles W of Columbia- Florence continues to weaken; additional flooding expected. Incident closed.

The storm is located approximately 40 miles west of Columbia, South Carolina and exhibiting maximum sustained winds of 35 miles per hour with higher gusts. Florence is expected to turn and dissipate over the Northeast in the next couple of days.

Over 30 inches of rain have been recorded near Swansboro, North Carolina and more than 25 inches have been recorded in Newport, North Carolina. Florence is expected to continue to produce excessive rainfall in southern and central portions of North Carolina and into the far northeast of South Carolina. 

Significant impacts including flooding and structural damage have reported across the Southeast and Mid-Atlantic regions, especially in South Carolina, North Carolina, and Virginia. Widespread evacuations remain in place across North Carolina. Approximately one million people were initially evacuated. Major flooding continues to be reported in coastal North Carolina; approximately 400 swift water rescues took place in New Bern and thousands of buildings have sustained damage. Multiple tornado touchdowns were reported down in NC over the past couple of days. Numerous major roads continue to be intermittently closed due to high water and debris. There have been at least 14 storm-related deaths. 

Governors Roy Cooper of North Carolina, Henry McMaster of South Carolina, Ralph Northam of Virginia, Larry Hogan of Maryland, and Nathan Deal of Georgia all preemptively declared states of emergency for their respective states. This incident is closed.

Headline: Mutant Virus Strain May Result in Produce Shortages, Supply Chain Disruptions, Rising Prices in UK
Details:
On Saturday, December 19, British Prime Minister Boris Johnson announced a new set of restrictive measures due to the emergence of a novel mutant strain of the SARS-CoV-2 virus that causes COVID-19. Preliminary analyses indicate that the strain, which has been dubbed VUI-202012/01, is approximately 70 percent more effectively transmitted from person to person than the existing variant of SARS-CoV-2. The World Health Organization has stated that there is currently no indication that VUI-202012/01 results in more severe COVID-19 than the existing variant of the virus, nor does it possess higher morbidity. As of this writing, there has been no indication that current COVID-19 vaccines are less effective against this variant of the virus. New restrictions imposed across England include shifting areas such as London into Tier 4, wherein residents are to stay at home with the exception of essential activities, and non-essential international travel is banned. Media reports have emerged indicating that additional police units are being deployed to transport hubs such as train stations across the affected areas to enforce compliance with restrictive measures. Furthermore, a number of countries in Europe, including Germany, the Netherlands, France, and Switzerland, as well as elsewhere, have imposed a precautionary ban on travel into their respective territories from the UK for the foreseeable future. While there were no indications of associated bans on travel from mainland Europe into other countries in the region at the time of this writing, it is worth noting that VUI-202012/01 has reportedly also been detected in Denmark, Belgium, and the Netherlands. 



Media reports have emerged indicating that associated restrictions and travel bans are resulting in disruptions to cargo transport, and British ports, which have already been under pressure due to COVID-19 restrictions and a recent uptick in worldwide container traffic, are under increasing strain. Royal Mail has purportedly suspended deliveries of packages and letters from the UK to mainland Europe, and postal services from other countries in the region, such as Germany, to the UK and the Republic of Ireland have likewise been suspended for the foreseeable future. The European Union held a meeting to discuss the bloc’s response to the emergence of VUI-202012/01 on December 21; however, there were no indications as to any conclusions drawn from the meeting known at the time of this writing. 



Assessment: While the novel mutant strain of SARS-CoV-2 is reportedly not associated with higher morbidity, a surge in daily new deaths in the UK is likely in the foreseeable future off the back of rising daily case incidence resultant from higher transmissibility of VUI-202012/01. As the vaccination campaign progresses in the country, community immunization efforts may mitigate the negative impacts of the recent outbreak of this strain. It is worth noting, however, that media reports have emerged suggesting that this strain initially emerged in the UK in September but remained at low levels nationwide until mid-November, when its transmission may have been propagated by an unspecified “super-spreader” event. As such, the possibility that further restrictive measures on movement and/or gatherings may be imposed across England in the coming days and weeks in an effort to curb viral spread cannot be ruled out. 



Tier 4 restrictions and travel bans imposed on the UK by other countries are likely to incur supply chain disruptions to businesses from a variety of sectors, such as manufacturing, due to delays in imports and exports or cancellations of deliveries. Such disruptions are likely to result in financial losses to impacted organizations and, as daily case incidence in the UK is currently on an incremental trajectory, the possibility that these restrictions and associated disruptions may persist for the coming weeks cannot be ruled out. Disruptions to cargo transport may result in shortages of produce, including food, and associated rising prices within the UK for the foreseeable future. It is worth noting, however, that government officials have indicated that only some 19 percent of daily freight traffic is foreseen to be affected by travel bans and other restrictions. It is advised to continue monitoring developments associated with the emergence of VUI-202012/01 in the UK and elsewhere, related restrictions on transit and cargo transport, and heightened police presence across Tier 4 areas. Moreover, it is recommended to be vigilant to the potential for disruptions to supply chains through the UK and possible future shortages of produce in the country.

Details: Indonesia media sources indicated that authorities in Jakarta are planning to extend an odd-even traffic policy until the end of the year following the closing of Asian Para Games which had finished on October 13. Ahmad Yani. However, it does not apply on the nearest intersection up to the toll gates. The traffic policy has been implemented prior to the 2018 Asian Games in order to ease traffic congestion for athletes and visitors. Customers with interest in land freight movement in Indonesia are advised to liaise with local service providers to keep abreast of the latest traffic regulations.

Headline: Security Increased Ahead of SEA Games on Luzon Island between 11/30 and 12/11
Details:
On Monday, the Philippine National Police (PNP) called for a full alert status in the National Capital Region (NCR) and Regions I, III, and IV-A ahead of the 30th Southeast Asian (SEA) Games between Saturday, November 30, and Wednesday, December 11. The full alert will continue until December 14. The alert has been called as a precaution, and the PNP previously said that they are not aware of any imminent threats to the games. At least 27,000 security personnel will be deployed to secure the SEA Games, including 17,700 Metro Manila police officers.

Assessment: Around 10,000 athletes and their support staff are expected to attend the games. The games are being held in dozens of venues across Luzon Island, which have been divided into four clusters: the Metro Manila cluster, the Clark cluster, the Subic cluster, and other areas. The list of venues can be found here: https://2019seagames.com/venues.html. There continues to be a threat from Islamist militant groups in the country, although their strongholds are in the southern Philippines and are far away from the event venues in Luzon. However, the prominent nature of the games are undoubtedly an attractive target for terrorists, and police disrupted a terrorist plot targeting the previous SEA Games in Malaysia in 2017. The plot was organized by the Philippine-based Abu Sayyaf militant group. Customers are advised to expect an increased security presence around event venues, transportation hubs, and other prominent locations, which could result in associated delays for the duration of the games. A heightened level of situational awareness should also be exercised due to the persistent threat of terrorism across the Philippines.

Headline: COVID-19 Cases Within Royal Family Reflect Authorities’ Difficulty Controlling Transmission
Details:
On Thursday, the New York Times, citing local sources, reported that 150 members of Saudi Arabia’s royal family have contracted coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). Citing an internal memo sent out at King Faisal Specialist Hospital, the Times reported that among those infected is a senior prince who is governor of Riyadh and is in intensive care. As many as 500 beds are reportedly being set up at the hospital to treat a potential influx of sick royals and their associates. Doctors and those close to the royal family believe that many of the cases were likely imported from Europe, to which Saudi princes routinely travel. King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MbS) have reportedly isolated themselves at remote palaces along the kingdom’s Red Sea coast, near Jeddah. As of Thursday, Saudi health authorities had registered 3,287 positive COVID-19 infections, along with 44 associated deaths.



Assessment: The reports of COVID-19 infections spreading within the royal family reflect the difficulty experienced by Saudi authorities in preventing the spread of the virus. Indeed, the Saudi government has ordered some of the most stringent containment measures in the region, with the sickness within the royal family potentially a motivating factor for the speed in which they were adopted, as well as an indicator of the seriousness of the situation. Still, the kingdom’s health minister predicted on Tuesday that new coronavirus cases could surge to as many as 200,000 in the next few weeks, signaling that Saudi’s COVID-19 curve continues to rise, with a sharper trajectory possible in the near future.

Headline: Chicago Teachers Union Strike Expected to Begin on Thursday as Negotiations with CPS Continuing
Details:
A teacher strike affecting Chicago Public Schools (CPS) involving at least 30,000 teachers with the Chicago Teachers Union (CTU), is expected to begin on Thursday, October 17. In anticipation of the strike, classes have been canceled for all 361,000 students in CPS. Public school buildings are expected to be staffed by district officials and will remain open during the day for students. Schools will continue to serve breakfast and lunch. After-school activities, such as field trips, tutoring, and sports, will be canceled due to the strike. Picketing and protests are likely by CTU teachers during the strike. 

Assessment: The CPS and CTU continue to negotiate but are not expected to come to an agreement on a new contract for teachers before Thursday. The CTU is looking for a new contract that includes increased compensation for teachers, especially classroom assistants and veteran teachers, paid prep time for teachers, and smaller class sizes. CPS had an offer of 16 percent raises over a five-year contract rejected by the union, which is looking for 15 percent raises over a period of three years. It remains unclear at this time how long the strike is expected to last. Similar teacher strikes have occurred in a number of states over the last year, including Oklahoma, California, Tennessee, Oregon, and West Virginia. Those strikes were typically resolved within a timeframe between one to two weeks with the teachers largely successful in school districts acquiescing to their demands. The school cancellation in Chicago is expected to remain ongoing as long the strike continues.

On Tuesday, February 25, officials with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) announced that they believe there is potential that the outbreak of Novel Coronavirus (COVID-19) to get worse in the United States in the coming days and weeks. As of this writing, there are 57 confirmed cases within the United States. Twelve cases are in people who had recently returned from China, two are transmission from person-to-person, three are repatriated citizens from Wuhan, China (the center of the ongoing outbreak), and 40 are repatriated citizens from the Diamond Princess cruise ship, which has been docked in the Port of Yokohama in Yokohama, Japan. On Monday, President Donald Trump requested an emergency fund of $2.5 billion to help the CDC with the continued response to the COVID-19 outbreak. 

Health officials in the U.S. have warned that the number of cases may be significantly underreported due to multiple factors. These include the fact that COVID-19 symptoms are similar to those of the flu meaning some patients who have COVID-19 may not get tested and assume they are suffering from the flu. Additionally, U.S. testing guidelines currently only include people who are reporting respiratory symptoms and have recently traveled to China or had close contact with an infected person. However, within the last two weeks, local outbreaks have occurred in South Korea, Italy, and Iran showing the ability of outbreaks to occur without patients from China. On Monday, Canada also reported the first case within its borders of a patient who had returned not from China, but Iran. Along with the limited testing profile, the initial testing kits sent out by the CDC were deemed to have a faulty component and as such, there are currently only 12 labs in the U.S. that can test for COVID-19. Officials have stated they are considering widening testing protocols and are anticipating commercial labs being able to test for COVID-19 soon; however, a timeline has yet to be reported. 

Assessment: The last reported COVID-19 case in the U.S. that did not involve repatriated citizens from Wuhan, or the Diamond Princess cruise ship, was on February 13. Regardless, officials with the CDC have stated that they expect additional cases and spread of COVID-19 in the U.S. in the near future. The widening of testing protocols and addition of facilities that are able to test for COVID-19 is also likely to raise the number of cases. South Korea, one of the countries that has seen a significant uptick in cases over the last week, has reported almost 1,000 confirmed cases and has reportedly administered upwards of 35,000 tests whereas the U.S. has so far only administered 426 tests. 

While the CDC has warned of the potential spread of COVID-19 within the United States, as of this writing, the risk to the American public is still considered low. During a press briefing on Tuesday, CDC officials noted that were the virus outbreak to worsen, the American public would likely see disruptions such as school closings, workplace shutdowns, and canceling of public events and large gatherings. As such, customers are advised to continue monitoring developments and heed all instructions and procedures from authorities and health officials. Potential symptoms of COVID-19 include fever, cough, and shortness of breath. Authorities have asked those people with possible symptoms to notify healthcare officials immediately and self-isolate to limit exposure to others. The CDC has a dedicated page on the ongoing outbreak, including symptoms, number of cases, and travel advice, which can be viewed at the following link: https://www.cdc.gov/coronavirus/2019-nCoV/index.html.

Headline: Authorities Arrested a Suspect who was Planning Multiple Attacks Across Southern California
Details:
A suspect, identified as 26-year-old Mark Steven Domingo, was arrested in Reseda, CA on Friday, April 26, after plotting to carry out multiple attacks across Southern California. Domingo had discussed a number of plans with who he believed to be co-conspirators but were actually undercover federal agents. These included a plan that involved detonating a bomb at a white supremacist rally that was scheduled in Long Beach over the past weekend. Domingo had also discussed plans to target and attack police officers, attack a military facility, attack crowds at the Santa Monica Pier, target Jewish communities, and set off explosives at Los Angeles freeways. The suspect had bought nails to serve as shrapnel in homemade bombs for the proposed Long Beach attack and was arrested on Friday after placing what he believed to be a real bomb into a vehicle of an informant working for the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). 
 
	Assessment: Authorities do not believe any ongoing threat remains in relation to the bomb plot or suspect. FBI authorities had been in contact with Domingo since March 2019 after he made online posts and pledged allegiance to Islamic State (IS). Domingo was a United States Army veteran who had recently converted to the Islamic faith and had no prior criminal record. Domingo was planning the bombing in Long Beach and possible other attacks in direct response to the recent attack at two mosques in Christchurch, New Zealand which killed 50 people. 
 
	The recent Christchurch attack has spawned multiple response attacks and plots including the attempted Long Beach bombing. The bombings at multiple churches and hotels in Sri Lanka on Easter, which killed 250 people, were claimed by IS and also carried out as revenge for the Christchurch shootings. A shooting in nearby Poway, CA that killed one person on Saturday, April 27, at a Jewish synagogue, is believed to have been inspired by the Christchurch attacks but is not believed to be connected to the possible attacks Domingo was planning. These attacks and plots highlight the risk of retaliatory attacks carried out following incidents that are religiously motivated. An increased police presence has been reported outside both mosques and synagogues across the U.S. as a precaution and should be expected for the immediate future. Resilience360 customers are advised to adhere to the Department of Homeland Security s  If You See Something, Say Something  campaign and report any suspicious activity or objects to authorities.

Headline: Police seize GBP 120m worth of heroin hidden in container at Port of Felixstowe
Details: Media sources report that police have seized GBP 120m worth of heroin that was hidden inside bags of rice. The drugs were found in a container ship at the port of Felixstowe, in Suffolk, on September 20. Authorities then returned the ship under surveillance as part of an international operation. It sailed to Antwerp in Belgium where it docked on Tuesday and the container was driven by lorry to a warehouse south of The Hague in the Netherlands. Upon arrival, officers moved in and arrested three people – the driver and two men involved in the unloading.

Local reports stated that the move will allow for production to continue and workers to continue to work after severe raw material shortages. Previous sources on February 27 indicated that about 200 factories mostly producing garments are at high risk of suspending operations or slow production in March over a lack of raw materials from China.

Headline: UPDATE 1 - Agriculture bills increasing intent for opposition unity, COVID-19 disruption will marginally affect public support for Indian government
Details: India’s Minister for Food Processing Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned on 17 September after stating that three recently proposed agriculture bills – which have since been passed – would disadvantage farmers, particularly in her representative state of Punjab. Badal is a member of Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), an alliance partner of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led government. Her resignation follows ongoing protests by several hundred thousand farmers in Punjab and neighbouring Haryana against the bills.Farmer protests led by the Indian Youth Congress against the agriculture bills continue in New Delhi, India on 22 September 2020, with thousands participating.Sonu Mehta/Hindustan Times via Getty ImagesProtests from farmers – which are likely to continue over the coming weeks – will probably encourage SAD and other parties to threaten to exit the government alliance, weakening the government’s position in the upper parliamentary house. Minister Badal’s resignation almost certainly came in response to farmers’ opposition to the bills. Although it poses little risk to government continuity, given that further ministerial resignations are unlikely, it is the first major resignation in Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s cabinet since he came to power in 2014 and therefore represents an early indication of internal opposition. If farmer protests spread to states such as Bihar and Tamil Nadu – although this is unlikely to happen imminently – SAD and other regional alliance parties are likely to leave the government coalition. In the lower parliamentary house, the BJP holds a simple majority (303 of 542 seats), and although alliance parties strengthen its position, their exit would be unlikely to stall policymaking. In the upper house, the BJP is short of a majority (it holds 86 of 250 seats by itself, and 101 together with allies), and allied parties departing the coalition would strengthen the government’s recent strategy to undertake policymaking via ordinances (a direct executive order), thus bypassing parliament.The government’s preference for policymaking through ordinances will likely encourage attempts by the opposition to unite through co-ordinated policy positions and support for emerging anti-government protests. Since India imposed a national lockdown to mitigate the spread of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) in March, the BJP has undertaken urgent policymaking through ordinances instead – particularly during parliamentary recess. These have included delaying insolvency proceedings, storage of essential commodities, and loan moratoriums. Given that policy will probably stall in the upper house, it is likely that the BJP will continue to use ordinances to pass policy and that the opposition will argue that this subverts parliament. A probable opposition alliance would primarily be led by the main opposition Indian National Congress party and would include parties from states such as Maharashtra and West Bengal, with a focus on negotiating a co-ordinated position against future policies. These policies are very likely to include new labour laws (including legislation designed for contract working and to re-establish mechanisms for workplace audits, which was passed on 23 September), increased privatisation in sectors like banking and mining, and compensation under the Goods and Services Tax. The opposition will also very likely support emerging anti-government protests, including ongoing farmer-led protests and trade union-led strikes against the privatisation programme. Such protests are unlikely to result in policy roll-back, but will probably compel the government to slow implementation. A shift in urban and rural public opinion about the government’s response to COVID-19 – if realised – would indicate a growing likelihood of a cabinet reshuffle, particularly of senior members. India is currently the world’s second-most affected country in terms of the total number of COVID-19 cases and is very likely to overtake the United States, and thus become the epicentre, by November. Anecdotal reporting and IHS Markit sources indicate shifting public perception in key cities such as Mumbai, New Delhi, Chennai, and Bengaluru as healthcare services report a shortage of beds and prolonged response times. Anti-government sentiment appears to be rising, reflected among groups that had hitherto supported the government’s response. This extends to India’s urban upper-middle class, including leaders of medium- to large-sized conglomerates, whose vehicle for protest is unlikely to be street action but will instead take the form of social media rhetoric, coverage in national English-language media, and forthcoming political donations. Their impetus will likely be strengthened by India’s severe economic downturn: the government reported on 31 August that India’s first-quarter fiscal year 2020-21 GDP contracted by 23.9% – the steepest contraction globally this year – and IHS Markit estimates that India’s annual GDP growth will slow to -10.2%. Opposition in India’s non-urban areas – such as in Bihar, where state elections are due by November 2020 – will likely manifest as a reduced vote-share for the BJP. A combination of opposition from India’s upper-middle-class urban population and rural classes will probably force the government to amend its COVID-19 response strategy, and/or pacify such sentiment by undertaking a cabinet reshuffle. Indicators of changing risk environmentIncreasing riskHoarding or sharp price rises for staple foods in response to the reduced government role in setting prices (as stipulated in the new agriculture bills) would likely broaden farmer-led protests to include intermediaries who purchase produce for urban supply.A loss for the BJP in the upcoming Bihar state elections – the first major poll in India since the COVID-19 virus outbreak began – would indicate that public support for the central government is weakening.If the BJP’s parent organisation, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), opposes the agriculture bills and calls for their withdrawal, then this would strongly indicate RSS’s acknowledgement of growing opposition against the government.Decreasing riskThe government announcing a consultation process with farmer groups to reconsider contentious provisions of the agriculture bills would likely limit farmers’ intent for protests at least until after the consultation process.Given opposition parties’ claims of procedural malpractice by the government during the passage of the agriculture bills, guarantees from the government – including a pause on policymaking via ordinances and a revocation of the suspension of some opposition members of parliament – would reduce their intent to form an alliance. Effective implementation of makeshift hospitals and price caps on COVID-19 treatment in the private sector would likely help to improve public perception of the government’s response.© 2020, IHS Markit Inc. Headline: Australia: Power cuts in northern Sydney
Details: Continuing storms have caused more power cuts in northern Sydney. Approximately 2,400 homes and businesses have been left without power near Hornsby, Asquith, Mount Colah, and 700 have been affected in North Turramurra. The Australian energy grid, Ausgrid, is still dealing with previous power outages caused by previous storms and bush fires saying that more than 50,300 homes and businesses in Sydney have had power restored. Ausgrid has urged people to stay clear of fallen branches and trees as they could be disguising an electrical hazard. Some travel disruption should be expected. It is currently unknown when the situation will return to normal.

The storm reportedly has maximum wind speeds of 45mph (72kph), with forecasts indicating four to six inches of rain is possible in most coastal Texas counties. Flash, urban, and minor river flooding are anticipated due to the slow movement of the storm, which was approximately 3mph (6kph) at the latest National Hurricane Center report. Some instances of flooding are have already been reported and water rescues are said to be occurring in southwest Houston. Associated road disruptions are also occurring due to the inundations. Beta is expected to weaken into a depression by late Tuesday into Wednesday as it travels northeastward along the Texas Gulf Coast.

Headline: UPDATE 5 - Indonesia - Workers completed a nationwide three-day strike on Thursday, October 8. Event closed.
Details: Media sources reported that workers across industries represented by multiple labor unions completed a nationwide three-day strike on Thursday, October 8. The strike was organized by the national trade union center Konfederasi Serikat Pekerja Indonesia and was in response to new labor laws that will affect wages. The labor unions involved included Indonesian Trade Union Confederation (KSPI), Confederation of All Indonesian Workers' Union (KSPSI AGN), KSPSI Yorrys and national welfare movement (GEKANAS). Strike action was reported in several cities including Tangerang, Jakarta, Bogor, Karawang, Bekasi, Purwakarta, Bandung, Subang, Lampung, Gresik, Surabaya, and Batam. The exact amount of people expected to participate in the strike has been estimated as low as two million, and as high as five million. The strike involved factory walk-outs and protests in front of government buildings. This event is closed.

Headline: London bus drivers union to hold ballot for strike action
Details: The Unite union have announced that it plans to hold a ballot of members in London who are bus drivers over whether to launch a campaign of strike action. The union has demanded bus operators take a number of steps to address the problem of exhaustion among drivers. Unite has also called on bus operators to end low pay which they claim creates a ""long-hours culture that’s fuelling driver fatigue."" TfL director of bus operations Claire Mann urged Unite to continue to work with the body to address the issue. It is unclear when the strike ballot will be held; however if strike action does occur, significant disruption is likely to bus services across the city.

Headline: India: Associated disruptions likely during Durga Puja festivities over 15-19 October
Details: Associated disruptions are to be expected throughout the country for the annual Hindu Durga Puja festival. Though a ten-day event, it is the last five that are marked by popular practices, over 15-19 October. Although primarily celebrated in West Bengal (especially Calcutta), as well as other northern and eastern states, the remainder of the country also gives importance to the festival. Devotees install stages on streets and at market places for the worship, called 'pandals'. Some of the most noteworthy places to visit pandals that large numbers travel to include in Bengaluru: Socio Cultural Association of Indiranagar; Bhubaneswar: Rasulgarh; Chennai: Besant Nagar's Bengali Association; Gurugram: Purbapally Durgotsav in Sector 15; Hyderabad: Bangalee Samity Community Centre; Kolkata: Durgotsab near Sovabazar Ferry; Lucknow: Bengali Club in Shivaji Marg; Mumbai: Balkanji Bari in Santacruz; Nagpur: Dhantoli; New Delhi: Aram Bagh; Pune: Nandanik Durgapuja in Koregaon Park; and Varanasi: Ma Bagheshwari Durga Puja Club. Multiple reports of additional security measures across individual states have been received. Significant police deployments, large crowds and traffic restrictions are to be expected in the vicinity of the events, particularly where processions take place. Travellers are advised to bypass the festivities to mitigate against associated disruptions. Plan for additional security checks, reported across multiple states. Refer to official communications regarding the planned events for further information. Exercise vigilance in crowded locations as a precaution.

Headline: CORRECTION: Conditions gradually improve at after court orders Transnet Port Terminals strike halt
Details:
A previous version of this incident mistakenly classified it as an industrial fire and has now been corrected. 

Reports indicate that a company-wide go-slow strike began at the end of June after the state-owned port operator Transnet Port Terminals failed to disburse an anticipated bonus payment to employees. The strike has resulted in vessel berth waiting times of 4 to 5 days at the Port of Durban, where 60% of South African imports and exports are processed. Unspecified equipment failures are further complicating matters at the port. However, the most severe impacts are at Ngqura Container Terminal near Port Elizabeth, where total waiting times for berths have increased to 7 days or more. This has had a significant impact on local agricultural cargo, particularly citrus exporters who are in high season between the months of February and August. Volkswagen, one of the container terminal’s largest customers, utilizes the terminal as a critical transit point for parts supplied to their assembly plant in Uitenhage. A vessel with 150 containers including some critical automotive parts is reportedly in the Nelson Mandela Bay area but has not yet managed to berth at the terminal. Reports indicate that trucks have been forced to wait for up to 18 hours for inbound and outbound shipments, with members of local meat, textile, and electronics industries also reporting ground transportation disruptions.

Historically, Transnet has announced incentive bonus payments on the morning that financial statements are released to the public. Such an announcement was anticipated at the end of June and it is understood that employees were under the impression that bonus payments would be processed at that time in a regular fashion. However, the financial statement release has been delayed by an ongoing audit that is not likely to be concluded until mid- August, and Transnet is not able to disburse the funds until the audit is completed. 

As the end of June neared, with funds for bonus payment disbursal inaccessible until the audit is completed, Transnet managers issued a new stipulation that bonus payments will be paid to employees on the condition that employees have met on-time-performance targets, a proposal that was reportedly rejected by some workers. While labor unions representing Transnet employees chose not to resort to industrial action, non-unionized workers expressed frustration at the handling of the matter and organized their own strike. As evidence of their frustration, this action was executed without sanctioning from South African courts, which protects employees from being fired for strike participation.  At least 11 employees have been suspended for their participation. 

On July 14, Transnet announced that it has obtained an interdiction from the Labor Court of Port Elizabeth that orders striking employees to halt their action. Headline: Full Environmental and Health Impact From ITC Fire Remains Unclear While Air Quality has Normalized
Details:
On Thursday, March 21, a shelter-in-place was temporarily issued for the Deer Park and Galena Park communities in Texas, due to reports of elevated benzene levels in the air. Both orders were lifted by Thursday afternoon as officials determined that air quality in the area is improving. Inhaling benzene can cause irritation to the skin, eyes, and respiratory system. Severe exposure can harm the nervous system or lead to unconsciousness. The benzene levels are related to an earlier fire at the Intercontinental Terminals Company (ITC) facility in La Porte involving as many as eight tanks of chemicals, which burned from Sunday to Wednesday before being contained. Nearby Highway 225 was also temporarily closed in both directions but has since reopened. 
 
	Assessment: Officials are using a foam blanket at the site of the ITC fire to help keep possibly dangerous chemicals from spreading further. As of this writing, the cause of the fire remains unknown and the full environmental impact from the fire remains unclear. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), and the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) are testing local waterways and soil samples for possible further contamination. The EPA also continues to monitor air quality form La Porte to Katy. The Port of Houston and the Houston Ship Channel have remained open during the fire and continuing cleanup. Resilience360 customers with interests in the region should continue to heed all instructions from local authorities. Real time updates of air quality measurements by the EPA and TCEQ can be found at the following link: https://www.tceq.texas.gov/response/itc-terminal-fire-update.

Headline: USGS reports magnitude 6.3 earthquake 4km southeast of Calatagan, Batangas Province
Details:
The United States Geological Survey (USGS) has recorded a magnitude 6.3 earthquake 4km southeast of Calatagan on Friday, 25 December. The quake has occurred at a depth of 114km at 07:43 local time. There has not been a tsunami warning issued and there are no immediate reports of damages, though they are possible due to the intensity of the tremor.
USGS (United States Geological Survey) is a scientific agency of the U.S. government which monitors earthquake activity worldwide. USGS earthquake alerts are assessed primarily using the moment magnitude (Mw) scale. However, local magnitude (ML), surface-wave magnitude (Ms) or body-wave magnitude (Mb) may be used in lieu of the Mw scale. All magnitude scales should yield approximately the same value for any given earthquake.

Headline: Greenpeace Protest on Hartman Bridge on Thursday Temporarily Closed Portion of Houston Ship Channel
Details:
On Thursday, September 12, 23 protesters associated with Greenpeace demonstrated along the Fred Hartman Bridge in Baytown, TX just outside of Houston. The protest began around 6:30 AM local time and included 11 of the protesters rappelling down the bridge to disrupt shipping traffic in the Houston Ship Channel. While the bridge stayed open during the protest to vehicular traffic, a half-mile portion of the ship channel was closed between Light 102A and Light 104 until reopening early Friday morning after protesters were arrested. The protest remained peaceful; however, the initial blocking of the bridge led to a minor motor vehicle accident which injured one person. 

Assessment: The Greenpeace activists stated that their goal of the protest was to attempt to disrupt the oil and gas shipments that go through the Houston Ship Channel. The group timed their protest to attempt to get the attention of Democratic presidential candidates who were in Houston Thursday for a Democrat National Committee presidential debate. The Houston Ship Channel and Port of Houston are vital to U.S. oil and gas exports and the ship channel is the busiest in the country annually generating approximately $339 billion and providing over 1.35 million jobs to the state of Texas. The portion of the ship channel that was closed on Thursday normally sees approximately 300 vessels pass through, and according to media sources, at least seven were blocked during the temporary closure. The protest did not cause any significant disruptions to shipping interests, as many companies often build in an extra day to shipping schedules as a precaution. 

An uptick in climate change-related protests has been seen in recent months, especially across Europe. The majority of protests are organized by groups such as Greenpeace or Extinction Rebellion and have been relatively peaceful, although some have been disruptive with protesters blocking bridges, and trains, similar to the Greenpeace protesters temporarily shutting down the Houston Ship Channel on Thursday. Additionally, a weeklong series of protests are being planned across the world beginning Friday, September 20 as part of a global climate strike action. The relative ease with which the Greenpeace protesters in Baytown were able to shut down a portion of the Houston Ship Channel using a small group of people and the increased focus on climate-related protests highlight the possibility of an increase in similar protests across the United States. As such, Resilience360 customers with cargo interests should anticipate the possibility of disruptions to supply chains due to climate-related protests.

Headline: Labour strikes and protests affecting non-strategic sectors likely to...
Details: Risks: Protests and riots; labour strikesSectors or assets affected: All sectorsOn 29 August 2018, thousands of members of the United Workers Front (Frente Unitario de Trabajadores (FUT), Ecuador's largest trade union federation held a march in Quito to protest several economic measures adopted by the government through 2018. These include a reduction in gasoline (petrol) subsidies and planned redundancies in the public sector caused by the government's austerity drive that includes a restructuring of ministries, and state-owned enterprises in the public construction, pharmaceutical, and manufacturing sectors. The FUT, alongside other civil society groups representing students, teachers, peasant farmers, and pensioners are planning a national march on 20 September. Separately, the country's largest indigenous umbrella organisation, the Confederation of Indigenous Nationalities of Ecuador, resolved on 29 August to hold a national protest towards the end of October over the same issues. The government is very unlikely to capitulate and reverse these measures; In June public debt reached almost USD48 billion, or 46.1% of GDP. IHS Markit forecasts the fiscal deficit to reach close to 5% of GDP in 2018.Significance: Opposition to the government is likely to mainly take the form of labour strikes, particularly in the public sector, supported by peaceful protest marches involving thousands at a time, towards Quito and other major cities including Cuenca and Guayaquil. Headline: Southeast and Midatlantic ports to shutter ahead of Hurricane Florence
Details: Industry sources indicate on September 11 that Maersk is implementing emergency contingency measures in anticipation of the land fall of Hurricane Florence within the next 72 hours, developed on recognizance of National Hurricane Center developments as well as US Coast Guard advice. The Ports of Wilmington, NC and Charleston, SC will close their inbound channels at 6PM on September 12, at which point the last vessel needs to depart. Gates have been closed for export drop-off at Wilmington since September 10 at 7PM, while they will close for import pickup on September 11 at a time to be determined. The times for the previous two categories are yet to be determined for Charleston. The Ports of Norfolk, VA and Baltimore, MD, will close on September 12 at 6AM, the same time that vessels need to depart. Gates will close for export drop-off and import pick-up at Norfolk on September 11 at 11:59PM. The times for the previous two categories are yet to be determined for Baltimore. Rail operations will close at Norfolk on September 11 at 11:59 PM, while the rail operation closure time is yet to be determined for Baltimore, Wilmington, and Charleston. Furthermore, any closures or cargo updates are yet to be determined for the Ports of Philadelphia and Savannah. Those shipping to and from Philadelphia, Baltimore, Norfolk, Wilmington, Charleston, and Savannah should anticipate notable disruption to regular operations during the landfall and passage of Hurricane Florence and should plan accordingly.

Headline: Southeast Spain - Emergency declaration lifted and recovery stage initiated. Incident closed.
Details:
The emergency declaration has been lifted and the recovery stage has been initiated after flooding impacted areas across southeast Spain for several days. Cleanup operations are underway and roadways are being cleared; however, possible residual closures could persist as cleanup continues. The regions most impacted included the Valencian Community, Murcia, the Balearic Islands, southeastern Castile-La Mancha, and eastern Andalusia. Heavy rains have subsided and over 1,100 military personnel have were dispatched across the area to assist in rescue and recovery operations. At least 3,500 people were rescued during the course of the flooding. At least seven people were killed, with deaths being reported in Redovan, Almeria, Caudete, Orihuela, and at an unspecified location in Granada Province. Additionally, two people were reported as missing. Over 4,000 people were evacuated as well, including around 2,000 residents of Santomera in Murcia who were displaced due to the controlled release of a local dam. An additional 200 people were evacuated in Heredades in Alicante due to water levels of the Segura River rising. Red alerts were lifted in Almer a, Valencia, Alicante, and Murcia. Yellow alerts were also in effect for Castile-La Mancha. In Orihuela, photographs indicated that floodwaters impacted households and roadways. Water levels were recorded at an upwards of five feet. There were reports of property damage as a result of the flood, including vehicles, trash, personal belongings and other items in the water. Residents were not able to leave their households for four days. 

The Region of Murcia International Airport (RMU) was temporarily closed, and disruptions were reported at Barcelona-El Prat Airport (BCN) and Palma de Mallorca Airport (PMI). Almeria Airport (LEI) was also closed, but was later reopened. Operations at the Port de Sagunt were halted earlier, but have resumed as well. The railway linking Alicante to Madrid and Barcelona was closed, as was the Murcia regional railway service. More than 74 roads and highways were blocked by flooding across the area, and motorists are still advised not to attempt to drive through flooded

Headline: UPDATE 145 - Massachusetts - School regulations have changed due to decrease in risk levels of many communities.
Details:
The following information is a summary of COVID-19 within Massachusetts and its associated impacts.

COVID-19 Numbers: 
- Approximately 172,727 positive or presumptive positive cases have been reported. 
- Up to 10,163 virus-related deaths have been confirmed.
- More than 6,767,987 people have been tested.
 
New Updates:
- 105 communities have been removed from the high-risk list and are expected to return to in-person learning as long as they remain in the gray, green or yellow risk levels. 
- California has been removed from Massachusetts’s travel order exempt list. People traveling from California will now be required to fill out a travel form and quarantine for 14 days upon arrival. 

Reopening Details: 
- Governor Baker announced a series of new COVID-19 restrictions. A stay-at-home advisory will be implemented from 10:00 PM to 5:00 AM local time, every night, effective Friday, November 6. Indoor recreational facilities, theaters, casinos and entertainment venues are required to close at 9:30 PM local time. Indoor gathering at private residences has been reduced to ten people. Outdoor gatherings have been set at a 25-person capacity. Indoor and outdoor events at homes must end by 9:30 PM local time. Face coverings are required in public spaces. 
- Governor Baker announced that effective October 5, lower risk counties will be permitted to move into Step Two of Phase Three of Massachusetts’s reopening plan. Under Step Two, indoor and outdoor performance venues will be permitted to open at 50 percent capacity with a maximum of 250 people. Gyms, museums, libraries and driving and flight schools will also be permitted to increase their capacity to 50 percent. Fitting rooms will be permitted to open in all types of retail stores. For arcades and indoor/outdoor recreation businesses, additional Step II activities like trampolines, obstacle courses, roller rinks and laser tag will also be permitted to open, and capacity will increase to 50 percent.
- Most of the state entered Phase Three on July 6. Under Step One of Phase Three, museums are limited to 40 percent occupancy, tours such as trolleys and harbor cruises are limited to 50 percent occupancy with passengers separated by empty seats, walking tours are limited to ten people, and fitness centers are limited to 40 percent occupancy with equipment spaced 14 feet apart or six feet apart with barriers. Movie theaters and casino gaming floors are also permitted to open with restrictions, frequent cleaning, and limited capacity. Outdoor events of up to 50 people are also allowed with a permit. People participating in these activities must still practice safe social distancing and wear a mask.
- Effective Monday, September 28, restaurants are allowed to expand seating from six to ten people and open bar seating. Tables must be six feet apart, and customers must wear a face covering at all times, unless seated at a table. Bar patrons must remain seated at the bar and must order food. The new guidelines apply to both indoor and outdoor seating. Boston will wait on the seat expansion. Bars and nightclubs are still closed until Phase 4.
- Governor Charlie Baker outlined a four-phase approach for reopening the state. In the “Start” phase, limited industries will be allowed to resume operations with restrictions. In the “Cautious” phase, additional industries can resume operations with restrictions and limited capacity. In the “Vigilant” phase, additional industries may resume operations with guidance. In the “New normal” phase, the development of a vaccine allows for a new normal.
- Anyone traveling into the state will need to quarantine for 14 days or produce a negative COVID-19 test result. Violators can be fined up to US$ 500 per day. Travelers from Hawaii, Maine, New Hampshire, New York, Vermont, Washington and the District of Columbia are exempt. Travelers from Rhode Island are not exempt and will need to quarantine.

Previous Updates:
- According to new state COVID-19 reporting guidelines, only 16 communities in Massachusetts are considered high-risk; a 105 drop from the reporting guidelines of last week. The 16 communities considered in the Red Category are Brockton, Chelsea, Everett, Fall River, Fitchburg, Lawrence, Lowell, Lynn, Methuen, New Bedford, Norfolk, Revere, Seekonk, Somerset, Springfield, and Westport.

Although case numbers are included, it is important to note that these numbers are constantly changing, and the most up-to-date statistics are published by the CDC or local public health agencies. This risk event is located statewide regardless of where or how many cases are being confirmed.

Headline: Four Died in Unspecified Hazmat Incident; Circumstances Appear Similar to Deaths Earlier this Year
Details:
On December 24, local media outlets reported that four people have died, and at least 18 others have been hospitalized, possibly due to an unidentified gas leak in Pakistan’s Keamari neighborhood in Karachi. However, the cause of the incident remains unconfirmed, and it is unclear whether the situation is ongoing. Reportedly, the Ziauddin Hospital received the patients over the past week, all of whom suffered from breathing problems. 



Assessment: In the incident that occurred this past week, all the patients reportedly had the same symptoms registered in a similar incident in mid-February 2020, when 14 people died and more than 250 fell ill in Keamari. The true cause of the incident in February remains unclear. An investigation by the Sindh Environmental Protection Agency (SEPA) showed that a toxic gas leaked from a terminal storing crude oil and petroleum products in residential areas. A report from Karachi University’s International Centre for Chemical and Biological Sciences (ICCBS) suspected that soybean dust allergens, dispersed during the unloading of a docked ship, may have caused the deaths; however, this claim has been largely ruled out by authorities. As the cause of the February incident and the latest hospitalizations in Keamari remain unconfirmed, security measures may be implemented in the coming days to mitigate any possible future risk. Following the deaths in February, the Pakistan State Oil (PSO) corporation and several private oil companies closed storage terminals at the Port of Karachi. Additionally, schools and factories were temporarily closed; such security measures may be employed again. Protests are also possible in response to the most recent hospitalizations and the perceived failure of authorities to detect and correct the problem.

Headline: Dow declares force majeure on all MDI products in the U.S.
Details: Media sources reported on October 1 that Dow Inc. has declared force majeure on all methylene diphenyl diisocyanate (MDI) products in the U.S due to logistics and raw material constraints following the passage of recent storms in the U.S. Gulf Coast. Texas and Louisiana, which contain the bulk of the country’s petrochemical infrastructure, have been impacted by several hurricanes and tropical storms, causing a number of chemical plants producing feedstocks and intermediates used in MDI production to experience shutdowns and subsequently disrupting logistics and transportation in the region. Dow Inc. reportedly operates a 340,000 tonnes/year MDI plant in Freeport, Texas. Dow Inc. manufactures and supplies chemicals for liquid injection molding, architecture fabrication, leather, textiles, automobiles, rubber consumer goods, and food industries.

Headline: Trump Administration Issues New Guidelines on the Potential Reduction of Social Distancing Orders
Details:
On Thursday, April 16, the Trump administration issued new guidelines titled “Opening Up America Again” that detail a new three-phased process to begin easing social distancing guidelines and returning to normal day-to-day life. Prior to implementing guidelines, it is recommended states and/or regions have a documented decline in COVID-19 cases for a 14-day testing program, a widespread testing program in place for at least at-risk healthcare workers, and healthcare facilities having enough personal protective gear (PPE), beds, and medical supplies. Additionally, states are encouraged to have widespread testing and contact tracing abilities and plans in place to protect at-risk populations and workers before beginning to ease social distancing guidelines. The general phases have been described as follows: 



Phase One: This phase could begin when all the above conditions are being met. All at-risk individuals, such as the elderly or those with pre-existing medical conditions should continue to shelter in place. Social distancing guidelines should continue to be followed when in public and all gatherings of ten or more people should continue to be avoided. All nonessential travel should be minimized. Telework is encouraged as much as possible and schools should remain closed. 



Phase Two: This phase could begin for states and regions that enacted Phase One guidelines with no evidence of a rebound in infections and are continuing to satisfy Phase One criteria. All at-risk individuals should continue to shelter in place. Nonessential may resume. Gatherings of more than 50 should be avoided. Schools and daycares may begin reopening. Large venues such as restaurants, bars, movie theaters, and places of worship, can reopen continuing physical distancing rules. Telework is still encouraged when possible and work common areas should remain closed. Elective surgeries at healthcare facilities can resume when appropriate. 



Phase Three: This phase could begin for states and regions that enacted Phase Two guidelines with no evidence of a rebound in infections and are continuing to satisfy Phase Two criteria. This phase involves a return to a relatively normal day-to-day life. At-risk populations can return to public life but should continue to maintain physical distancing. Low-risk populations should attempt to minimize the time spent in crowded environments. Normal staffing of worksites is allowed. Large venues can operate with some physical distancing measures still in place. 



The full guidelines can be found at the following link: https://www.whitehouse.gov/openingamerica/. 



Assessment: It should be noted that the new guidelines issued on reopening are recommendations from the federal government and that President Donald Trump also announced that it would largely be on each state and locality to determine when and how reopening should occur. To that end, state governors have set up several regional groups to plan the reopening with cohesiveness among nearby states. There is a west coast group of California, Washington, and Oregon, an east coast group of New Jersey, Connecticut, New York, Pennsylvania, Delaware, Rhode Island, and Massachusetts, and a group of Midwest states including Illinois, Michigan, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Indiana, and Kentucky. 



Public health officials continue to warn that if reopening occurs too quickly and without adequate testing or healthcare availability, outbreaks could worsen, further straining healthcare systems and likely leading to additional restrictions being enacted for potentially an even longer duration. Moreover, it remains to be seen how quickly states begin enacting the recommended guidelines as the majority of states do not currently have adequate testing for COVID-19 and continue to see healthcare systems at capacity. Officials have repeatedly stated that it is likely some form of social distancing guidelines remain in place through at least the end of 2020. The public is advised to continue monitoring developments related to the COVID-19 situation closely and adhere to all social distancing guidelines.

Headline: Heightened Security Likely Ahead of Defense Sector Event in Karachi
Details:
The ninth edition of the International Defense Exhibition and Seminar (IDEAS) will begin in Karachi, Pakistan, on November 27. The four-day event will be held at the Karachi Expo Center and is expected to attract trade visitors and high-profile defense delegates from around the world. While no specific details have been announced, it is reasonable to expect heightened security measures around the venue and elsewhere in Karachi through November 30. This is particularly true in light of the November 23 attack on the Chinese consulate in Karachi that left seven people dead, including the three attackers, and was claimed by the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) separatist group. No Chinese nationals or consulate staff were among those killed or injured. 
 
	Assessment: The BLA said it specifically targeted Chinese interests in last Friday s attack over what the group called Beijing s  occupation  of Pakistan, ostensibly a reference to China s development of the port of Gwadar, its military presence in Balochistan province, and its involvement in the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) project. While not specifically linked to the IDEAS conference, the episode highlights the continued threat posed by militants to foreigners in Pakistan. More immediately, Resilience360 customers in Karachi are advised of the potential for disruptions to transportation and business operations between November 27 and November 30 due to the enhanced security measures adopted for the IDEAS event. Therefore, travelers and expatriates should implement precautionary measures to mitigate potential complications, including secondary and tertiary routes for road travel due to the likelihood of traffic congestion.

Headline: Over 100 Protesters Detained at Anti-Government Demonstration in Managua on Saturday
Details:
On Saturday, hundreds of supporters of the Civic Alliance opposition coalition gathered for a demonstration in downtown Managua. The action was intended to protest against the administration of incumbent President Daniel Ortega, and to demand the release of political prisoners. As Ortega s government had previously outlawed anti-government demonstrations, security forces rapidly descended on the scene and forcibly dispersed the crowd with truncheons, tear gas, and rubber bullets. Nicaraguan authorities claimed that 107 protesters were detained for  violating public order.  The opposition claimed that 164 demonstrators were detained, and that six had been wounded by rubber bullets. Multiple news outlets and non-governmental organizations have claimed that several journalists that were covering the demonstration were assaulted by police and/or robbed of their cellphones. There were no reports of injuries among law enforcement personnel. 
	 
	Assessment: Political leaders from the United States, Uruguay, and multiple European countries condemned the actions taken by Nicaraguan authorities on Saturday. Representatives of the European Union called on the Ortega administration to respect the principles of freedom of peaceful assembly and freedom of the press. Nicaragua s opposition movement claims that 770 people have been imprisoned on spurious, politically motivated charges since civil unrest broke out across Nicaragua last April. The government freed 112 detainees in late February, and 50 more were transferred to house arrest on March 15th. Nevertheless, members of the Civic Alliance have deemed the concessions to be inadequate, and the issue remains one of the major sticking points preventing the two sides from resuming negotiations. 
	 
	As no solution to Nicaragua s ongoing political crisis appears to be within sight, similar bouts of anti-government protest activity and ensuing clashes with security forces will likely continue to sporadically crop up in the coming weeks and months. Resilience360 continues to advise customers to avoid non-essential travel to the country, due to the risks posed by civil unrest and the government s arbitrary enforcement of laws.

Headline: UPDATE 2 - FCO issues alert regarding preventative measures in place to limit the spread of COVID-19
Details: The Foreign and Commonwealth Office (FCO) has released the following alert: 'There have been no confirmed cases of COVID-19 in Uzbekistan. The Uzbek authorities have strengthened sanitary and epidemiological controls at ports of entry and border crossing points. British nationals arriving directly from China, South Korea, Iran, Italy, Afghanistan, Japan will be quarantined for up to 14 days and not be allowed to leave the quarantine facility during this period. British nationals arriving in Uzbekistan and who have visited China, South Korea, Iran, Italy, Afghanistan, Japan, France, USA, Germany, Singapore, Spain, Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan in last 14 days are subject to home isolation/quarantine. You will be subject to monitoring and required to remain at your place of residence/stay for up to 14 days, not allowed to visit public places and required to avoid contact with other people excluding family members. British nationals arriving from Thailand, Azerbaijan, UK, UAE are subject to 14 days medical supervision at their place of stay/residence and are advised to avoid contact with people – excluding family members - and visiting public places. Under the measures introduced by the Uzbek authorities, any person subject to the above controls breaking quarantine or self-isolation is liable to a minimum fine of 11 Million UZS (approx £900) or up to three years imprisonment.'

Under the Entity List, the BIS can restrict the export, re-export, and transfer (in-country) of items subject to the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Additional license requirements apply to listed entities and the availability of most license exceptions is limited.

Headline: Peru   Updated reports indicate the strike has been called off after negotiations. Incident closed.
Details:
Truck drivers affiliated with the Union of Transporters and Logistics (GTL) staged a nationwide strike across Peru. Updated reports indicate the strike has been called off after successful negotiations on Saturday. The strike was called to demand a reduction in tolls and taxes on diesel, as well as a solution to alleviate vehicular congestion at the port of Callao. Union representatives claimed that at least 40,000 truckers participated in the labor action across the country. Media sources reported that at least 200 fuel transporters joined the labor action on Thursday, which threatened to cause fuel supply shortages in the northern regions of Lambayeque, Piura, Cajamarca, La Libertad, San Martin, and Amazonas. In addition, the strike caused supply chain disruptions to the distribution of important commodities, such as cement, sugar, rice, and other agricultural products. 

Truck drivers that participated in the labor action utilized their tractor-trailers to block intercity highways in multiple locations throughout the country. At least one roadblock was reported in the southern region of Arequipa along Highway 115. As a result of the roadblocks in Arequipa, at least 30 public transportation companies, including inter-provincial bus services, suspended ticket sales across the region as a safety precaution for travelers. Authorities requested that bus companies suspend ticket sales to various southern regions, including Lima, Ica, and Tacna.  Local news outlets reported other blockades were erected along the Panamericana Norte Highway, preventing the transportation of dairy products and other goods from Cajamarca, Chiclayo, and Trujillo southward to Lima. Furthermore, media sources reported that up to 60 thousand tons of goods were effectively stranded at the port of Salaverry, in the northern region of La Libertad. Five maritime vessels were unable to unload their cargo at the port due to the backlog. Expect residual disruptions as cargo transportation returns to normal. This incident is closed.

Headline: TMA Predicts Normal to Above-Normal Rainfall during Upcoming Rainy Season
Details:
On Thursday, the Tanzania Meteorological Agency (TMA) predicted that normal to above-normal rainfall will occur across most of Tanzania during the upcoming rainy season. TMA Director General Dr. Agnes Kijazi told media sources that the rainy season is expected to begin during the fourth week of February and will bring normal to above-normal rains to the following locations: the northern eastern highlands, the eastern and southern eastern parts of the Lake Victoria basin, the southern parts of the northern eastern highlands, and the northern coast. However, lower than average rainfall is predicted in the Morogoro areas. 
 
	Assessment: Heavy rains are common across Tanzania during the two rainy seasons, which generally run from March to May and November to December. The rains can cause flooding and landslides, as well as damage to infrastructure, including roads, bridges, and homes. Other flood-related disruptions can include power outages, disruptions to water services, and outbreaks of some water-borne diseases, such as cholera. Due to the increased risk of heavy rains and flood-related disruptions over the coming months, Resilience360 customers in Tanzania are advised to monitor weather forecasts and exercise caution when traveling to low-lying and flood-prone areas.

Headline: Criminal Investigation Launched Following Genoa Bridge Collapse
Details:
On Wednesday, Italian Prime Minister Giuseppe Conte declared a one-year state of emergency in the region of Liguria following the deadly bridge collapse in Genoa on Tuesday. Conte also said an initial US $5.7 million in national emergency funds would be available for Liguria. At least 39 people were killed from the collapse of an approximately 260-foot section of Morandi Bridge, and at least 16 others were injured. The collapsed section of the A10 toll highway stood about 150 feet above the Polcevera River, an industrial and retail zone, and railroad tracks. While search and rescue teams have been working at the site, the prospect of finding more survivors is waning. The number of missing is unknown. More than 400 people have been evacuated from the vicinity of the bridge, with local residents being warned of cracking under a bridge pillar. Toll road operator Autostrade per l Italia had been conducting maintenance work to shore up the bridge s foundation when the structure fell during a period of heavy rain, though the exact cause of the collapse is not yet known. 
 
	Assessment: Tuesday s collapse is believed to be the fifth bridge collapse in Italy in as many years. The Italian government has accused Autostrade of bearing responsibility for the collapse, and the public prosecutor s office has launched a criminal investigation. Italian Transport Minister Danilo Toninelli said that officials would begin examining the possibility of fines against Autostrade and revocation of the firm s concessions. The company has rejected accusations by officials, contending it could show fulfillment of its obligations, including bridge checks every three months, and that more than US $1.13 billion had been invested in network maintenance and safety annually in the last five years. Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini has drawn criticism for suggesting European Union budget regulations blocked infrastructure investment, and officials have called for increased public spending to evaluate and upgrade infrastructure around the country following Tuesday s collapse. The bridge was built of reinforced concrete, opened in 1967, and has been a major route connecting the Italian and French Rivieras. After the collapse, Italy s civil engineering society said bridges constructed in the 1950s and 1960s had a working lifespan of about 50 years. Resilience360 customers are advised to anticipate transportation disruptions in the region and to continue monitoring associated developments as inspections are undertaken of infrastructure around the country.
