Headline: China allegedly stops buying all Canadian canola seed exports
Details:
In recent weeks, Beijing and Ottawa have been locked in a contentious trade dispute over Canadian canola seed exports to China.

On March 1, China’s General Administration of Customs (GAC) issued a notice revoking the license of Richardson International, Canada’s largest canola distributor, to export canola to China after it allegedly found ‘dangerous pests’ in its products. Subsequently, Canadian reports on March 22 indicated that Chinese importers were allegedly unwilling to purchase Canadian canola seed exports – with industry experts suggesting that the restrictions are thought to be targeted at new canola sales rather than contracts already in place. A second Canadian canola producer, Viterra, a unit of Glencore Plc, also had its license revoked on March 26 for an alleged similar pest infestation issue.

Chinese customs authorities announced on March 7 that leptosphaeria maculans and other pest infections were detected in Richardson International’s canola seed imports on multiple occasions at ports in Dalian, Nanning, Shenzhen, and Guangzhou. On March 26, Chinese media reports announced that further pest infestations, including of the leptosphaeria maculans bacteria, had allegedly been found in Viterra’s canola shipments at the ports of Dalian and Nanning.

Diplomatic spats

The unexpected ban on Canadian canola products comes on the back of a diplomatic dispute that has been linked to the detention of a senior Chinese corporate executive in Vancouver last year. Although Chinese officials and media sources cite agricultural safety concerns as the main reason behind the Richardson and Viterra decisions, other reports suggest that diplomatic tensions between Beijing and Ottawa are the more likely root cause behind the seemingly retaliatory measures.

Canadian officials have strongly refuted Chinese allegations. Richardson has likewise rejected these claims, while Viterra has yet to comment. In addition, the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) officials on March 25 denied Canadian media reports that strict customs inspections were also being applied to other Canadian agricultural exports such as wheat, peas, and flax seed. Some observers – including former Canadian ambassadors to China – are urging the government to file an official complaint at the World Trade Organization, but the Canadian trade minister is calling on China to provide sufficient scientific evidence before taking any further measures.
It remains unclear as to whether there will be an outright ban of Canadian canola imports or if another producer will follow Richardson and Glencore in having their import licenses revoked. On April 3, Canada’s agriculture ministry denied media reports that a third canola exporter was being targeted by China, clarifying that there has not been another company to have their registration suspended.

Regulatory ambiguity produces uncertainty

Canola – a variant of rapeseed – is used for cooking oil and animal feed for livestock, but also as a source of renewable energy through biodiesel in some markets such as Europe. As the world’s largest canola exporter, Canada supplies about 40 percent of China’s canola exports with 4.32 million metric tons of canola seeds last year – a volume that surpasses both the second and third largest exporters combined.

With the planting season looming in mid-to-late April, the dispute comes at a crucial moment when canola farmers worldwide will need to decide on which crops to grow including wheat, barley, and canola. Given that many farmers have already finalized their investment and planting decisions, the continued disruption is leaving canola producers, and suppliers seeking canola exports, with further uncertainty in the face of declining crop prices and regulatory ambiguity in China.

As of this writing, Beijing has not issued any official statements on whether all imports of Canadian canola seeds are banned.
Customers focusing on Chinese industries will need to remain alert on any further potential regulatory disruptions on Canadian agricultural products by customs authorities. The ongoing canola dispute comes on the heels of another similar delay in customs clearance of Australian coal imports last month, understood to be as a result of diplomatic tensions between Canberra and Beijing.

Headline: Tanker ship disabled on maiden voyage near Fedje, drifts dangerously close to coast
Details: Media sources indicate that in the early morning hours local time on March 29, product tanker ""Ionian Star"" (IMO 9828895) suffered an engine failure while traveling near the coast northeast of Fedje, Norway. The vessel went adrift and came dangerously close to the coast before it was rescued and taken in tow by the Coast Guard Patrol ship ""KV Senja."" The vessel was on its maiden voyage which started in Ulsan, Korea in January.

Headline: US Embassy Issues Health Alert Regarding Rising COVID-19 Cases
Details:
On Friday, the United States Embassy in Tokyo issued a Health Alert regarding the ongoing increase in COVID-19 cases in Japan. The message reads in part:



“The U.S. Embassy and consulates continue to monitor COVID-19 conditions in Japan closely. Case numbers continue to rise throughout the country, and media reports indicate that healthcare capacity in several regions, including Tokyo, Osaka, and Hokkaido, is becoming strained both in terms of available critical care bed space and sufficient numbers of medical personnel. The national government and some prefectural governments have begun announcing new COVID-19 mitigation measures, including discouraging travel to certain areas with high case numbers and encouraging limited hours for bars and other entertainment venues. The “Go To Travel” campaign now excludes travel to Sapporo and Osaka, while Tokyo Governor Koike urged residents over 65 or with preexisting medical conditions to refrain from participating in the program. U.S. citizens are strongly encouraged to monitor changes to prefectural government alerts, especially when considering travel across prefectures, and should continue to follow measures introduced by Japanese national and local government officials designed to mitigate COVID-19 outbreaks in their areas.



On December 3, officials in Osaka raised the prefecture’s health alert to red – the highest level – indicating that the city’s hospital bed occupancy rate for serious cases will soon reach 70%. They urge residents to limit non-essential outings and to observe COVID precautions if they must go out. In response, U.S. Consulate General Osaka is taking steps to reduce public services and in-office staffing levels in order to minimize the risk of COVID-19 exposure. Please check the website for more information.



Aichi Prefecture raised its COVID alert on November 19 from yellow to orange, the second highest of four levels, in response to a third wave of infections that started to impact the region in late October. Residents are asked to exercise heightened caution and to avoid non-urgent travel to Tokyo, Osaka and Hokkaido.



The Government of Japan has renewed calls for residents to wear masks and take other common-sense COVID-19 mitigation precautions. Government officials at all levels have particularly urged mask wearing while dining out in restaurants. Diners should only remove their masks for short periods of time to eat or drink, and wear masks while having conversations. Residents should also continue to avoid the “Three Cs:” closed spaces, crowded spaces, and close-contact settings.”



The entire Health Alert can be viewed here: https://jp.usembassy.gov/health-alert-december-4-2020/



Assessment: Japan remains in a third wave of COVID-19 infections, with daily cases having roughly quadrupled since early November. Likewise, the number of patients in serious condition has tripled over the past month, while daily deaths reached a record-high on December 4 with 45. The worsening situation is said to be testing hospitals, as occupancy is starting to approach capacity and medical personnel are suffering from exhaustion. Regional media sources have indicated this is leading to growing criticism of the government’s handling of the pandemic, mostly from prefecture leaders. If these sentiments continue to grow, it could manifest in protest activity and/or labor strikes by doctors and nurses.

Details: Media sources report on December 27 that Brightway Holdings is under investigation after a government raid found labor abuses in multiple manufacturing plants. The raid was focused on two of Brightway Holdings' subsidiarities: a La Glove factory in Kajang and a Biopro factory located in Port Klang. Brightway Holdings produces natural and synthetic gloves for medical, industrial, and cleanroom applications and can produce 340 million gloves per month. Headline: Congestion issues at Port of Southampton deteriorate as ocean carriers omit calls - UPDATE 2
Details:
Shipping sources report on December 8 that amid worsening congestion issues at the Port of Southampton, THE Alliance has announced it will cancel calls at the port for its vessels NYK Deneb and CMA CGM Kerguelen. The port has faced issues of bad weather, vessel delays and a customs software shutdown in the last few days, resulting in failed deliveries and an increase in backlogs. 
Previously, ocean carriers announced they would impose congestion surcharges on cargo shipped to and from the Port of Southampton due to the congestion. Hapag-Lloyd previously announced a surcharge of EUR 175 per TEU for cargo from Far East Asia to London Gateway from November 15. In addition, CMA CGM will impose a surcharge of USD 100 per TEU for cargo from and to Australia and New Zealand from November 30 and from and to the Indian subcontinent, the Middle East and the Red Sea from November 15. It will also impose a surcharge of USD 150 per TEU for cargo from North East and South East Asia, China, Hong Kong and Macao to Southampton from November 15.

Headline: Dubai Reopens Parks, Hotel Beaches in Further Easing of COVID-19 Restrictions
Details:
Late on May 12, Dubai allowed public parks to reopen and hotel guests to access private beaches, as the government gradually lifts restrictions imposed to combat the COVID-19 outbreak. Gatherings at public parks can be in groups of no more than five people, and hotel guests must practice social distancing at beaches. Tram and ferry services also resumed and groups of up to five can now practice recreational activities in open areas. Mosques, cinemas, public beaches, and nightclubs remain closed. Other emirates have followed Dubai in easing restrictions, as in Abu Dhabi, some malls have resumed business, and in Sharjah, malls and dine-in restaurants have reopened. The total number of confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the UAE was 20,386 as of May 13, and 206 deaths have been attributed to the virus. 



Assessment: Despite the consistent rise in coronavirus infections in the country, the government has been steadily easing restrictions since late April. The continued rise in infections could be attributed to a recent increase in testing among migrant and domestic workers, although this cannot be proven. It is possible that Dubai could witness a resurgence in cases following the relaxing of restrictions and increased movement. The public is advised to heed all guidance issued by health professionals and local authorities to continue efforts to stem the spread of COVID-19.

Headline: Piracy Increases in the Singapore Strait; Two Incidents Reported on Friday
Details:
On Friday, two vessels were attacked by suspected pirates in the Singapore Strait. The first incident targeted a tanker, while a bulk carrier was targeted less than two hours later. In both instances, crew were tied up but the pirates were able to escape. No significant losses were reported. In the first boarding, three pirates were sighted, while six were reportedly involved in the second boarding. 

Assessment: Since the start of the year, there have been 29 piracy incidents reported in the Straits of Malacca and Singapore (SOMS) area. This is a significant increase from the eight incidents that were reported in 2018. While the exact reason for the increase is unknown, it is possible that a new criminal group is operating in the area. The number of incidents is still much lower than the peak of piracy in the region in 2015, which saw 96 incidents. However, the relatively high numbers so far this year could be a sign that piracy is becoming a more serious problem in the SOMS area. Customers with supply chains traveling through the region should be aware of the increase of piracy incidents and consider having vessels heighten their vigilance and take other security precautions as appropriate.

Headline: Dockworkers protest against driverless trucks at Port of Los Angeles
Details: Local media sources reported that hundreds of union dockworkers with the Port of Los Angeles turned out for a protest Tuesday (April 16, 2019) morning against the use of automated trucks at one of its terminals. During a brief but packed meeting, the L.A. Board of Harbor Commissioners unanimously voted to table a decision on whether to approve a permit which would allow the Dutch company APM to use driverless cargo vehicles at its Pier 400 terminal. The five-member board decided to delay the vote in response to a letter from L.A. Mayor Eric Garcetti. The vote was followed with boos and jeers from the crowd as the approximately 5-minute meeting was quickly brought to an end. Since APM requested the permit back in September of 2018, the issue has prompted several demonstrations from Port of L.A. dockworkers who fear the introduction of driverless vehicles at Pier 400 will begin a slippery slope that will lead to the loss of thousands of jobs at both the Port of L.A. and the Port of Long Beach.

Details: The latest forecast from the National Hurricane Center has downgraded Hurricane Florence to a Category Two storm. The system continues to produce powerful maximum sustained winds of 110 miles per hour and it is likely to strengthen before landfall. During the next 12-36 hours, Florence is expected to move west-northwest and slow down, with the anticipated point of landfall being the southern North Carolina coast before moving inland. Though the storm has weakened slightly, the threat from storm surge, significant rainfall, and hurricane force winds has not diminished. A Hurricane Warning remains in effect for coastal areas from Charleston, South Carolina, to Knotts Island, North Carolina. Additionally, there remains a potential for coastal areas of Georgia to be impacted. Resilience360 advises clients to continue to stay closely apprised of the hurricane's development, as forecasts continue to evolve. Adhere to all guidance from state and local officials in anticipation of further emergency preparation efforts.

Headline: US Embassy Issued a Health Alert About Rising COVID-19 Cases in Japan and Travel Restrictions
Details:
On Monday, the US Embassy in Tokyo issued the following Health Alert:



“Location: Japan

Date: November 16, 2020



COVID-19 in Japan



The U.S. Embassy and consulates continue to monitor COVID-19 conditions in Japan. Positive test numbers are rising in many areas of Japan, and Japanese authorities are warning of a third wave of infections. Japanese media report that the effective reproduction rate nationwide has been above 1 since mid-October, meaning that the epidemic curve is rising as are hospitalization rates throughout the country. The seven-day rolling average of new cases nationwide was 951 as of November 9, up 20% from two weeks ago.



As we move into the colder months, U.S. citizens are strongly urged to continue to take personal health measures to protect themselves, including socially distancing, wearing masks, and avoiding crowded areas with poor ventilation. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) strongly recommend that U.S. citizens get flu shots to prevent a major flu outbreak. Finally, U.S. citizens should continue to obey measures introduced by Japanese officials designed to mitigate COVID-19 outbreaks in their areas.



The Hokkaido Prefectural Government raised its COVID-19 alert level to Stage Three on a five-stage scale on November 7. The government identified Sapporo’s Susukino entertainment district as a point of particular concern and asked that residents avoid restaurants that serve alcohol after 10:00 p.m. in the area. It also asked several other kinds of businesses, including host/hostess clubs and bars, to close at 10:00 p.m., and requested others stop serving alcohol at 10:00 p.m.



Okinawa continues to remain at a prefectural warning level 3 due to COVID-19, with recent daily new infections holding steady in the lower double digits. Governor Tamaki continues to urge caution, asking that diners refrain from eating or drinking in parties greater than five for more than two hours, and that companies and families continue to be vigilant with infection prevention measures.



For more COVID-19 information in Okinawa, please review the online information here and here (Japanese with machine translation).



As infection rates continue to rise in Japan, U.S. citizens are strongly encouraged to monitor changes to prefectural government alert statuses, especially when considering travel across prefectures.



Travel Restrictions



Japanese government travel restrictions remain in place that prevent most U.S. citizens from entering the country. Japan continues to modify its policies to facilitate certain kinds of travel. Recently, the Government of Japan announced new regulations permitting residents of Japan to take short business trips abroad without requiring quarantine upon their return. The rules governing this program are strict, and business travelers should be sure they understand the program before departing the country. For complete information on travel restrictions, as well as requirements for re-entry, please consult the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://www.mofa.go.jp/ca/cp/page22e_000925.html) or the Ministry of Justice (http://www.moj.go.jp/EN/nyuukokukanri/kouhou/m_nyuukokukanri01_00003.html).



Travel for tourism and most other short-term purposes is still not permitted, and there is no indication that this will change in the near term.



The U.S. Embassy strongly urges any U.S. citizens considering travel to Japan to review carefully the information available from the Government of Japan. Please note these regulations are subject to change with little notice. The U.S. Embassy’s ability to intervene on behalf of travelers denied entry into Japan is extremely limited and travelers denied entry at Japanese ports of entry will likely be immediately reboarded on flights back to the United States.



U.S. military members traveling under the Status of Forces Agreement should consult with their chain of command for the most current requirements pertaining to their entry as United States Forces Japan continues to enforce restrictions associated with a declared Public Health Emergency extended through the end of 2020.



Follow us on Twitter (https://twitter.com/acstokyo) and Facebook (https://www.facebook.com/ACSTokyo/).”



The full text of the alert can be viewed here: https://jp.usembassy.gov/health-alert-nov16-2020/

Headline: Authorities Arrest Two People Accused of Spying on Behalf of UAE
Details:
On Friday, media sources reported that Turkish authorities arrested two individuals earlier this week that purportedly confessed to spying for the United Arab Emirates. According to senior officials, authorities are investigating whether one of the detainees was sent to investigate the murder of Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi at Saudi Arabia s Istanbul consulate last year. Additionally, authorities have said that a computer seized from the so-called spy ring s base suggests a possible attempt to monitor Arab political exiles and students living in Turkey. Turkey s public prosecutor reportedly charged the pair with  political, military and international espionage  on Friday. 
 
	Assessment: The development could strain ties between Ankara and Abu Dhabi and, by extension, Saudi Arabia. The former has been somewhat estranged from the latter and their Arab allies over their nearly two-year-old land, air, and sea blockade of Qatar, one of Turkey s close allies. Saudi Arabia and the UAE have accused Doha of supporting Islamist militant groups, including the Muslim Brotherhood, with which Turkey s ruling Justice and Development Party (AKP) has close ties.

Headline: UPDATE 1 - JNPT may reach capacity and face near-complete halt in 3-4 days
Details: Updated sources indicate that severe cargo congestion is increasing at Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT) and Mundra Port as only a small portion of import cargo is being collected by carriers, and the 21-day national lockdown has minimized all export cargo. As a result, sources suggest that the key ports are facing unprecedented import cargo congestion and may reach capacity in approximately 3-4 days from April 6. At that point, sources indicate that import cargo retrieval from the ports may halt completely. Even after the lockdown period's scheduled lift on April 14, conditions may persist, and upcoming shipments to JNPT and Mundra Ports may be diverted by shippers to alternative ports such as Jebel Ali, Salalah, and Colombo.

Headline: US Embassy Issued a Health Alert About Additional COVID-19 Conditional Movement Control Orders
Details:
On Monday, the US Embassy in Kuala Lumpur issued the following Health Alert:



“Event: COVID-19

Location: Malaysia 



Recovery Movement Control Order

On August 28, 2020, the Prime Minister announced an extension of the Recovery Movement Control Order (RMCO) through December 31, 2020.  The Malaysian Ministry of Defense instituted a mandatory mask requirement effective August 1, 2020.  Failure to comply with any of the RMCO restrictions, including the mask requirement, may result in a fine of RM 1,000 (USD $235) or more, and/or jail time. 



(NEW!) Conditional Movement Control Orders

While general restrictions have been relaxed during the RMCO, specific “red zones” with higher numbers of COVID-19 cases may be placed under a Conditional Movement Control Order (CMCO).  On November 7, the Government of Malaysia announced an extension of the CMCO in effect in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, and Sabah.  The CMCO will now remain in effect until December 6.  Additionally, the CMCO has been broadened to include the states of Kedah, Perak, Pulau Pinang, Melaka, Johor, and Terengganu.  The following restrictions will continue to be enforced:



Prohibition on inter-district travel. Those who need to cross borders must present their employee pass or a letter of permission from their employer;

Only two members of a household may leave the house to buy necessities;

All schools, higher education institutions, training institutes, kindergartens, childcare centers, public parks and recreational centers will be closed;

Mosques and other non-Muslim places of worship will also be closed;

Most sports, recreational, social and cultural activities including weddings are prohibited; and

Entertainment centers and nightclubs will not be allowed to operate.



Sabah and Sarawak

Additional entry requirements may apply for travel to the East Malaysian states of Sabah and Sarawak, which have local autonomy over immigration at domestic and international ports of entry.  For detailed requirements on traveling to Sabah (https://phednp.wixsite.com/website) or Sarawak (https://sarawakdisastermc.com), please contact the local immigration authorities directly.



Sarawak state authorities announced on October 9 that beginning on October 10, all travelers to Sarawak will be required to undergo the mandatory COVID-19 testing and fourteen-day quarantine at a government facility.  Previously some travelers, including Sarawakians, were permitted to self-quarantine. 



Additionally, a travel ban to and from Sabah will be in place through December 6.”



The full text of the alert can be viewed here: https://my.usembassy.gov/health-alert-covid19-110920/

Headline: Salvage completion on Long Tau River delayed to February 2020 - UPDATE 3
Details:
Updated sources indicate that salvage operations of the VietSun Integrity have been temporarily suspended on the Long Tau River due to a major diving incident. The estimated timeline for completion of the operations has been postponed to February 2020. A channel waterway with draft restrictions of 10m has been arranged as an alternative route to Cat Lai Port. Vessels with drafts exceeding 10m have been allowed to pass on a case-by-case basis. 

Previous reporting in October 2019 indicated the following information:  

Cargo vessels with port calls at Cat Lai Container Terminal in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam are facing disruptions in freight movement and restrictions on capacity due to delays in vessel schedules after Long Tau River was closed temporarily on October 19 as a result of a maritime accident. 
VietSun Integrity, a domestic vessel, was carrying 285 unspecified containers with 17 crew members onboard when it started to list and later sank at around 01.30 (local time) on October 19, shortly after leaving the port. Although all crew members were rescued, the containers as well as the ship sank within two hours after the initial distress signal was issued. 

Marine traffic suspended
In response, Ho Chi Minh City Port authorities have temporarily suspended all marine traffic from the junction of the Dong Tranh - Long Tau River for an indefinite period and all vessels to Cat Lai have been directed to use Soai Rạp channel as an alternative route. The closure allows time to clean up 150 tons of spilled oil as well as to recover the lost containers and the ship. 

While initial reports suggested that the closure may last for up to 3 or 4 weeks, local sources on October 30 indicated that it may be extended for up to 100 days or 3 months as the salvage operation is expected to take longer. This is reportedly because the sunken ship may need to be segregated into 20 pieces with a crane. As of October 28, 63 containers have been found, about 42m3 of oil has been collected, and buoys have been placed around the accident site to prevent the oil from spreading further. 

Impact to cargo movement

The average waiting time for vessels at Cat Lai port is currently around 1.5 to 2 days with reports suggesting that marine traffic near the affected site has slowed down. Ships are also facing an increase in fuel costs due to the longer distance that need to be traversed via the Soai Rap River. Moreover, carriers are also being forced to reduce cargo capacity as the river’s depth is shallower than Long Tau River’s. 
At present, the maximum cargo capacity for carriers using the river is at 30 percent with the maximum draft restriction for vessels at 9 meters. Vessels with drafts that are above 9 meters have been directed to Cai Mep International Container Terminal, mainly used for export and import of agricultural products. As the draft restrictions limit vessels in their cargo loading capacity, some shipping lines have reportedly reduced freight at other international ports in order to have enough draft to bypass the route and to pick up goods at Cat Lai Port. As a result, carrier operations and port schedules have been impacted, especially during the peak period of import and export season, as the year is coming to an end. 

The Vietnam Maritime Administration has requested import and export enterprises to provide services at ports in Ho Chi Minh City, Vung Tau, and Dong Nai to ease difficulties for carriers. Cat Lai is the biggest container terminal in Ho Chi Minh City's port area, and is mostly used to ship containers to and from the industrial areas of Ho Chi Minh City. Everstream Analytics customers with shipments to Cat Lai are advised to liaise with local carriers and consider cargo offloading and loading options at Cai Mep - Thi Vai Port to avoid the draft restrictions. However, delays in pickup and delivery services and changes to port calls on short notice can be expected at least until the Long Tau River reopens.

Headline: Spain: Various weather warnings in place across the country for strong winds and heavy rain
Details: The State Meteorological Agency (AMET) has issued various weather warnings across the country on Thursday, 7 November. Orange weather warnings have been issued in A Coruña, Asturias, Cantabria and Biscay, due to dangerous conditions in the coastal areas. Lugo, Asturias and León have all be issued yellow warnings for snowfall. Ávila‎ and Segovia, in the centre of the country have also been issued a yellow warning for snowfall. Alicante and Valencia have a yellow warning for rough seas while Mallorca and Menorca are on the same level warning but for rainfall. Yellow weather warnings have been issued in Granada and Almeria for strong wind and dangerous coastal conditions. All the aforementioned warnings will remain in place until at least 23:59 local time on Friday, 8 November.

Headline: Virginia declares state of emergency ahead of Tropical Storm Florence
Details: Media sources indicate on September 10 that Governor of Virginia Ralph Northam declared a state of emergency on September 8 in anticipation of the potential landfall and impact of Tropical Storm Florence, as well as its potential to escalate into a hurricane. The declaration allows for mobilization of the Virginia National Guard, facilitation of interstate aid, and activation of emergency management procedures. If making landfall in or near Virginia, the storm could have a notable impact on the Port of Norfolk as well as defense installations in the area. Those conducting business in Virginia should anticipate changes in normal operations in anticipation of Florence and should plan accordingly.

Headline: Australian economy’s rebound is stronger than expected in Q3, with road to recovery paved with stimulus measures
Details: The Australian economy expanded 3.3% in seasonally adjusted quarter-on-quarter (q/q) terms during the September (third) quarter thanks to consumers and government stimulus spending, while exports were a drag on growth. The day prior to the GDP release, the Reserve Bank of Australia announced that it would keep its expansionary monetary policy settings unchanged.Consumption helps Australian economy rebound, even with Victoria lockdownAustralia real GDP (% change, seasonally adjusted)Q/QY/YNominal share (2019)Q3 2020Q2 2020Q3 2020Q2 202020182019GDP, total3.3-7.0-3.8-6.42.81.9-Exports-3.2-7.5-14.9-11.45.13.322.2Imports6.5-12.8-13.9-19.54.0-1.018.5Private consumption7.9-12.5-6.5-13.32.51.252.8Public consumption1.43.07.87.14.25.821.3Gross fixed-capital formation-0.1-4.9-6.0-5.02.1-2.522.5Source: Australian Bureau of Statistics© 2020 IHS MarkitThe September-quarter expansion was stronger than market expectations, given that the country’s second largest state economy – Victoria – was under lockdown for the entirety of the quarter. But consumers in other states came out of their coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19)-related lockdown/containment measures with significant pent up demand, which explains why private consumption expanded in real, inflation-adjusted terms at the fastest pace on record and contributed 4.0 percentage points to quarterly GDP during the quarter, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS). The increases in private consumption spending were broad-based and often achieved double-digit growth in real q/q terms, with consumers only reining in their spending on three categories: cigarettes and tobacco (down 0.9% q/q), alcoholic beverages (down 0.5% q/q), and household furnishings (down 0.9% q/q), with both alcoholic beverages and household furnishing recording robust growth in the June quarter. Meanwhile, the increase in public consumption spending arose primarily from the national government’s non-defence spending, largely tied to fiscal support measures such as the Jobkeeper programme and support for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Government fixed capital formation spending made no significant contribution to growth during the quarter, because increased investment in national defence and by public corporations were offset by reduced investment spending by state and local governments.  Private-sector fixed capital formation spending also had little impact on growth during the September quarter. There was a 5.1% q/q surge in dwelling alterations and additions, which pushed dwelling construction up 0.6% q/q – the first quarterly expansion in two years. However, the non-dwelling construction slump worsened, as investment in this category fell by another 4.9% q/q after falling 2.4% during the June quarter. Investment into machinery and equipment also fell for a second consecutive quarter – this time by 3.7% q/q – marking an improvement from the June quarter’s 8.2% q/q plunge. The positive contribution to growth from inventories during the quarter arose from a smaller decline in inventories as manufacturing, the public sector, and farms rebuilt inventories, offsetting significant inventory shedding in the wholesale sector. Net export position weighed on growth, but current account remained in surplusThe net export position was the primary source of drag on the Australian economy in the September quarter, detracting 1.9 percentage points from growth as imports recovered and exports slumped. According to the ABS’s balance-of-payments publication, the recovery in real imports was led by consumer goods, including a 48% q/q surge in motor vehicle imports, and double-digit increases for household electrics, toys, and leisure goods, as well as textiles and apparel. Services imports also rose 4.4% q/q in real terms, with indications that some of this was driven by financial services.  On the export side, there was a 2.1% q/q fall in real goods exports led by non-agricultural commodities exports, with metal ores (largely iron ore) exports falling 5.9% (largely unwinding the June quarter’s 6.2% q/q rise), while rural goods (largely agricultural products) exports were down 7.3% q/q in real terms. Services exports continued to slump but fell by a milder 8.8% q/q in real terms after two consecutive quarters of double-digit falls, caused by tourists staying away due to the bushfires of early 2020 and the spread of the COVID-19 virus globally.    The current account remained in surplus for a sixth consecutive quarter, but the surplus narrowed from the rebound in imports and sustained weakness in export receipts. The impact of the weaker merchandise and services trade surpluses was weakened by the primary income account narrowing to a 26-year low as primary income debits rose only 1% q/q, but credits arising from income earned abroad were up 14% q/q thanks to strong returns from direct investment and portfolio investment. Headline: Reports of More than 20 Ships Transporting Australian Coal Waiting for Months to Unload in China
Details:
According to recent media reports, there are at least 21 ships transporting Australian coal that have been waiting for a month or longer to unload at the Port of Jingtang in Tangshan, southeast of Beijing. Of those anchored off the coast, 15 have been waiting to dock since June. The delays come following reports last month that Chinese authorities had ordered some utilities to stop importing Australian coal. Approximately 400 sailors are onboard the ships off Jingtang, along with up to two million tons of coal. China also officially suspended imports of timber from the Australian state of Victoria this week due to bark beetles having been discovered in previous shipments. A similar ban on timber from Queensland took effect earlier this month.



Assessment: Several of the coal freighters waiting to unload at Jingtang have Indian crew members, and their shipboard conditions have drawn the attention of the Indian government. The Jag Anand, owned by Mumbai-based Great Eastern Shipping, has been waiting to berth since June, with 23 Indian crew aboard, while another ship, the Anastasia, has 18 Indian crew members. The Chinese foreign ministry on Friday denied reports that the Jag Anand has been restricted from departing China, blaming the ship’s operator for not wanting to change its itinerary for financial reasons. Great Eastern Shipping has claimed that it has tried to send the ship on to Japan for a crew change but has been unable to due to unspecified reasons. The crew is unable to disembark in China because of COVID-19 restrictions. The Indian Embassy in China is in contact with the Hebei provincial government over the ship’s situation, and the Australian government has also reached out to Chinese authorities in relation to the ship. According to the International Transport Workers’ Federation (ITF), some of the sailors on the Jag Anand have been on board for nearly two years, while the National Union of Seafarers of India has described the ships waiting off Jingtang as “floating prisons.” There is the potential for labor action in solidarity with the confined sailors, although nothing has been immediately announced. 



The directions last month from Chinese authorities to halt Australian coal imports were reportedly delivered verbally and there has still been no official indication from the government of a direct block on coal from Australia. The Australian government, however, has reported a sharp drop in demand from China for coal over the past month, and some Australian shipments have been diverted to other markets. As for the block on timber shipments due to bark beetles, Australian officials have acknowledged concerns over how effective pest fumigation is on timber from trees that were affected by last season’s wildfires, and have stated that they are cooperating with China on the issue. This would seem to indicate that the ban is a legitimate issue for China to raise, even if it fits nicely with current economic measures being taken against Australia as relations between the two countries remain low. Tensions between Australia and China are likely to deteriorate further as coal shipments remain delayed, while China-India relations could also take another hit if the sailors waiting on the ships become more of a high-profile humanitarian issue. Those with interests that might be impacted by the ongoing frictions in these national relationships are advised to remain abreast of developments.

Headline: Interstate war: Venezuelan military deployment to Colombian border...
Details: In 25 September 2018, Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro ordered the deployment of an undisclosed number of troops to the patrol the 2,219-km border with Colombia, ostensibly to conduct counter-crime operations. The deployment comes in the context of growing, through still minority, regional support for military intervention in Venezuela as well as a sharp deterioration in relations with Colombia specifically. Regional concern regarding the situation in Venezuela is growing as a result of the consistent undermining of the rule of law by the Maduro administration, as well as the country's growing economic and humanitarian crisis, which has triggered the mass migration of Venezuelans into neighbouring countries; some 2.3 million have left the country, according to the United Nations. The United States has refused to rule out military intervention in the country and is increasing pressure in the form of sanctions. In mid-September, Canada, Colombia, and Guyana, all members of the 14-strong Lima Group of countries, refused to sign a declaration ruling out military intervention. In Colombia, the new Ivan Duque administration (inaugurated 7 August 2018) has taken a far harder line towards Venezuela than that adopted by the previous Juan Manuel Santos administration, although continues to rule out military intervention. The new administration accuses Venezuela of harbouring left-wing insurgents, a sensitive diplomatic issue avoided by Santos's government. Colombia is also the country most affected by the exodus of Venezuelans, with approximately 1 million Venezuelans currently residing in Colombia.Interstate war risks are increasing and elevated in the one-year outlook, but an all-out war is unlikely. Nevertheless, there is an increased likelihood of border incidents resulting from the increased presence of military troops. Incidents are likely to include occasional gunfights between troops as a result of being misidentified as members of a drug trafficking, smuggling, or insurgent group. This is likely to be exacerbated by uncoordinated national and transnational operations by police and military forces, all of which are vulnerable to corruption, especially on the Venezuelan side of the border. An obstacle to Maduro indefinitely allocating additional troops to the border regions is that it will leave the capital Caracas and central states such as Aragua, Carabobo, Miranda, and Vargas vulnerable to increasing anti-government protests and the looting of supermarkets, pharmacies, and retail stores. An increase in protests would indicate a falling risk of interstate war, as the military would likely be redeployed away from the border to protect the capital. Headline: Police Investigating Brawl Saturday Between Millwall and Everton Supporters
Details:
On Saturday, a violent brawl broke out between Millwall and Everton soccer team supporters at about 4:40 PM local time in the area of Hawkstone Road, near Millwall s home venue of The Den in Southwark, London. The fight between dozens of males was broken up by police. One man in the clash was slashed in the face with a bladed item and was being treated at a hospital for the wound, which was not life threatening. No arrests were made in the immediate aftermath of the fight, though police are continuing to investigate the fight and identify individuals involved in the clash. A bus carrying Everton fans to the match was also targeted by Millwall supporters threw bottles and other items at the bus, smashing several windows although not resulting in any known injuries. 
 
	Assessment: Both teams are known to have hooligan supporters and there was an increased police presence in the vicinity of the match venue on Saturday. The teams were playing in fourth-round FA Cup competition. Because the security incidents occurred outside the venue grounds, the FA is not investigating the matter in addition to law enforcement, though Millwall Football Club said it is working with authorities. However, the FA and Millwall FC launched an investigation into alleged racist chanting at the match Saturday. Millwall FC said anyone found guilty of the incidents Saturday would face a lifetime ban from their home field. Resilience360 customers are advised of the risk of further clashes between opposing fans; it is recommended to avoid the vicinity of large groups of fans, including any potential hooligan activity due to the possibility of bystanders becoming caught up in unrest.

Headline: Philippine Coast Guard Increasing Patrols Around Ports of Manila, Batangas Following Robbery Reports
Details:
On Thursday, Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) officials announced that patrols and intelligence-gathering operations are being increased in the vicinity of the Ports of Manila and Batangas due to a recent rise in shipboard robberies reported by the Singapore Navy. As part of the initiative, offshore surveillance will be increased in the Bay of Manila and along the coast of southern Luzon. PCG personnel will increase the number of boarding operations of suspicious vessels carried out in the region, especially overnight. The PCG is also coordinating with local governments and law enforcement on the measures.



Assessment: The reported rise in robberies comes as the Philippine government has been promoting the use of the country’s ports as crew-change locations. According to the Singapore Navy, most of the recent robberies have been carried out by suspects entering docked ships via climbing, either from the shore or from small boats. Suspects have then used knives to threaten people on board the ships, absconding with equipment and other objects. There have been no initial reports of serious injuries in the recent incidents. PCG officials have stated that they had received reports of recent burglaries of items from ships, but no armed robberies. Those utilizing shipping in the region are advised to maintain strong security precautions on board ships, and to expect an increased coast guard and police presence in and around the Ports of Manila and Batangas.

Headline: Tensions with Indigenous Mapuches Remain High in Araucanía after Series of Protests, Arson Attack
Details:
In recent days, activists affiliated with the Mapuche indigenous community have held a series of demonstrations across the southern region of Araucanía, some of which have degenerated into violent clashes. Last weekend, protesters occupied town halls in the municipalities of Collipulli, Curacautín, Ercilla, Traiguén, and Victoria. Participants alleged that Chilean authorities had failed to comply with Convention C169 of the International Labor Organization (ILO), which holds that indigenous communities should be provided with certain protections. Some demonstrators also called for the release of so-called “political prisoners,” many of whom are members of militant Mapuche groups that have been incarcerated on arson charges. On Sunday, all of the demonstrators at such locations were forcibly evicted, in some cases by crowds of residents with no law enforcement authority. Some news outlets have claimed that unspecified “right-wing groups” instigated violent confrontations. In some cases, vehicles belonging to Mapuche protesters that had been parked nearby were flipped over and/or torched. While there were no reports of any critical injuries, media sources indicate that least 48 people were arrested. 



On Wednesday evening, a band of 15 masked arsonists carried out an attack at a factory in Araucanía’s Padre Las Casas district. At least 14 tractor trailers were set on fire, along with several structures and pieces of heavy machinery.  There were no reports of casualties. A militant Mapuche organization called Weichán Auka Mapu claimed responsibility for the attack. Araucanía Governor Víctor Manoli denounced the incident as an act of terrorism.



Assessment: Multiple factors have contributed to the recent flareup in tensions. First, the lockdown measures that have been implemented throughout the region to help prevent the spread of COVID-19 have brought financial hardship to many members of the Mapuche indigenous community. Araucanía suffered from a relatively high poverty rate (in comparison to the rest of the country) even before the onset of the pandemic. Additionally, a number of incarcerated Mapuche activists have embarked on a hunger strike at prisons in Araucanía and the neighboring region of Bío Bío. They demand that they be permitted to serve the remainder of their sentences under house arrest due to the risks posed by the pandemic. 



In an effort to defuse the situation, Chilean authorities have invited representatives of the Mapuche indigenous community to attend a summit with policymakers on Friday, August 7. While the dialogue process could potentially ease tensions, a number of similar initiatives in the past have either broken down or been boycotted by more radical elements of the indigenous community. The potential for further protest activity and arson attacks will likely remain elevated across southern Chile in the coming weeks. Those with interests in the region are advised to stay abreast of ongoing developments. Furthermore, it is generally advisable to avoid all ongoing protest activity as much as possible, as even demonstrations that are intended to be peaceful can rapidly escalate and turn violent. Additionally, any atypical behavior or suspicious items should be promptly reported to local authorities.

Headline: Customs officials seize 242 kg of cocaine in containers at Port of Rotterdam
Details: Dutch media sources on July 24 reported that customs officers working at the Port of Rotterdam found two different shipments concealing a total of 242 kilograms of cocaine, worth EUR 18 million (USD 21,15 million). Both shipments were discovered in containers, beginning with a batch of 30 kilograms found in a sea container filled with the pulp of oranges. The citrus product was destined for a Rotterdam company, and had arrived on a vessel which departed from Santos, Brazil. The cocaine was found hidden behind a wall inside the container. The much bigger load of 212 kilograms of the drug was found in a container filled with printer ink. The shipment was to be delivered to a company in Germany, after arriving in Rotterdam from Paranagua, Brazil. The drugs were found inside 11 duffel bags stuffed in the sea container.

Headline: UPDATE: Pakistan partially closes 3 international routes over Karachi until August 31; India threatens to block ships bound for Karachi Port in retaliation
Details: Updated media reports indicate on August 28 that Pakistan has closed three aviation routes over Karachi from August 28-31, according to the country’s civil aviation authority, after a senior Pakistani minister stated a day earlier that the government was contemplating a complete ban on Indian flights using the country’s airspace. The four-day ban will reportedly expire on September 1. Pilots have been provided with an alternate route to get around restrictions on the Karachi airspace. Reports suggest that the decision was reportedly taken to allow for possible missile test firing in light of recent rising bilateral tensions. In retaliation, senior Indian politician and Bharatiya Janata Party‎ (BJP) leader suggested on Twitter that India should respond by blocking ships bound for the Port of Karachi by placing a naval blockade in the Arabian Sea. Pakistan previously lifted all commercial restrictions over Pakistani airspace on the morning of July 16 after the airspace was closed to civilian flights from February 27 due to tensions between India and Pakistan in the Kashmir region. Bilateral tensions have been simmering this month after Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi revoked Kashmir’s special status. Customers are advised to monitor developments closely and re-route shipments through alternative air and land transport routes should Pakistan decide to close the airspace indefinitely.

Headline: UPDATE 2 - Joint Administrative Order issued to alleviate congestion at Port of Manila
Details:
Updated sources on April 3 indicate that a Joint Administrative Order (20-01) has been issued to alleviate severe congestion at the Port of Manila. Sources indicate that Luzon ports remain operational and that the SBITC (Subic Bay International Container Terminal) has confirmed that it can accommodate cargo overflow. The measures are detailed as follows: 

-	Importers / Consignees are directed to effect the immediate withdrawal of reefer containers or face abandonment proceedings.
-	Reefers must be pulled out within seven (7) days / chilled cargo within five (5) days from the discharge date.
-	Cargo in the terminal beyond 30 days from discharge date are required to be withdrawn within the next 5 days.
-	A list of all reefer containers in the port including names of consignees will be published in government websites and newspapers.

Headline: US Embassy Issued a Health Alert on New Restrictions Under Recovery Movement Control Order (RMCO)
Details:
On Friday, the US Embassy in Kuala Lumpur issued the following Health Alert:



“Event: COVID-19



Location: Malaysia



On August 28, 2020, the Prime Minister announced an extension of the Recovery Movement Control Order (RMCO) through December 31, 2020.  Under the RMCO, some restrictions were lifted, including the requirement to obtain a police permit and Embassy letter for interstate travel.  The Malaysian Ministry of Defense instituted a mandatory mask requirement effective August 1, 2020.  Failure to comply with any of the RMCO restrictions, including the mask requirement, may result in a fine of RM 1,000 (USD $235) or more, and/or jail time.



Conditional Movement Control Order

While general restrictions have been relaxed during the RMCO, specific “red zones” with higher numbers of COVID-19 cases may be intermittently placed under a more restrictive Conditional Movement Control Order (CMCO).  On October 7, 2020, the Malaysian government announced that the following districts will be under the CMCO for two weeks, beginning October 9:



Selangor: Klang District (including Port Klang)

Sabah: Sandakan, Papar, and Tuaran Districts

During the CMCO, movement in and out of these districts is restricted to delivery of essential goods and services.  Schools, houses of worship, and non-essential businesses will be closed.  Essential businesses will operate with restricted hours, and only two individuals per household may leave the house to buy groceries and other necessities.



Sabah and Sarawak

Additional entry requirements may apply for travel to the East Malaysian states of Sabah and Sarawak, which have local autonomy over immigration at domestic and international ports of entry.  For detailed requirements on traveling to Sabah or Sarawak, please contact the local immigration authorities directly.



Sarawak state authorities announced on October 9 that beginning on October 10, all travelers to Sarawak will be required to undergo the mandatory COVID-19 testing and fourteen-day quarantine at a government facility.  Previously some travelers, including Sarawakians, were permitted to self-quarantine at home.



Additionally, a travel ban from Sabah to Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak and Labuan will be in place from October 12 until October 25.



Malaysian Entry Requirements

On September 18, the Immigration Department of Malaysia announced (https://esd.imi.gov.my/portal/latest-news/announcement/entry-hold-my-permission-updates/) that foreign travelers with long-term passes may enter Malaysia with approval by the Immigration Department of Malaysia.  This announcement softened some of the September 7, 2020 restrictions for some travelers, which prohibited all foreign nationals from 23 countries, including the United States, from entering Malaysia.



According to the September 18 announcement, holders of the following passes may apply for entry permission: “Residence Pass-Talent (RP-T) and their dependents,  Employment Pass (Category EP I, II and III), Professional Visit Pass (PVP), Dependent Pass to expatriate for all categories, Long Term Social Visit Pass (LT-SVP) to expatriate for all categories, and Foreign Maid to expatriate for all categories.”  The Director General of Immigration may consider appeals to enter Malaysia on emergency and compassionate grounds.



On October 8, Malaysian Immigration launched a consolidated portal called My Travel Pass (https://mtp.imi.gov.my/myTravelPass/main) for all categories of pass holders to request permission to enter (or exit and re-enter) Malaysia during the MCO.  Travelers must have formal written approval from the Malaysian Government before attempting to enter Malaysia



International Students

On October 4, Malaysian Immigration announced that the entry of all new and existing foreign students, including those who had already received entry approval, will be delayed until December 31, 2020.



Malaysia My Second Home Holders (MM2H)

The Embassy has not yet received clarification on whether MM2H visa holders are exempted from the September 7 restrictions on entry by U.S. citizens.  Effective October 5, the return approval process for MM2H visa holders is managed by Malaysian Immigration rather than the Ministry of Tourism, Arts, and Culture.  Return approval may be requested from Immigration via My Travel Pass (https://mtp.imi.gov.my/myTravelPass/main).



Quarantine and Testing Information

Any travelers permitted to enter Malaysia during the RMCO are subject to COVID-19 testing and all travelers are required to undergo a mandatory fourteen-day quarantine at a facility designated by the Malaysian government.  The full cost of testing and quarantine must be borne by the traveler.Travelers who test positive are transferred to a designated government hospital for treatment; there are no exceptions to this mandatory hospitalization and at this time there no private hospitals authorized to treat COVID-19 patients.  Travelers must download the MySejahtera application and may be asked to wear a wristband for identification and monitoring by the authorities.  For additional information on quarantine requirements, please contact the Malaysian National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA).”



The full text of the alert can be viewed here: https://my.usembassy.gov/health-alert-covid19-100920/

Headline: Several roads blocked across Costa Rica today amid general strike call
Details:
Local media source reported that several points of the country suffered blockades due to the numerous trade unions and groups of workers who joined the call for a national strike against the fiscal plan:
-The step behind the municipality of San José was blocked this morning.
-The southern side of the Legislative Assembly was also closed and at around 11 in the morning all around this venue was full of demonstrators.
-In El Higuerón, Pavas, about 20 pirate taxi drivers blocked the road in the morning.
-Dozens of workers at the Mexico hospital blocked the pass over the General Cañas highway
-20th Street in front of Coopeservidores also remained blocked for several hours.
-The Paseo Colón in San José was also taken by the protesters and was closed all morning.
-A small group of demonstrators gathered outside the Max Peralta hospital in Cartago, blocking the way.
-The passage in front of the National University (UNA) in Heredia and its main roads was also blocked.
-Dozens of protesters interrupted the flow of vehicles at the entrance of Nicoya, Guanacaste.
-Finally, Route 2 (Interamericana Norte) at km 135 near Pérez Zeledón, on the bridge over the Gilguero River remained closed for several hours.

Headline: Three tanker rail cars derail in Hathazari Upazila
Details: Local media sources indicate on April 30 that three tanker rail cars in a freight train derailed on a bridge near Hathazari Upazila in the Chittagong district at 2:40 PM on April 29, with one of the three cars spilling into the Halda River. The 3 cars, full of a total of 73,500 liters of furnace oil, were en route to a nearby powerplant when the accident occurred. While first responders claim that the spill was contained, operations to restore the cars will take an unspecified number of days. Those shipping through Hathazari Upazila by rail should anticipate delays and should plan accordingly.

Headline: Two barges stolen at Tanjung Kupang Port in Malaysia
Details:
On January 17, local media sources reported that on January 13, 2 barges worth 45 million Ringgit (10,940,000 USD OR 9,590,000 EUR) were stolen by a member of the crew on duty and their unaffiliated accomplices. There was no cargo on board at the time. The vessels were associated with a Chinese mining company and were berthed near the Gelang Patah Forest City site. Media sources reported that the vessels were under lease, although it is not clear if the lease was to the mining company, or if the mining company had leased the vessels to another party. 

According to a crew member on duty, the vessels were suddenly hijacked by another crew member (out of 4) when their accomplice, an unidentified Chinese national, arrived on the scene. The hijackers then took the cell phones of the other crew members, unberthed the vessels, took the remaining crew to Johor via life boat, abandoned them, and then fled by car with multiple accomplices. While the event took place on Sunday January 13, the Johor police chief told media that the crew did not report the hijacking until Tuesday, January 15. Interpol has been contacted, and the Johor police chief relayed that he received information the vessels were near Vietnamese waters at the time of reporting.

Headline: UPDATE 1 - Mainland China’s participation in naval base upgrade supports military, commercial interests in Cambodia and South China Sea
Details: Cambodian Deputy Prime Minister Aun Pornmoniroth on 14 November again denied allegations that the government had granted mainland China exclusive rights to use its Ream Naval Base near Sihanoukville on the Gulf of Thailand. He was responding to a report from the US-based think tank, the Center for Strategic and International Studies, on 9 November claiming that Cambodia had demolished a US-funded facility at the base in preparation for Chinese construction. Earlier, Defence Minister Tea Banh had asserted that the maintenance facility cited in the report was being “relocated”, and that Cambodia “would not allow an exclusive or permanent foreign military presence anywhere in the country”. In October, Vice-Admiral Vann Bunlieng, Cambodia’s chief of the naval general staff, told Nikkei Asia that mainland China’s government was funding a project to expand Ream and deepen the waters around it. The report also mentioned that a Chinese state-owned company would carry out the expansion. In July 2019, the Wall Street Journal had first published a report quoting unnamed US officials that there was an alleged “secret deal” between mainland China and Cambodia allowing the Chinese navy to establish a permanent presence at Ream, while a new Chinese-built airport in nearby Koh Kong was suspected by US officials of having military capabilities. Significance: Although there is no independently verified evidence that parts of Ream would become a permanent Chinese naval base, mainland China’s role in its expansion suggests that it would likely be able to make frequent use of Ream’s upgraded facilities. This would likely be similar to the logistical and resupply access that the US Navy enjoys in Singapore. Chinese naval presence in Ream would improve mainland China’s ability to carry out patrols to assert its territorial claims in the South China Sea, supplementing the existing Chinese naval base at Sanya on Hainan island, thereby increasing regional military competition with the US. Additionally, mainland China is the biggest investor in Cambodia, and its military presence would increase perceived safety for Chinese staff and can help improve investment appetite for Chinese commercial assets in sectors such as tourism, real estate, and power-generation. Increasing military co-operation between the US and its “Quad” allies, India, Japan, and Australia, would provide greater incentive for mainland China to persuade Cambodia to grant it permanent presence at Ream (see Australia – India – Japan – United States: 2 October 2020: Future of Australia-India-Japan-US Quad dialogue and maritime security in the Indo-Pacific).Risks: Interstate warSectors or assets affected: All© 2020, IHS Markit Inc. Headline: Port of Hong Kong’s container terminals at the center of new Covid-19 outbreak
Details: On August 17, a new wave of the Covid-19 outbreak has hit Hong Kong with nearly half of the latest cases coming from the city’s Kwai Tsing Container Terminals. The Centre for Health Protection reported that Hong Kong recorded 74 new Covid-19 infections on Sunday, reversing the recent downward trend in cases. There are 34 cases linked to the cluster at the Kwai Tsing Container Terminal, of which 33 patients work for the same company. The center has sent more than 100 Wang Kee employees into quarantine, while Covid-19 testing is underway for more workers at the terminal. More than 10 subcontracted companies in the terminal have each had at least a few employees test positive for the coronavirus so far. The Kwai Tsing Container Terminals, located in the north-western part of Hong Kong, have nine container terminals with a total handling capacity of over 20m TEU a year.

Headline: Canada: Severe winds causes transport disruption and power outages across southern British Columbia
Details: Canadian reports have confirmed that severe winds across southern British Columbia have caused widespread disruption to travel services and impacted power to multiple locations on Thursday. Winds up to 100km/h have been recorded and come after Environment Canada earlier issued a weather warning. Roads have been closed in Vancouver, Vancouver Island, Abbotsford and Chilliwack due to uprooted trees, while ferry services between Vancouver and Vancouver Island have been cancelled. As of 19:00 local time, almost 280,000 BC Hydro customers were without power, with the majority of the outages reported across the Lower Mainland and Sunshine Coast. There is no time forecast for when the electrical services will return to the affected properties. Although the wind speeds have lessened, travellers can still expect transport disruption in the impacted areas and further interruptions to the power supply are still possible. Exercise caution when travelling in adverse weather. Monitor local media reports for area specific details.

Headline: United Kingdom: Human rights organisation plans vigils in London, 24 August
Details: The Inminds human rights organisation is planning to stage several vigils in London today, 24 August. The first will take place in the vicinity of the Embassy of Bahrain (30 Belgrave Square) between 14:30 and 16:00 (local time). This action is in solidarity with activist Ali Mushaima, who is conducting a hunger strike against the detention of his father by Bahraini authorities. The second will take place outside the headquarters of the National Union of Journalists (NUJ) in London (72 Acton Street). This has been organised to protest against the NUJ's silence at Israel allegedly targeting Palestinian journalists. The case of Palestinian journalist and activist Lama Khater will be raised, who was detained by Israeli authorities in July. Participants will gather at the location between 16:30 and 18:00 local time. Travellers are advised to bypass the locations during the protests to mitigate against any potential disruption.

Headline: Thousands of Police Officers Deployed across the Country for Undas on November 1 2
Details:
On Tuesday, the Manila Police District (MPD) said that it was deploying 4,000 officers to the Manila North Cemetery, the Manila South Cemetery, the Manila Chinese Cemetery, and the La Loma Cemetery to provide security for All Saints  Day and All Souls  Day, also referred to as Undas, on Thursday, November 1 and Friday, November 2. Security will also be increased at bus terminals, airports, seaports, churches, and other tourist sites through Saturday, November 3. A list of roads that will be closed or rerouted through Saturday by the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) can be found here:  https://www.facebook.com/pg/MMDAPH/photos/?tab=album album_id=2086294571409194 . Bags will also be checked at the entrances of the cemeteries, with alcohol and weapons being prohibited. In addition, 14,000 police officers have also been deployed to major cities in the Calabarzon and Mimaropa regions while over 4,000 officers have been deployed to the Soccsksargen region. 
 
	 
		Assessment: All Saints  Day and All Souls  Day are Christian holidays where Filipinos typically visit cemeteries to pay their respects to the deceased. The crowds at the cemeteries are large, and it was estimated that around two million people visited cemeteries in Manila last year. The Philippine National Police (PNP) has said that they are not aware of any major threats to Undas this year but that they will remain on high alert. Resilience360 customers are advised to maintain a high level of situational awareness during Undas, as Islamist militants have attempted to target other prominent Christian holidays in the past.

Headline: Incoming US administration unlikely to immediately reverse US actions against mainland China but will avoid damaging commercial interests
Details: The administration of US President Donald Trump has in recent days accelerated the imposition of targeted actions against the mainland Chinese government and its commercial interests. The US State Department on 3 December announced restrictions on visa issuance to Communist Party of China (CPC) members, which represent 6–7% of China’s population, and their immediate family members. The same day, the US Department of Defense added four Chinese companies, including state-owned energy company CNOOC, to the “Communist Chinese Military Companies” list. On 2 December, US Customs and Border Protection announced the use of a “withhold release order” to block cotton products from the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps, which the Treasury Department included on the Entity List on 31 July.   Significance: Ahead of President-elect Joe Biden’s January 2021 inauguration, the Trump administration will likely seek to impose – as much as possible – all planned measures targeting China, particularity over alleged fraudulent businesses practices, commercial espionage, state- or military-linked businesses, political influence activities, and human rights concerns. This will make it difficult for Biden to significantly retract from the current US-China strategy. However, Biden’s policy platform of a domestic-focused, pro-multilateralism approach indicates that he is very unlikely to adopt the same approach as the Trump administration. For instance, Biden’s administration is unlikely to take any new unilateral, punitive actions beyond January 2021. Although existing measures, such as tariffs on Chinese products and sanctions against CPC personnel, are unlikely to be immediately reversed after Biden takes office, Trump’s measures will give Biden additional bargaining leverage when negotiating with China on issues where co-operation is preferred on the US side, such as climate change, global vaccine distribution, and North Korea and Iran. Continuing arrests of pro-democracy activists in Hong Kong SAR by the police – or public statements against human rights concerns from Western countries – would indicate that Biden’s team will likely maintain some level of sanctions against China, such as travel restrictions and freezing assets of senior CCP officials or rejecting some state-affiliated Chinese companies from investing in US markets, exposing Chinese companies to continued US regulatory targeting. However, Biden’s approach will be more considerate of US commercial interests and more likely to involve the engagement of the US’s allies in Europe and Asia, such as the EU’s proposal for a Transatlantic Trade and Technology Council that would create negotiated technology safeguards to directly compete with Chinese-developed standards. Details: Local media sources indicate on November 15 that interim President of Bolivia, Jeanine Anez, announced her decision to leave the Bolivarian Alliance (ALBA) and said she is considering a departure from the Union of South American Nations (Unasur). Bolivia leaving the two blocs may cause disruption to the country’s trade outlook and affect tariffs.

Headline: Major Raids Target Opposition After Local Elections Inflict Losses to United Russia s Control
Details:
On Thursday, authorities raided over 200 sites across more than 40 cities in Russia. The operation was targeting opposition activists and entities and has been denounced as a political crackdown in retaliation for President Vladimir Putin s party suffering losses in last Sunday s local elections. While the Kremlin maintains a strong grip across Russia, opponent Alexey Navalny s  smart voting  plan is believed to have contributed to the erosion of United Russia s control of local office seats. Combined with sustained summer protests and increasing discontent with the status quo, the Kremlin will likely take further measures trying to thwart growth and unification of opposing forces, though activists continue to show resilience to such efforts. As well as possible protests over the crackdown and disputed election results, demonstrations over an array of other grievances may be met by crackdowns and other efforts by authorities to quash expressions of opposition and discontent.

Recent Developments

From early Thursday morning, police carried out raids in 43 cities across the country in a sweeping crackdown on opposition politicians and their supporters. The raids happened four days after local elections around Russia, which saw President Vladimir Putin s United Russia party take serious hits. During the operation Thursday, offices of opposition leader Alexey Navalny s Anti-Corruption Foundation (FBK) had equipment seized as part of an investigation launched in August for alleged money laundering, with homes searched as well. According to the FBK chief of staff, both employees and volunteers with the foundation had equipment, documents, mobile phones, and funds seized by authorities. As a result of a raid in Chelyabinsk, multiple staff at the targeted office received medical treatment on site but were not hospitalized. During searches of FBK offices in Saransk, an activist was struck and injured by a police vehicle. Election monitoring non-governmental organization Golos also reported raids Thursday targeting the homes of its activists. More than 1,000 officers were involved in the raids, and Navalny claimed more than 200 locations were searched.

The highest-profile battle over local elections occurred in Moscow, with election officials preventing or disqualifying an array of candidates for local posts, sparking sustained protests frequently marred by clashes and heavy crackdowns. However, Navalny advocated a system of  smart voting  intended to encourage people to vote for the candidate in each race considered most likely to beat United Russia or other Kremlin-backed candidates. United Russia lost more than a third of the Moscow city council seats it had previously held, with the result largely attributed to tactical voting. In addition to reported voting irregularities on Sunday, there were reports of violence and other forms of intimidation linked to the elections. A poll monitor at a station in St Petersburg who had filed a formal complaint over a voter registration matter was punched by a man who then left, while police on scene made no effort to respond. Another observer had been punched in the face several times heading into the same polling station that morning.

Election results have spurred additional protest activity in some locations around Russia, including sustained protests in Siberia s Buryatia region. At least 17 activists have been detained by authorities in Ulan-Ude while disputing the mayoral election results for the regional capital. Police contended the activists had thrown a tear gas canister at officers, while media outlets have reported police threw the tear gas canister inside a bus of activists. Potentially as an effort to defuse tensions, a rally has been authorized by Ulan-Ude officials for Sunday evening, though unauthorized protests remain possible.

Background

The refusal to register an array of opposition candidates for Moscow s local elections sparked some of the largest sustained protests in Russia in recent years. The largest demonstration drew about 60,000 participants, while thousands frequently turned out to protests in the run-up to elections, even despite major crackdowns on unauthorized gatherings. More than 2,000 people were detained during election-related protests over the summer, with some facing brief jail terms while others facing charges of mass unrest could receive lengthy jail sentences. Controversy over several issues, including pension reform, poverty and other economic concerns, as well as topics such as wildfires and waste management continue to drive discontent with the ruling powers in the country. Overt and aggressive crackdowns on protests, censorship and internet restrictions, and blatant election rigging continue to be sources of potential protest activity over perceived injustices.Assessment

Navalny supporters contend that the raids and money laundering allegations are being used to strike back at opponents of Putin and the ruling elite, particularly targeting those who backed  smart voting  tactics, protests, and other measures to combat Putin and United Russia s grasp on power around the country. The  smart voting  tactics have been invoked in other elections around the world, and could be used in future Russian elections. The method of concentrating votes with any single opposing candidate to defeat a Kremlin-supported candidate could remain more challenging to thwart. While United Russia secured victory in many regional elections, the party had substantial losses in local elections around the country.

Despite the ousting of an array of Kremlin-backed candidates with the tactic of smart voting, Communists and candidates from other smaller parties who were the primary victors from such methods generally remain at least somewhat influenced by the Kremlin. Nonetheless, in Moscow, no candidate from United Russia was on the ballot, with candidates previously with the party or otherwise pro-Kremlin opting to run as  independent  due to perceived discontent in the capital with the ruling party. Such a development highlights the growing challenges to the Kremlin s grasp on power amidst increasing disapproval of the status quo in Russia.

A heavy-handed approach to opposition forces may deter some supporters and damage the networks and resources of Navalny s FBK. However, crackdowns can also spur resistance to such tactics and opposition activists have shown resilience and innovation to authorities  efforts to stifle them. While the wave of protests during the summer has tapered off, additional demonstrations over the latest election, crackdowns, and other efforts to repress opposition supporters are possible. In conjunction, any unauthorized demonstration in Russia may face a swift crackdown by police and the Kremlin may pursue additional actions to combat any suspected erosion of support and power in the country. Resilience360 customers are advised to continue monitoring associated developments in the post-election period and to avoid any demonstration activity in Russia due to the risk of mass detentions and clashes with authorities.

Headline: 97 miles NW of Manzanillo - Tropical Depression Tara has dissipated along coast. Incident closed.
Details: Tropical Depression Tara has dissipated in the Pacific Ocean and was last tracked at about 97 miles northwest of Manzanillo, Colima, Mexico. The National Weather Service has discontinued its Tropical Storm Warning and Watch alerts for the affected coastal area; however, weather advisories issued by local officials in Mexico remained in effect, from Cabo Corrientes to Manzanillo and from Punta San Telmo to east of Manzanillo. Five to ten inches of rain were reportedly expected in parts of Nayarit, Colima, and Jalisco states on Tuesday and early Wednesday. Up to 15 inches of rain may occur in parts of western Jalisco and Colima. Such rainfall has the potential to produce flash flooding. There have been no reports of injuries from the storm. This incident is closed.

Headline: Container ship issues NUC warning after engine failure; almost runs aground on Elbe River
