Headline: Many Online Services Shut Down, Freight Shipping Largely Unaffected by Toll Group Ransomware
Details:
A ransomware attack began on Monday against Melbourne, Australia-based Toll Group, which provides shipping and warehousing services. The attack has prompted the company to shut down many online services, including online customer applications and package tracking, and employees are reportedly unable to use company computers. Toll officials have stated that shipping is mostly unaffected, although some customers may experience delays or other disruptions. The company is prioritizing the shipment of COVID-19-related medical equipment. Toll’s systems in New Zealand, where it is a major user of freight rail services, were down for around 36 hours beginning on Monday morning but many were later restored, including the Toll Global Express online customer portal. The company stated that it has been mainly using backup manual processes and will most likely continue to do so through the rest of the week. 



Assessment: Toll Group, a subsidiary of Japan Post that operates in some 50 countries with approximately 44,000 employees, was hit by a ransomware attack in February that took five weeks for the company to completely recover from. The company does not believe the current attack to be related to the earlier incident. The type of ransomware being used in the present attack has been identified as Nefilim, which is often used by suspects who threaten to expose a company’s data instead of simply erasing it if their payment demands are not met. In Toll’s announcement of the attack, the company stated that it had no reason to believe that any data had been extracted from its networks and said that the ransom demands would not be complied with. The company is instead working to restore files using backup data, clean affected servers, and rebuild its core systems. Toll is working with the government’s Australian Cyber Security Centre (ACSC) on responding to the incident. Having recently experienced a similar situation with the ransomware incident in February, the company may have better protocols in place for responding to the current crisis, and it is possible that the recovery period this time may be swifter than the earlier incident. Nevertheless, possible shipping delays and disruptions should be expected to continue at least through the end of the week, and it is likely that some residual difficulties will linger even if the current response is effective. The ACSC, which is within the Australian Signals Directorate, provides advice to businesses and individuals on protecting data from numerous cybersecurity threats here: https://www.cyber.gov.au/advice.

Headline: Exact Details Awaited as President Trump Says US Will Move to Revoke Hong Kong’s Special Treatment
Details:
On Friday, United States President Donald Trump announced that the US would “begin the process” of ending the separate treatment that Hong Kong receives from the US in some trade, travel, and law enforcement matters in comparison to the US’s relationship with mainland China. The US will also move to sanction mainland and Hong Kong officials viewed as undermining Hong Kong’s autonomy. The moves come after the passage by mainland China’s National People’s Congress (NPC) on Thursday of security legislation that the US state department earlier described as removing most of Hong Kong’s autonomy from the mainland amidst ongoing protests.



Assessment: Many details remain to be provided following the president’s Friday statement, which leaves the administration considerable latitude on how it actually chooses to proceed against Hong Kong and China. The president did indicate that Hong Kong would be subject to the same restrictions on some technology transfers that mainland China currently is, and that an extradition agreement with Hong Kong that is currently in place would be ended. His statement, however, did not specifically address whether Hong Kong would be placed under the same tariffs as the mainland, nor whether visa-free travel between the territory and the US would be affected. A complete revocation of Hong Kong’s special status in terms of its relations with the US would require at least an executive order from the president, and it is possible that the administration may only take more partial measures instead. The president also did not provide a timeframe for implementing changes in the relationship with Hong Kong. Those with interests in US-China relations are advised to follow developments as additional details on the changes are released.

Headline: CMA CGM announces port congestion surcharge for Port of Fuzhou
Details: On October 29, industry sources reported that shipping operator CMA CGM has announced a port  congestion surcharge for the Port of Fuzhou in China. According to the operator, the port is currently experiencing congestion due to longer customs inspection times of reefer imports, with most reefer plugs being occupied and supply likely to remain tight until the end of 2020. A surcharge of USD 800 per reefer unit will apply to all reefer cargo on shipments from most ports globally from November 1 to December 31. The surcharge will go into effect for reefer cargo from the US and Brazil on November 27 and remain in place until December 31.

Headline: Malaysia and Singapore De-Escalate Maritime Dispute; Should Prevent Additional Incidents
Details:
On Thursday, Malaysia and Singapore agreed to de-escalate their maritime dispute by reverting their port limits. Malaysia agreed to return Johor Baru port limits to their pre-October 2018 boundaries, while Singapore reverted its port limits to pre-December 2018 lines. The extensions had caused the port limits to overlap. Both countries have said that they will start negotiations over the disputed maritime border within a month. Singapore and Malaysia also agreed to not authorize commercial activities or anchor government vessels in the disputed area, as well as to follow international maritime law to avoid any incidents. 
 
	 
		Assessment: The maritime boundary extensions caused the relationship between the two countries to deteriorate and also resulted in confusion for international shippers. There was a minor incident in February after a Malaysian vessel collided with a Greek ship in waters claimed by Singapore that highlighted the dispute but did not result in major shipping disruptions. The return to the status quo and an adherence to international law should prevent any further maritime incidents. The negotiations will also seek to resolve disputes regarding the price Singapore pays for Malaysian water and Singapore s management of a small part of Malaysian airspace over southern Johor. Resilience360 customers with interests in bilateral relations between the two countries are advised to monitor the progress of negotiations.

Headline: Transport Workers Threaten to Strike in November after Holding a Disruptive Nationwide Action
Details:
On Monday, the Bangladesh Road Transport Workers  Federation threatened to hold another strike in November if their demands are not met by the government. These demands include the cancelation of fines for being involved in an accident and lowering the required education level for certain types of driving licenses. The workers held a nationwide strike between Sunday and Tuesday, which caused severe transportation disruptions. Many public buses were off the road, while some workers harassed and vandalized vehicles that did not follow the strike call. Services at Chittagong Port were negatively affected, as the lack of trucks going to and from the port during the strike suspended loading and unloading operations. 
 
	 
		Assessment: The transport workers said that they would give the government advance notice before holding the next strike but also said that their demands must be met within 21 days. The government has said that they would not be able to change laws before Parliament convenes next year, but the workers said that an ordinance would be sufficient. Resilience360 customers with interests in Bangladesh are advised to closely monitor the negotiations and expect similar disruptions to transportation if another strike is called.

Headline: Philippines Warns China over Thitu (Pag-asa) Island in the South China Sea; Protest Held in Manila
Details:
On Saturday, President Rodrigo Duterte warned China that occupying Thitu (Pag-asa) Island in the South China Sea would risk starting a war. His statements were in response the presence of around 200 Chinese fishing vessels around the Sandy Cay area, which the Philippine government has called illegal. The Philippine Navy has monitored around 600 Chinese vessels coming and going in the first quarter of the year. A protest was also held on Tuesday outside the Chinese Embassy in Manila, where around 1,000 demonstrators demanded that President Duterte take a stronger stance towards China. 
 
	 
		Assessment: Thitu Island is occupied by the Philippines but is also claimed by China, Taiwan, and Vietnam. Despite the strong rhetoric from President Duterte, it is unlikely that China or the Philippines would risk a major military conflict over the presence of fishing boats near Thitu Island. President Duterte has sought a closer alliance with China, especially in economic matters, and China is prepared to offer the Philippines large loans towards infrastructure projects. However, accidents or minor skirmishes involving vessels from the two countries could lead to a deterioration in relations and increase the risk of additional protests against Chinese interests. Resilience360 customers are advised to monitor the situation and avoid all areas where protests are taking place.

Headline: Attempted Murder in Surrey Investigated as Terrorism Amidst Increased Scrutiny of Far-Right Violence
Details:
On Sunday, police said an attempted murder in Stanwell, Surrey, on Saturday evening is being investigated as a terrorist incident. Suspected of being  inspired by the far-right,  a 50-year-old man allegedly stabbed a 19-year-old, inflicting non-life-threatening wounds. The older man was reported to have been acting aggressively along Viola Avenue, yelling racist remarks and carrying a knife and baseball bat. Witnesses said the assailant had yelled,  white supremacy,  and,  kill a Muslim,  before subsequently stabbing the victim in a Tesco parking lot. The attacker was reportedly a Stanwell local. 
 
	Assessment: The incident occurred amidst heightened attention of far-right violence following the Christchurch mosque attacks in New Zealand last Friday. British Counter Terror Police chief Neil Basu said the incident Saturday evening bore the hallmarks of a terror event, though it was not immediately known whether the suspect had any links to far-right groups. While the Stanwell attack was described as a terrorist incident, a suspected hammer assault outside a mosque on Cannon Street Road in Whitechapel, east London, on Friday was being investigated as a hate crime. An Asian man was wounded with a blunt object by three white men who had made anti-Muslim comments. Assistant Commissioner Basu said Friday that policing had been stepped up around places of worship and  specific communities  following the Christchurch attacks as a precautionary measure, though no specific threat in the UK was known. The incidents underscore the concern that individuals harboring extremist views, even if such people are not connected to an extremist group, may feel emboldened to undertake violence or otherwise behave aggressively following the worldwide attention of the Christchurch attacks, including the shooter s extremist views. While there remains no specific, credible threat known in the United Kingdom at this time, Resilience360 customers are advised to practice increased situational awareness when in public areas and to report any suspicious behavior or items to local authorities.

Headline: UPDATE 26 - 102 miles SSW of Roanoke– Post-Tropical Cyclone Zeta continues to move east-northeast. Event closed.
Details:
Tropical Storm Zeta made landfall as a Category 2 hurricane on the afternoon of Wednesday, October 28 near Concordia, Louisiana. Zeta has since lost tropical characteristics and was declared post-tropical. Post-Tropical Cyclone Zeta continues to move east-northeast at 55 miles per hour, while exhibiting maximum sustained winds of up to 50 miles per hour and higher gusts of 55 miles per hour. Tropical-storm-force winds will continue to extend outward up to 310 miles. Three deaths have been reported thus far; one in Biloxi, Mississippi, a second in New Orleans, Louisiana, and a third in Cherokee County, Georgia. Heavy flooding and wind damage were reported in Louisiana, Mississippi, and Alabama. 

Strong gusts are still possible across portions of eastern North Carolina, southeastern Virginia, and the southern Delmarva Peninsula during the next couple of hours. Moreover, the last of the heavy rainfall along the track of Zeta will impact the Mid-Atlantic through this evening. Additional rainfall totals of an inch or less are expected across these areas, possibly resulting in flash, urban, small stream, and isolated minor river flooding. There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.

The Tropical Storm Risk has issued a Yellow Alert for Atlantic City, NJ, Salisbury, MD, Kitty Hawk, NC, and Hatteras, NC, currently. Furthermore, a Yellow Alert has been issued for Providence, RI, Boston, MA, New York, NY, Chatham, MA, Montauk, MA, Siasconset, MA, and Belmar, NJ, within nine hours. A Yellow Alert indicates there is a 10–30 percent probability that the storm will result in maximum sustained winds of at least Category 1 strength, or greater than 50 percent probability that it will result in maximum sustained winds of at least tropical storm strength. This event is closed.

Headline: UPDATE - USA: Hurricane Dorian forecast to impact coasts of Georgia and Carolinas, as well as Florida
Details: According to the latest details on 1 September, Hurricane Dorian remains at Category 4 strength as it moves westwards at 8 mph, with maximum sustained winds of 150 mph; just shy of Category 5. Peak winds are predicted to increase to 155 mph. The weather system, previously heading towards Florida's Atlantic coast, is now forecast to target the coasts of Georgia and the Carolinas, where it may approach as a Category 2 system, bringing life-threatening storm surges. The cities of Brunswick, GA; Charleston, SC; and Wilmington, NC, could all see more than six inches of rainfall. A number of Florida’s mandatory evacuation orders have since been postponed, though voluntary requests for evacuations remain across several counties. A significant storm surge and devastating hurricane-force winds are both possible along portions of Florida’s east coast by the early-to-middle part of next week. Even while the majority of computer models predict Dorian to remain just offshore of Florida, officials have warned of significant and potentially devastating impacts. A stretch of Florida's east coast, from Deerfield Beach to Sebastian Inlet, is under a Tropical Storm Watch. Since the storm is predicted to slow down and turn northward as it approaches, the effects from wind, rain and storm surges could be prolonged. Nevertheless, the storm's path could still change and fluctuations in intensity are likely. However, irrespective of the storm’s ultimate course, significant coastal flooding is to be expected.

Headline: Cleanup Operations and Investigation Underway Following Second Recent Oil Spill Near Port Dickson
Details:
Authorities this week discovered a nearly two-mile stretch of oil along a beach at Pantai Cermin, south of Port Dickson. Officials from the Department of Environment (DOE) took samples in an attempt to discover the leak’s origin, and cleanup operations are underway. The affected beach is expected to be closed until at least Friday or Saturday.



Assessment: Although the nature of the Pantai Cermin spill has not been definitively determined, authorities have speculated that it might have come from a passing boat. Some local environmental and economic impact is expected, but officials believe that it will not be very serious. The spill is the second to occur near Port Dickson in a little over a week, following a leak that was detected in the Kampung Gelam area on October 4. That spill, which came from old crude oil pipelines, has since been cleared. Nearby disruptions should be expected while cleanup operations are carried out and an investigation is conducted into the current spill.

Headline: British National and Wife Abducted from Resort in Zamboanga del Sur; Highlighting Kidnapping Risk
Details:
On Friday, a British national and his Filipino wife were abducted from a resort they owned in the Tukuran town of Zamboanga del Sur Province, located on the western part of Mindanao adjacent to the northern Celebes Sea. The kidnapping reportedly involved six armed gunmen who used two motorized boats. At least two of the suspects had checked into the resort the day before the kidnapping. At this time, there have not been any ransom demands issued for their release. Authorities have said that they have leads on the location of the suspects and kidnapped individuals but have not released any additional information.

Assessment: It is possible that the individuals were abducted by Abu Sayyaf, a militant group that carries out kidnapping operations in the area to fund their operations. The location of the resort on western Mindanao and its close proximity to the ocean means that there is easy access for militants to carry out abductions and escape back to their strongholds in Basilan, Sulu, and Tawi-Tawi, which are located along the northern Celebes Sea and southern Sulu Sea. The group has targeted coastal resorts in the past, such as the kidnapping of four individuals from Samal Island, located off the coast of Mindanao s Davao City in 2015, and the attempted kidnapping of tourists from Bohol, which resulted in the deaths of six Abu Sayyaf militants. The group has also been blamed for dozens of kidnappings off Malaysia s Sabah State. It is also possible that the abductions are linked to the recent firing of several teachers by the two abducted individuals, although this seems to be less likely given the use of firearms and watercraft. Due to the ongoing threat posed by militants, Resilience360 customers are advised to be aware of the danger posed by kidnapping, particularly around remote coastal resorts where there is a longer response time from maritime authorities, and any resorts bordering the southern Sulu and Celebes Sea area.

Headline: Tokyo braces for impact as Super Typhoon Hagibis looms
Details:
After almost one month Typhoon Faxai battered Tokyo metropolitan area in September, the city and its surrounding areas are once again preparing to face an even stronger typhoon on October 12 as it is forecasted to make landfall near Tokyo in the morning. The Category 5 Super Typhoon Hagibis has been termed as “violent” by the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) as the highest classification in the typhoon scale carrying a maximum wind speed of 257 kilometer per hour. 
The typhoon’s intensity is expected to weaken down to a wind speed of 145 kmh by the time it reaches Japan’s shores overnight on October 11-12. Nevertheless, JMA predicts that Hagibis will bring gale force winds, high waves and torrential rain over parts of Honshu, particularly affecting coastal areas that face the Pacific Ocean and Sea of Japan. 
 
Super Typhoon Hagibis projected path over Japan and Everstream Analytics alerts; Source: Everstream Analytics

Port closure
The following seaports have confirmed closures ahead of Typhoon Hagibis. The time periods indicated in the table are approximate local times. Bunker delivery operations at Tokyo Bay and Nagoya have stopped from October 11 until October 15. Bunker prices are unlikely to be affected as suppliers have reportedly made necessary adjustments to their bunker delivery schedules. 

Port   	        Status	Closing date	         Expected reopening date
Tokyo 	        Closed	October 11	        October 13, 12:00 or October 14, 05:30
Yokohama	Closed	October 11	        October 13, 12:00 or October 14, 05:30
Chiba	        Closed	October 12	        October 13, 12:00 or October 14, 05:30
Nagoya	       Closed	October 11	        October 13, 12:00 or October 14, 05:30
Kobe	       Closed      October 11, 12:00	October 13, 06:00
Osaka	     Closed	October 11, 12:00 	October 13, 06:00


Airline and rail disruptions
Japan Airlines (JAL) and All Nippon Airways (ANA) have announced cancellation of over 800 domestic flights and 72 international flights via Tokyo’s Narita and Haneda airports from October 11 to 12. Airports that are located along the forecast path of Typhoon Hagibis are likely to face disruptions; these include Nagoya Chubu, Osaka Itami, Osaka Kansai, Sendai airports. Singapore Airlines and EVA airways have also cancelled and rescheduled over 23 international flights to various destinations in Japan scheduled for October 12-13.

Narita is Japan’s top air cargo hub with reported cargo volume of 2.2 million tons in 2018; Kansai and Haneda Airports ranked second and third accordingly. While these airports have not indicated temporary closures on October 12, further flight cancellations may impede air shipments to cause cargo backlog for 24 to 48-hours at least until October 14.   

For rail, fast speed rail services by East Japan Railway Co., Central Japan Railway Co., West Japan Railway Co. will be suspended on October 12 in Hokuriku, Kyoto-Osaka-Kobe, Northern Kinki, San-in and Wakayama lines. JR East operations may also stop both regular and Shinkansen lines in Tokyo area on October 12-13. The Odakyu Electric Railway and Tobu Railway companies will also restrict services in Kanto region. 
Industry Impact 

The projected path of Super Typhoon Hagibis and Typhoon Faxai takes a similar track despite its different intensities. Nevertheless, similar impact can be expected as Tokyo Electric Power Company has warned residents to take measures to prevent blackouts. Everstream Analytics data shows that facilities from four industries are cluttered primarily in Kanagawa prefecture. These include Socionext Inc., chip manufacturer, Mitsui Chemicals, Yorozu Corporation, a manufacturer of automotive and agricultural machinery parts, and Therabiopharma Inc., a biotech firm. Nippon Steel has already announced temporary production halt at its plant in Kimitsu city, Chiba prefecture for safety. The firm has decided to stop blast furnaces and repair works at its plant following infrastructural damages due to Typhoon Faxai. As a result the firm had stopped part of a production line that makes alloy steel materials for automobiles.
 
As the storm’s path as well as its intensity is unpredictable and may change at a short notice, Everstream Analytics customers with sub-tier suppliers based on the path of Super Typhoon Hagibis should prepare for logistical arrangements ahead of the storm. Majority of Japanese manufacturers normally shut down factories for a 24-hour period for safety. However, flooding and power outages are the biggest challenges for manufacturers after the typhoon passage, as inundated roads prevent employees from commuting to business sites and resume productions without appropriate power voltage. In addition, companies are advised to monitor Japan Meteorological Agency for information on weather related warnings as well as to have hurricane preparedness plan on standby to implement when necessary.

Headline: UPDATE 1 - Election unlikely to affect Jordan’s COVID-19 recovery plan, focus on reducing state spending and growing agribusiness, pharmaceuticals
Details: Jordan’s King Abdullah II during a summit with Iraq and Egypt held in Amman on 25 August 2020. Jordanian Kingdom Council/Handout/Anadolu Agency via Getty ImagesKing Abdullah II has directed Bisher al Khasawneh, interim prime minster until elections are held on 10 November, to focus on combating the COVID-19 pandemic, improving health care provisions, and economic recovery. The policy priorities set out by the king will likely be carried over to the next cabinet. The king appoints the prime minister and directs government policy, and election results do not affect the formation of the cabinet, making it highly unlikely that the election will result in policy changes. The high daily rate of COVID-19 infections (2,459 on 18 October) make it increasingly likely that the election will be postponed, and Khasawneh will remain in office beyond the ‘interim’ period. King Abdullah outlined a series of objectives in his letter of designation on 7 October, including increasing foreign investment and completing public-private partnership projects, enhancing medical tourism, and expanding Jordan’s food processing, pharmaceutical and medical supplies industries. IHS Markit expects Khasawneh’s cabinet to present a more detailed government plan in the coming week. Lack of investment in agriculture and pharmaceutical sectors, combined with a slow recovery in tourism, will very likely undermine the pace and outcome of policy. Jordan's pharmaceutical sector is one of the most developed in the region, but lacks the levels of private investment required to significantly improve production and export capacity. This limits its longer-term growth potential. Increasing protectionist policies in other Middle East markets will also make regional export growth difficult. In an effort to increase food security, Jordan is likely to reintroduce live dairy cattle imports and impose supportive policies for farmers to bolster domestic production and exports of fruit and vegetables. Even if live cattle imports resume, IHS Markit does not expect activity in the dairy industry to recover in the next three years, as more investment is needed in logistical infrastructure. Multilateral investments in company expansions are likely to advance as Jordan’s government prioritises food security. Equally, the important tourism sector (15% of GDP in 2019) is unlikely to recover to previous levels in the one-year outlook, making significantly increased medical tourism unlikely. Rising unemployment was already a main driver of protests in Jordan, and combined with the government’s need for fiscal austerity will very likely increase the frequency and scale of protests going into 2021 (see Jordan: 13 April 2020: Unemployment protests in Jordan likely to increase after COVID-19 virus outbreak and 28 June 2019: Jordan: Instability risks). Unemployment increased from 19% in Q4 2019 to 23% in Q2 2020, according to the Jordan Department of Statistics. The global economic slowdown due to the COVID-19 pandemic and the kingdom’s state of emergency limiting business operations will likely result in continued stark increases. On average, the economy is only able to create 30,000–40,000 jobs per year, which is insufficient to cover around 100,000 Jordanians that are joining the labour market each year. The trend of people who are unemployed regularly staging peaceful protest marches and sit-ins, especially around government buildings, is almost certain to continue. Continued economic decline (weak growth averaging 2.4% during 2010–19 compared with 6.6% growth from 2000 to 2009, and a growing budget deficit, expected to reach 7.0% in 2020 given lower revenue and COVID-19 pandemic-related costs, and remain elevated at 4.1% of GDP in 2021) has necessitated austerity measures, raising the likelihood of protests becoming larger and more frequent. Any effort to reduce subsidies and/or public-sector salaries as a means to limit the budget deficit, or further government decisions that allow companies to reduce employees’ salaries, would be likely to trigger protests and strikes by public sector workers, notably by teachers. A prolonged state of emergency is also likely to generate protests involving unemployed youths, trade unions, and opposition parties (see Jordan: 31 July 2020: Jordanian actions against dissent, including application of COVID-19 state of emergency, increase protest risk around November election), extending well into 2021. Such action would involve thousands peacefully rallying outside the prime ministry and royal court in Amman. Opposition primarily stems from the Islamic Action Front (IAF) – the political arm of the Muslim Brotherhood, who are likely to organise protests as a means to influence politics after the November election.Indicators of changing risk environmentIncreasing riskA new surge in infections would increase likelihood of the election being postponed and continued curfews hampering business activities, also increasing the likelihood of protests. Poor voter turnout, of around or below 25%, and reduced parliamentary representation for the IAF (which won 25% of the vote in 2016, but only 15 of 130 parliamentary seats) would encourage better co-ordination among the opposition to stage protests, with the capability of gathering thousands compared with the current trend of hundreds. Reports of widespread arrests and perceived excessive use of force by security forces during protests would likely result in protesters engaging in violence during demonstrations, including throwing loose and incendiary items at security forces and government buildings. Critical statements or protests by the “National Committee of Military Veterans”, most likely following and in support of trade union strikes, likely encourage larger participation, thereby increasing pressure for policy and constitutional changes.Decreasing riskJordan’s daily rate of COVID-19 virus infections stabilises, indicating that curfew would be likely to be eased, and encouraging the prospect of improvement in tourism activity. Additional financial aid from international lenders, especially money specifically for job creation, would reduce pressure on the state to increase public spending. Headline: South Africa’s road freight in jeopardy amid xenophobic attacks on foreign drivers
Details:
Cargo trucks driven by foreign nationals in South Africa have faced violent attacks by local truck drivers and other unknown groups since the beginning of the year and the situation has worsened in recent months. The recent attacks escalated after truck drivers affiliated with the National Truck Drivers Founders and All Truck Drivers Foundation (ATDF) issued an ultimatum for foreign truck drivers to vacate their jobs by December 1. This is because South Africans associated with the foundation believe that truck driving is not a specialized skill and can be done by a local driver. Protests against foreign truck drivers have been well-attended in urban centers, and interstate highways and key thoroughfares have been blocked intermittently. 

The anti-foreign sentiment towards foreign truck drivers and their employers in South Africa is not uncommon and the recent unrests associated with the hiring of foreign truck drivers in South Africa are expected to persist over the coming weeks, as the South African National Cargo Transport Drivers Association on December 17 has given 21 days to the National Bargaining Council to deregister all foreign truck drivers. The situation remains fluid, as foreign truck drivers have also threatened to ban South African drivers from entering neighboring countries if they are forced out of their jobs. 

Targeted highways:
Although South Africa’s President Cyril Ramaphosa has condemned the xenophobic attacks, little has been done to protect road freight logistics. Since November 19, 35 cargo trucks have been petrol-bombed. According to media sources, 9 trucks were set alight on the N3 highway during the course of a day, before the foreign drivers were attacked and their cargo looted. Other attacks include vandalism and road blockades with burning tires, making it impassable for vehicles. On November 23, a driver was fatally shot and another injured. The following roads and locations have been targeted since late November: 

•	Kwa Zulu-Natal province: N3, R103, R23, and R550 roads 
•	Free State province: the R59 between Parys and Sasolburg 
•	Gauteng province: N3 in Johannesburg, N12 in Benoni, and R21 in Boksburg 
•	Mpumalanga province: Key routes in Bethal 

In retaliation, foreign truck drivers have threatened to block South African truck drivers from crossing land borders into other neighboring countries, if they are forced to leave their jobs in South Africa. Any such attempts may lead to unrest at cross-border points resulting in congestion or delays for freight trucks and customs processing time, which is already significantly impeded by COVID-19 restrictions. 

Impact on road freight:
South Africa relies heavily on the road freight sector as about 90 percent of freight moves via land transport, particularly the N3 highway that connects between Johannesburg and Durban. It is also used as a key route to transport export and import goods from the Port of Durban to the capital. In recent months, the industry has been hampered by varying disturbances, including traffic congestion at border points, increasing cargo thefts, protests, and violence related to socio-economic issues resulting in road blockades, and mounting storage and demurrage costs on imports and slower freight clearance. In September, cargo trucks faced congestions at South Africa’s border checkpoints with Mozambique, Botswana, and Zambia as protesters against foreign truck drivers and blocked roads. 

Additionally, the South African economy is still reeling from the effects of the COVID-19 lockdowns. When the government imposed a level-5 COVID-19 lockdown in March 2020, local importers had to bear the storage and demurrage cost of around ZAR 1.4 billion (USD 95 million; EUR 77 million) while over 20,000 containers were left in storage facilities, according to the South African Association of Freight Forwarders. While the economy is still at a recovery stage, the recent protests against the hiring of and attacks on foreign truck drivers have caused panic amongst some logistics companies in utilizing their assets and resources, with some haulers having to downsize jobs as trucks stand idle. 

Anti-foreign sentiments:
Demonstrations and attacks against foreign truck drivers are not uncommon in South Africa as there is a widely held perception that trucking companies favor hiring foreign nationals as they accept lower wages. Moreover, the conflict comes at a time of high levels of unemployment amid the economic fallout from the COVID-19 pandemic, fueling xenophobic sentiments across the country. According to the South African Labor Ministry, at least 84 attacks have been registered since April 2020 over the employment of foreign truck drivers. While the ATDF claims that its motive does not stem from xenophobia, precedents indicate that the same type of aggression was directed specifically at foreign drivers and their employers.

Businesses with foreign truck drivers should consider additional security measures and reconfirm the status of routes prior to the journey.

Headline: Hong Kong prohibits US eggs and poultry based on departure date
Details: Industry sources indicate on March 15 that Hong Kong has issued a ban on imports of US eggs and poultry out of preoccupation for exposure during the avian influenza incubation period, and concern of its potential entry to the mainland Chinese market. Products produced before the incubation period will be permitted provided they were shipped before the ban imposition. The US Department of Agriculture (USDA) has further guidance related to the ban. Those shipping eggs and poultry from the US to Hong Kong should be mindful of the trade restriction and should plan accordingly.

Headline: Hwy 401 & Hwy 403 - No major disruptions after rolling blockade protest. Incident closed.
Details: An unspecified number of protesters participated in a rolling blockade travelling from London toward Six Nations on the Grand River via Highway 401. The action was organized in solidarity with the Wet'suwet'en Nation which is opposed to the Coastal GasLink Pipeline in their indigenous territory. No major disruptions were reported. This incident is closed.

Headline: Hong Kong   Seventeen people under quarantine reportedly tried to flee. Event closed.
Details:
On Saturday, March 7, Media sources reported 17 people who were under mandatory quarantine tried to flee. They were all stopped at the border. Four charter planes reportedly transported 533 Hong Kong residents back to Hong Kong from Hubei Province on Wednesday, March 4 and Thursday, March 5. Before returning, the residents were tested four times, and upon arriving in Hong Kong their temperature will be checked again and then they will be transported directly to the quarantine center to begin a 14-day quarantine. A 14-day quarantine will also be implemented for all Hong Kong residents that have visited South Korea, Iran, and three impacted regions in Italy due to the COVID-19 virus. If the resident has visited Daegu or Gyeongsangbuk-do in South Korea, they must undergo compulsory quarantine. Visitors arriving from Korea or visitors that have visited Korea in the past 14 days will not be allowed to enter Hong Kong. Anyone who traveled to the Emilia-Romagna, Lombardy, and Veneto regions in Italy are impacted by the quarantine. 

Since Saturday, February 8, travelers to Hong Kong from mainland China have been required to self-quarantine for 14 days. The government order applies to Hong Kong residents, citizens of mainland China, and foreign nationals who have been in mainland China within 14 days of arriving in Hong Kong, even if the travelers are arriving from a third country. Residents of Hong Kong may undergo their self-quarantines at home, while travelers may self-quarantine in their hotels or other accommodations. Those who do not have a place to stay for 14 days will be placed in government facilities. Authorities say that the self-quarantines will be vigorously enforced, and that those who avoid them may face prosecution and imprisonment. Some people who are involved in cargo transportation between Hong Kong and mainland China will be exempt from the quarantine requirement. Reports indicate all schools across Hong Kong are expected to remain closed until at least April 20. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) issued travel guidelines alongside a Level 1 warning for travelling to Hong Kong. This risk event is closed. 

Due to the broadening scope of this situation, this event is being closed and coverage has been consolidated in the Worldwide Travel Advisory. If you do not receive the consolidated reports, you can log onto the Resilience360 system to view new information.

Headline: COVID-19 Outbreak in Russia Continues to Worsen with New Record Levels of Daily Cases
Details:
On Wednesday, April 15, Russia set a new one-day record rise in COVID-19 cases for the country as the outbreak continues to grow. There were 3,388 new cases announced on April 15, bringing the official total of cases to 24,490. The bulk of confirmed cases have been in Moscow (14,776), with a substantially lower level of confirmed cases in St Petersburg (929), the next most affected city. Russian officials have reported only 198 COVID-19 deaths in the country in total. President Vladimir Putin gave a fourth national address on April 15 to announce additional financial support for companies hit by the outbreak and associated nationwide restrictions. The Kremlin has reported that more than half of businesses beyond Moscow had halted operations, with the majority struggling to continue paying employees. Putin earlier said the military may be mobilized to support the outbreak response. As a digital permit for movement was rolled out in Moscow on Wednesday, long lines to enter metro stations were reported, in addition to traffic jams exceeding the usual congestion. More than three million Muscovites received passes to leave their place of residence on Monday, while some 900,000 were denied a digital pass. The volume of movement has spurred fears of exacerbating the outbreak while the city of Moscow’s health department warned of a possible shortage of hospital beds for COVID-19 patients within the coming two to three weeks.



Assessment: Russia’s data on the spread of the virus has been met with suspicion and concern that the outbreak is more severe than official numbers indicate. There are also standing concerns that Russia’s healthcare system, including being able to test and treat patients, is insufficiently equipped to respond effectively and efficiently to the worsening outbreak. The mayor of Moscow introduced restrictions earlier than many other regions of the country, with the capital under lockdown since March 30. As the virus spreads more beyond metropolitan areas, rural communities may experience higher rates of severe illness and deaths from COVID-19 with fewer resources to treat patients. 



While Putin has announced some financial assistance, calls continue for greater government support for businesses and individuals in response to concerns that an insufficiently robust level of government spending will deepen an outbreak-related recession at least in the coming months. The International Monetary Fund has estimated that Russia’s economy would contract by more than five percent in 2020. However, the Kremlin has previously appeared wary of appearing as the central figure in responding to the outbreak, resulting in more of a region-by-region response. In addition to many Russians facing the choice of financial hardship or attempting to continue work, the upcoming weekend may exacerbate outbreak mitigation challenges as churches take an array of approaches regarding worshippers physically attending services for Orthodox Easter. It is advised to heed the guidance of local, national, and international authorities as the outbreak continues and as government restrictions and advice continue to evolve.

Headline: Arrests, Clashes with Authorities Following Sentencing of Quim Torra; Further Protests Likely
Details:
On Monday, September 28, the Supreme Court officially supported the decision of the Superior Court of Justice of Catalonia (TSJCAT) to sentence Catalonian President Quim Torra for a crime of disobedience and effectively remove him from office. The initial ruling of TSJCAT banned Torra from government office for a period of 18 months and fined him EUR 30,000 for refusing to take down a banner supporting pro-independence leaders from the balcony of the regional government’s headquarters in March 2019. The banner reportedly referred to former Catalan cabinet members, legislators, and activists who had been imprisoned or left the country following a 2017 declaration of independence. Torra’s deputy, Pere Aragones, is expected to take over as president-in-charge until the regional parliament elects a new leader or a new election is held. Pro-independence activists have called for protests across Catalonia, with several demonstrations taking place across the province of Barcelona on Monday. Protesters allegedly threw pigs’ heads, building materials, stones, and a firecracker at Mossos d’Esquadra guarding the Public Prosecutor’s Office. A march was held in Jardinets de Gracia, thousands attended a socially distanced rally near Placa de Tetuan, and approximately 60 people demonstrated in front of the Palafolls City Council. Protesters who gathered at Ciutadella Park reportedly broke into one of the entrances granting access to the Parliament’s doors and were dispersed by Mossos d’Esquadra, following which some of them continued to protest at Ronda de Sant Pere, where they reportedly set up barricades and burned containers. The demonstrations were called by organizations such as the Committees of Defense of the Republic, Omnium Cultural, and the Catalan National Assembly. At least five public disorder arrests were made during the demonstrations.



Assessment: While there has been opposition to TSJCAT’s decision, including a manifesto denouncing the disqualification of the president published by the Catalan National Assembly of Andorra, the Supreme Court judged that the decision did not violate Torra’s right to free speech, just limited what he could do in his role as an elected official. Torra’s predecessor, Carles Puigdemont, was removed from office following the 2017 push for the region’s independence, fled to Belgium, and had fought extradition to Spain. Nonetheless, Torra has stated that he will take his appeal against the ruling to European courts, purportedly including the Strasbourg Court. He has also called on Catalans to turn the next elections, scheduled for February 7, 2021, into a “de-facto plebiscite on independence” by voting for separatists. Polls and election results, however, suggest that there is a more or less even split among the 7.5 million Catalan residents on the subject of independence from Spain. Further demonstrations are expected in the run-up to elections. It is advised to continue to monitor developments in the time leading to the elections due to ongoing tensions over Catalan independence from Spain. It is also advised to avoid all protest activity due to the likelihood of arrests and the potential for clashes between pro- and anti-independence demonstrators, as well as with authorities.

Headline: Production Cuts at Shell and LYB as Houston Ship Channel Partially Reopens as Cleanup Continues
Details:
A seven-mile stretch of the Houston Ship Channel has partially reopened as of Monday, March 25, following a three-day closure due to contamination caused by a fire last week at an Intercontinental Terminals Company (ITC) facility in La Porte, TX. The closure extended from Tucker Bayou, which is near the ITC facility, to Houston Ship Channel light 116. The closure was initially enacted on Friday due to multiple contaminants from the fire, including gasoline, suppressant foam, and the chemical benzene, being detected in the water. As of this writing, at least 31 vessels were waiting to enter the channel and at least 31 vessels were unable to leave the Port of Houston. Outbound traffic has reopened to vessels with less than a 34-foot draft and only during daylight hours. Ships are moving through the opening spaced at approximately one-hour intervals and all vessels are required to be inspected for chemical contaminates. 
 
	Assessment: Cleanup efforts are ongoing but there remains no estimate for when the channel is expected to fully reopen to tanker traffic. The U.S. Coast Guard is not expected to completely reopen the channel until it is confirmed that the benzene has dissipated and the oil runoff has been collected or dispersed. Several test vessels were initially sent through the affected area and were successful in not interfering with cleanup or being contaminated before the Coast Guard partially reopened the channel. 
 
	The Houston Ship Channel closure has so far only affected tankers and there are no reports that any cruise or container ships have been impacted. Royal Dutch Shell and LyondellBasell Industries (LYB) have both cut productions at their refineries, located on the waterway, due to the channel closure. Shell has reduced output by approximately 275,000 barrels a day due to a shortage of crude oil. A portion of the Shell processing units remain in circulation so that normal production can resume quickly after the channel is fully reopened. Meanwhile, LYB has cut production by approximately 14 percent due to the inability to remove sulfur generated during fuel production and having limited storage on site. As of yet there has not been a significant impact on the price of crude oil and officials do not anticipate the channel closure turning into a long-term issue.

Headline: KwaZulu-Natal   Protests reported at Howard College and Edgewood campuses on Monday.
Details:
Updated reports indicate that on Monday, February 17, protesters have gathered at the Howard College and Edgewood campuses of the University of KwaZulu-Natal (UKZN). Protesters reportedly burned tires, which were removed by police, though there were no initial reports of violence. Expect disruptions in the area of UKZN campuses. 

On Friday, February 14, four student protesters were arrested after unrest broke out at the Steve Biko Campus of the Durban University of Technology. The individuals blocked the entrance of the campus, and damaged windows of one of the dormitories. There were no reports of injuries.

On Tuesday, February 11, protesters marched from the Howard College Campus to the Durban City Hall before holding a demonstration at the City Hall. There were no reports of violence or major disruptions associated with Tuesday's march. Lectures remain suspended at all University of KwaZulu-Natal campuses until further notice due to violent protests. University officials also met with students on February 12, to continue negotiations regarding the registration period, which has now been extended until March 6. Students have agreed to intensify their strike actions. Negotiations between UKZN representatives and the Minister of Higher Education were previously expected on February 10. 

Previously, on Monday, February 3, protesters demonstrated near the UKZN Edgewood campus in Pinetown, the Pietermaritzburg campus, and the Howard College Campus. One building at each of the campuses was set alight. At the Howard campus, demonstrators set fire to the HIV support center and challenged security guards with rocks and sticks. In retaliation, the guards fired rubber bullets at the crowd, and one of the protesters was injured. Furthermore, students vowed to burn the school down if they were not allowed to register.

Demonstrators are protesting a university policy that requires students to pay 15 percent of their historic debt prior to class registration. The expected duration of the protest has not been specified. Avoid protest activity due to the potential for violence.

Headline: Man Arrested in Barcelona on Friday Suspected of Plotting Terror Attack Amidst Lockdown
Details:
On Friday, authorities in Barcelona arrested a man suspected of plotting a terror attack in the Catalan capital. The suspect is a Moroccan man who had pledged allegiance to Islamic State (IS) and had demonstrated his radicalization over some four years. The man had been observed violating COVID-19 lockdown restrictions frequently, raising the suspicion of authorities that he may have been preparing an attack and evaluating different locations to strike. The suspect was taken into custody at his residence along Calle Josep Anselm Clavé, 1-2 blocks from La Rambla. Authorities did not indicate that any firearms or other more sophisticated attack implements had been acquired or constructed.



Assessment: The arrest underscores the ongoing threat of terrorism in Europe, including by individuals heeding calls from groups such as IS to carry out attacks in one’s place of residence. Authorities within and outside of Spain had been monitoring the suspect and were able to coordinate on the observation and arrest activities. Terror-related arrests linked to potential plots still occur on occasion around Spain, though Catalonia has not suffered a major terror attack since the August 2017 attacks in Barcelona and Cambrils. While no specific ongoing threat is known at this time, it is advised to maintain strong situational awareness in public areas and to report suspicious behavior or items to local authorities.

Travelers should continue to keep apprised of the situation via local media and follow all issued guidance. Additionally, travelers should adhere to a robust protection plan and maintain an adequate supply of water and non-perishable foods.

Headline: UPDATE - Jamaica: Multiple arrests reported in second day of State of Emergency police operations in Kingston
Details: Media sources report that authorities have detained 15 people in connection with ongoing State of Emergency police operations in the Corporate Area of Kingston. A spokesperson with Jamaica Constabulary Force's Corporate Communications Unit confirmed that several of the detainees were identified as persons of interest for breaches of the Dangerous Drugs Act. Security checkpoints have been established along the following roadways: Oakland Road, Spanish Town Road, Waltham Park Road, Delamere Avenue, Rousseau Road, Lyndhurst Road, Studio One Boulevard, Slipe Road, Harbour Street, Pechon Street, Maxfield Avenue, Orange Street, and Ocean Boulevard. The declaration is expected to remain in effect until Sunday, 7 October. Travelers should maintain valid identification on their person if transiting the aforementioned areas and allow additional journey time as established security protocols may impact travel.

Headline: Job Bill Protests Likely to Continue Despite COVID-19 Restrictions; Demonstrations Dispersed Tuesday
Details:
On Monday, Indonesia’s House of Representatives passed a controversial omnibus law on job creation. The legislation, which is intended to spur job creation and lower unemployment by allowing employers more flexibility in hiring decisions, has drawn opposition for revising required severance payments, allowing irregular working hours, and changing the way that minimum wage is calculated. It also removes some tax and environmental regulations for companies. The Confederation of Indonesia Trade Unions and other associations have embarked on a general strike through Thursday in opposition to the bill, with as many as five million people expected to participate. The bill drew largescale protests on multiple occasions in the months before its passage, and demonstrators gathered in various cities across the country on Monday and Tuesday.



Assessment: While the authorities have not explicitly said that protests related to the job law are banned, police officials have stated that large gatherings will remain barred under COVID-19 gathering restrictions. A demonstration against the law that was expected to see up to 5,000 people gather outside the House of Representatives in Jakarta on Monday was largely blocked by police preventing buses carrying protesters from entering the capital. Demonstrators who made it to the protest location were dispersed by officers. On Tuesday, demonstrations were dispersed in at least two cities. In West Java, police used teargas to clear thousands of demonstrators after firecrackers and rocks were thrown and a police vehicle was damaged. At least ten people were arrested. In Banten Province, a demonstration was dispersed with water cannons in Serang. Two police officers at the protest were reportedly injured when rocks were thrown by demonstrators. Authorities have created “cyber patrols” on some social media platforms in order to monitor protest actions, and while additional demonstrations are likely, it is probable that they will face a heavy police response. The Indonesian government has faced previous criticism of using the COVID-19 pandemic to push through controversial pieces of legislation while protest activity can be curtailed. It is advised to avoid the vicinity of any demonstrations due to the risk of escalation.

Headline: Tropical Storm Beta Forms in the Gulf of Mexico Bringing Flooding Threat to the Texas Coast
Details:
Tropical Storm Beta formed in the Gulf of Mexico on Friday and is currently located approximately 360 miles southeast of Corpus Christi, TX. The storm is forecast to meander through the gulf before making a westward turn on Sunday and strengthen into a Category 1 hurricane. Landfall for the storm remains uncertain; however, Beta is expected to move up the Texas coast and could potentially make landfall south of Houston on Tuesday or Wednesday. The National Hurricane Center (NHC) has not issued watches or warnings related to the storm as of Friday afternoon; however, the NHC warned these are likely beginning Friday night or on Saturday. The most up-to-date details on the storm, including path and strength, can be found at the following link: https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/. 



Assessment: Significant uncertainty exists regarding the current path and eventual strength of Beta. Initial estimates suggest that Texas communities along the coast from Brownsville to Houston could see upwards of 12 inches of rain from the storm. Officials have cautioned that the slow-moving nature of Beta could lead to a scenario that just occurred with Hurricane Sally in Florida and Alabama. Sally’s slow movement prior to and during landfall allowed for excessive rainfall with some areas, such as Pensacola, FL, reporting over 25 inches of rain and life-threatening flooding. Though none have been issued as of this writing, evacuations remain a possibility for coastal communities in Texas as the path and strength of the storm become clearer. Due to the potential impacts and uncertainty, those with interests along the Texas coast are advised to closely monitor developments related to Tropical Storm Beta. Emergency plans, potential evacuation routes, and disaster supply kits should be prepared and reviewed.

Headline: U.S. Mission Issues Alert as Protests Escalate and Militants Threaten Attacks on Oil Facilities
Details:
On Tuesday, the U.S. Mission in Nigeria issued the following Protest Alert for U.S. citizens in the country:



“Multiple demonstrations are ongoing across Nigeria – to include areas within the consular districts of Abuja and Lagos.  Although most demonstrations are peaceful, some have become violent and have shut down major thoroughfares and bridges.  Some police stations have been targeted.  Lagos State closed all schools indefinitely as of October 19 due to protests and implemented a 24-hour curfew starting at 4:00 p.m. on October 20.  Consulate General Lagos is closed for the rest of today and tomorrow. 



We continue to urge all U.S. citizens to avoid areas around protests and demonstrations and to check local media for updates and traffic advisories.  Continue to be vigilant and avoid areas affected by the protests.”



The entire Protest Alert can be viewed at the following link: https://ng.usembassy.gov/health-alert-u-s-mission-nigeria-37/



Assessment: Protests over alleged police brutality have escalated across Nigeria over the last few days, as demonstrators have attacked and torched a number of police stations, including in Lagos and Oyo, and helped orchestrate a prison break in Edo state over the weekend. Security forces and unidentified thugs have also continued to attack and clash with demonstrators, leaving at least 18 people dead since the protests began on October 8, including four on Monday alone. In response to the escalating violence, police have announced plans to deploy anti-riot police nationwide; however, the move could further exacerbate tensions and heighten the risk of further clashes between the two sides.



Additionally, there have been reports that militants in the oil-rich Niger Delta region have expressed solidarity with the demonstrators and threatened renewed violence if the demonstrators’ demands are not met. The Reformed Niger Delta Avengers (RNDA) issued a statement that its fighters have been placed on standby to engage Nigerian troops and resume attacks on oil facilities. In particular, the RNDA has singled out the Escravos-Warri-Kaduna distribution pipeline, Chevron Valve platform, Shell Forcados Terminal, Escravos trans Lagos pipeline, Escravos Tank Farm, and the Bonny Export Terminal. The threats suggest that militant groups could be exploiting the protest movement, broadening the demonstrators’ demands, and could heighten the risk to critical infrastructure, such as oil facilities.

Headline: Third Explosive Device Found in Hong Kong; Alleged Perpetrators Threaten Further Attacks
Details:
On Tuesday, a homemade explosive device was found at the Shenzhen Bay Control Point, located inside the Hong Kong Port area. A security guard found the palm-sized improvised explosive device (IED) inside a rubbish bin at approximately 10:25 AM local time and alerted police. Approximately 20 police officers and explosive ordnance disposal bureau officers responded and rendered the device safe. No injuries were immediately reported. The IED was nitrate-based and was reportedly designed to be detonated by a cell phone. Following the incident, a Telegram channel named  Dad finds boy  allegedly claimed responsibility for planting the IED and stated that it was  only a start.  In the message, the perpetrators ordered the government to close the border with mainland China within two days and threatened to  destroy railways and roads  connecting the two if no progress is made within three days. However, the claim remains unverified.

Assessment: Tuesday s IED was the third found in Hong Kong in just over 24 hours after two homemade explosive devices detonated inside toilets at the Caritas Hospital early on Monday morning and at King George V Memorial Park on Monday evening. While police are continuing to investigate all of the incidents, there has been some speculation that they could be linked to the ongoing anti-government protests and could imply that demonstrators are seeking to take advantage of the 2019-nCoV outbreak in mainland China to bolster their movement. It is also not unheard for pro-Beijing individuals to pose as protesters on Telegram to make threats, which have not materialized in the past. Although the three explosive devices were placed in confined areas, possibly to minimize serious injuries and damages and serve as a warning, the risk of further explosions is likely to remain elevated over the coming days and the potential that bystanders could get caught up in the blasts cannot be ruled out. As such, customers with interests in Hong Kong are advised to exercise an elevated level of vigilance over the coming days and report any suspicious objects to police.

Headline: Police Continue to Investigate Incidents of Drone Sightings that Shut Down Gatwick Airport
Details:
Sussex Police are continuing to investigate numerous drone sightings that caused the intermittent shutdown of London s Gatwick Airport (IATA: LGW) between December 19 and 21. At least 67 people reported sightings of drones during what are believed to be 37 separate occurrences over the course of the three days, with police officers, airport security personnel, and pilots among the witnesses. Around 1,000 flights and 140,000 airline passengers were impacted by the sightings, which did not totally end until the deployment of military anti-drone equipment to the airport early on the morning of December 21 local time. Two suspects who were arrested on the evening of December 21 were released without charge on Sunday. 
 
	Assessment: Despite a detective s statement over the weekend that it was possible that there were never actually any drones near the airport, Sussex Police said on Monday that they could  unequivocally state  that there had been numerous sightings, with the detective s doubt said to be a miscommunication based on the fact that no video evidence of drones had yet been acquired. Police were conducting house-to-house investigations near the airport over the weekend, and were examining a damaged drone that was found near the airfield. Members of parliament have criticized the Sussex Police handling of the investigation, including the misstatement over there being no drones and the apparent mistaken arrest of the two initial suspects, and have suggested that London s Metropolitan Police might be better equipped to handle such a high-profile investigation. Officials did not confirm what anti-drone military equipment was dispatched to the airport, but media sources reported that it was a  Drone Dome  system, which is designed to interrupt communications between a drone and its operator. Defense officials consulted with the CEOs of all UK airports on December 21, with Minister for Security Ben Wallace saying that military counter measures can be deployed against drones at airports across the country if needed, although it can be difficult to station certain types of equipment at civilian airports. Gatwick Airport itself has spent US $6.3 million ( 5 million) on unspecified additional anti-drone technology since the start of the incident, which it described as a  deliberate act to disrupt the airport s operations.  The airport is also offering a US $63,000 reward for information leading to suspects in the case, with another $12,000 being offered by the Crimestoppers organization. Under UK law, it is illegal to operate a drone within one kilometer (.6 miles) of an airport, and the maximum penalty for endangering an aircraft is five years imprisonment. The case is being investigated under the Aviation and Maritime Security Act. While there has been no indication that there is any ongoing imminent threat to Gatwick or other airports from drones, Resilience360 customers are advised to expect associated travel disruptions in the event of further drone sightings.

Headline: London, Canada Strike Short-Term Deal to Avoid Tariffs as Post-Brexit Trade Deal Gain Steam
Details:
Media sources report that the United Kingdom and Canada have struck a deal to prevent tariffs on goods and services between the two countries after the Brexit transition period ends at 2300 GMT on December 31. Reached on Tuesday, the agreement will see the parties continue to give one another’s products preferential tariffs until their respective parliaments ratify the Trade Continuity Agreement put forward last month. Canada’s House of Commons reportedly failed to approve the document prior to its holiday recess, which would in theory have resulted in trade between the countries no longer being covered by the Canada-EU free trade deal starting January 1. Bilateral trade between the UK and Canada was valued at US $22.5 billion in 2019, with London representing Canada’s fifth-largest trading partner and third-largest export market. For its part, Canada is Britain’s 15th-largest export market.



Assessment: Tuesday’s development comes amid reports that British and EU officials have made progress toward a post-Brexit trade deal. Previously, optimism that the parties would be able to reach an agreement to avoid tariffs and quotas on the UK’s foreign trade prior to January 1 was low, raising concerns of potential job losses, price increases, significant port congestion, and temporary shortages of some goods in the event that the UK would have to trade with the EU on World Trade Organization terms. Although it has been reported that some final issues had yet to be resolved, Western media sources suggested a deal could be announced as soon as Wednesday night, which would presumably remove many of these uncertainties. If a deal is not reached, most local observers have speculated that Britain would take the greatest hit, at least immediately, as the country is regarded as more reliant on trade with the EU. Such a scenario would also hurt the parties’ economically by stunting efforts to rebound from the COVID-19 pandemic. The public should stay apprised of developments related to the Brexit transition, as any deal is likely to at least entail changes to travel and immigration procedures.

Headline: Guangzhou Guangyou Communications Equipment Co., Ltd. placed on U.S. Entity List
Details: Media sources indicated that the U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) added Guangzhou Guangyou Communications Equipment Co., Ltd. to the U.S. Entity List for its alleged role in helping the Chinese military construct and militarize the South China Sea. A total of 24 Chinese companies were added to the list. Headline: IRGC Fires Missiles at Mock US Aircraft Carrier in Show of Force
Details:
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) launched underground ballistic missiles at a replica US aircraft carrier during military exercises in the Strait of Hormuz, near the port city of Bandar Abbas, on July 29. As a result, US troops were reportedly put on alert at the al Dhafra Air Base in Abu Dhabi and the al Udeid Air Base in Qatar. One day prior, the IRGC fired a missile from a helicopter targeting the same fake carrier. Wednesday was expected to be the final day of the maneuvers, in which several units from IRGC’s Navy and Aerospace Division took part. Such military exercises have the potential to result in casualties in cases of mistaken fire, though the maneuvers on July 28 and 29 passed without incident.



Assessment: The incident appears to be geared toward demonstrating Iran’s strength of its missile program, and intimidating US troops in the area. While, an Iranian military commander stated that this was Iran’s first successful attempt to carry out the launch of underground ballistic missiles, the military is known to have vast underground bases hiding its ballistic missile arsenal. In addition to highlighting the country’s network of subterranean projectiles, the military exercises also underline the lingering threat of military conflict between Iran and the US, after a series of escalating incidents last year led to a drone strike in January 2020 that killed Qassem Soleimani, the commander of the IRGC’s Quds Force. Additional incidents, including US officials calling for the UN weapons embargo on Iran, set to expire in October, to be renewed, and an incident on July 23, in which US fighter jets reportedly flew too close to an Iranian passenger plane near Beirut, have also renewed tensions. Despite appearing to heighten tensions, the maneuvers are likely only a show of force designed to intimidate the US, and do not necessarily increase any likelihood of direct confrontation between the rivals.

Headline: UPDATE: Venezuelan military further reinforces bridge blockade between Cucuta and Tachira
Details: Local media sources indicated on March 21 that Nicolas Maduro has ordered a reinforcement of the military roadblock with freight containers on the Puente Tienditas on the border between San Antonio del Tachira and Cucuta in Colombia, underway since February 5 and last reinforced on February 21. The blockade is impeding the entry of humanitarian aid into Venezuela. The military presence will be accompanied by the FAES Special Forces Police as well as the Bolivarian Militia. This development is the latest that started with customs processing at the Aduana Principal de San Antonio del Tachira being frozen on September 26, around the same time when the Director of Border Affairs and International Trade for Fedecamaras-Tachira announced a suspension of customs processing at the customs house in San Antonio del Tachira, a principal border town in Tachira state. As a result, as of initial reporting, 31 export operations, 33 import operations, and 29 customs agents have been paralyzed. The order came from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and is believed to target imports from Colombia, including, but not limited to, apparel, metalwork, industrial grains, yucca, soap, wood, vehicular components, tanks, and oxygen cylinders. San Antonio del Tachira is the principal gateway for ground commerce between Venezuela and Colombia. Those shipping between Colombia and Venezuela should anticipate further difficulties in cross-border commerce between the two countries and should plan accordingly.

Headline: Likely collapse of Yemen's Hodeidah ceasefire and government offensive...
Details: Risks: Civil war, TerrorismSectors or assets affected: Marine, Ground cargoThe Houthi movement announced at a news conference in Sanaa on 16 March that its forces would strike Riyadh and Abu Dhabi with ballistic missiles if the implementation of the United Nations (UN)-sponsored peace deal in the port city of Hodeidah was breached. The Houthis claimed to have intelligence that the internationally recognised Yemeni government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia and the UAE, is preparing to resume its offensive on the port city. The Hodeidah ceasefire came into force on 18 December 2018, but there has since been no progress on implementation of a joint withdrawal from the city. Saudi Arabia and the UAE are reportedly now insisting that they are no longer willing to wait.Significance: IHS Markit assesses that the fundamental disagreement between the Houthis and the government over who will provide the 'local forces' to provide security in Hodeidah after a withdrawal is unlikely to be resolved peacefully, and that the UN-sponsored ceasefire is very likely to collapse in the coming weeks. Should this be the case and a government offensive to recapture the city goes ahead, there would be a severe risk of indiscriminate property damage in the city and the adjacent port from Saudi-led coalition airstrikes and shelling, and protracted urban warfare. Faced with the loss of Hodeidah, the Houthi movement would most likely destroy port facilities and deploy sea mines, making the port unusable for at least several months, and resume missile and IED attacks against coalition shipping in the Red Sea. An indicator signalling an imminent government offensive would be an intensification in shelling of Hodeidah's southeastern neighbourhoods. An agreement by both sides to further face-to-face talks on a specific date would at least temporarily reduce the likelihood of a government offensive. In the event of a government offensive, Houthi retaliation would probably also involve the launch of 'Scud'-type missiles and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) strikes at military and infrastructure targets against Saudi Arabia, although their impact would be mitigated by Saudi Patriot air defences. Houthi UAVs are unlikely to have the range to strike targets in the UAE, despite a claimed UAV attack.                     Content provided by IHS Markit Foresight © 2019

The USGS also detected a magnitude 6.9 aftershock in the area that struck less than ten minutes after the initial tremor. EMSC (European Mediterranean Seismological Centre) is a scientific international organization, which aggregates and provides information generated by national seismological agencies worldwide. EMSC presents earthquake data across several magnitude scales including local magnitude (ML), surface-wave magnitude (Ms), body-wave magnitude (Mb), and moment magnitude (Mw). All magnitude scales should yield approximately the same value for any given earthquake.

Reportedly only one crew avoided pirates, the rest were kidnapped.

Headline: US Customs and Border Protection issues seaport inspection guidance
Details:
Industry sources indicate on August 3 that the US Department of Customs and Border Protection (CBP) has issued guidance for seaport inspectional processes which will take effect immediately. For cargo ships arriving from COVID-19 travel suspended countries, CBP is delaying the inspection of the crew until 14-days after foreign departure.  The crew remains onboard until inspected.  All vessels will be required to submit a security plan to include the hiring of additional guards for all vessels arriving from suspended countries.  Once the 14-day mark is passed, CBP will inspect the crew and may issue landing permits. In some cases, the ship may depart the port before 14-days and in those cases, the crew is remaining on board for the duration. This applies to vessels and crew arriving from the following countries: 
Iran, China (excluding Hong Kong and Macau), Austria, Belgium, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Italy, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, United Kingdom, Ireland, and Brazil.
