Headline: UPDATE 7 - Canada - Production has resumed in sectors nationwide after COVID-19 disruptions. Event closed.
Details:
As of late November 2020, production stoppages across Canada have mostly ended, and suspensions have been lifted. While a complete detailing of information has not been provided, there are no indications of sector-wide impacts. Nonetheless, companies may have imposed specific COVID-19-related measures to suit their business needs. Below is a summary of stoppages in Canada throughout the COVID-19 pandemic:

Ford Motor confirmed on Sunday, May 10 that it plans to reopen its Oakville Assembly plant in Oakville, Ontario on the week of May 25. The plant builds the Ford Edge and Lincoln Nautilus models.

A Cargill meat-processing plant in Chambly, Quebec shut down operations on Wednesday, May 13 due to a COVID-19 outbreak at their facility. At least 64 employees were infected. Approximately 171 employees were sent home already due to them being sick or having contact with someone with symptoms. Cargill’s High River, Alberta facility was set to resume operations the week of May 4 after temporarily shutting down on April 20 due to an increase of COVID-19 cases among its 2,000 workers. At least 821 Cargill employees tested positive for the virus, and one person affiliated with the facility died.

A poultry processing facility in Coquitlam, British Columbia suspended operations after an outbreak of COVID-19 among the staff at the location. The plant, which is owned by Superior Poultry Processors Ltd. was shutdown by Fraser Health following the discovery that two employees tested positive for the virus. All employees of the plant were screened, and those testing positive or who came into close contact with the individuals were told to self-isolate. Officials at the Canadian Food Inspection Agency advised there was no evidence to believe the virus is transmitted through food, and no chicken products from the location have been recalled. The plant is a sister facility to the United Poultry Co Ltd. in Vancouver, which shut down on Tuesday, April 21 after 29 employees tested positive for COVID-19.

Iamgold temporarily suspended operations at its Westwood gold mine in Quebec on March 25. Eldorado also temporarily suspended operations at its Lamaque gold mine in Quebec at the same time. Provincial authorities in Quebec previously ordered the closure of all non-essential businesses, including mines. Both facilities have reopened. Additionally, several measures have been implemented to ensure that employees are scanned for symptoms upon arrival at the locations.

Media sources indicated multiple meat producers reduced production at plants across Canada, including the Cargill meat facility in High River, Alberta due to COVID-19. Industry leaders have reportedly warned of possible effects on Canada's meat supply


Ford reportedly halted production at all facilities in Canada beginning after evening shifts on Thursday, March 19, and initially expected the closure to last through at least March 30. GM also suspended production at all facilities in Canada on Wednesday, and stayed closed through at least March 30.

Toyota extended the suspension of production at all of its Canadian facilities after conducting sanitation efforts in response to COVID-19 concerns. The initial closure took place on March 23 and 24. The most recent estimates suggest that production is now expected to resume on May 4.  

Cameco Corporation has placed its Port Hope UF6 conversion facility in a temporary shutdown state for approximately four weeks due to difficulties in keeping an adequate workforce. Production at the Blind Refinery is also temporary suspended for approximately four weeks; however, it remains open to receive uranium concentrate deliveries. Additionally, Cameco has announced that production at the Cigar Lake uranium mine remains suspended amid COVID-19 concerns. The suspension began on March 23, and was initially expected to last until Monday, April 3. The production stoppage will impact approximately 300 employees.  During this time, the operation will be placed into care and maintenance. About 35 employees will remain on site during the stoppage. On March 24, Orano Canada Inc suspended production at its McClean Lake uranium mill due to COVID-19 concerns, and 50 employees will remain onsite for care and maintenance. The suspension was expected to last two weeks. Updates indicate that both suspensions have been extended to last at least four weeks in total. Cameco is the world’s largest publicly traded uranium company. 

Fiat Chrysler Automobiles (FCA) began shutting down all facilities in Canada on Wednesday, March 18, and initially intended to remain closed through at least the end of March. Sources now indicate that the company has extended the stoppage until at least May 4 due to ongoing disruptions caused by COVID-19.

Honda has halted production at its auto plant in New Tecumseth since March 18. The suspension of production was expected to last through March 31, but was extended until at least May 1.

SSR Mining Inc. halted production at its Seabee gold mine, located in northern Saskatchewan Province, until at least April 30 due to COVID-19. Workers will be paid, and a small group of 20 people per shift will maintain minimum necessary operations. Additionally, Trevali has halted production at its Caribou zinc mine in New Brunswick Province due to the COVID-19 outbreak.

Longview Aviation Capital Corporation announced the suspension of the new production of Dash 8-400 and Series 400 Twin Otter aircraft. The production stoppage will impact approximately 1,000 employees, including employees of De Havilland Canada, of which Longview Aviation is the parent company. The decision to halt production of the aircraft was made due to uncertainty caused by the COVID-19 outbreak.

Operations at the Irving Shipbuilding Inc Halifax Shipyard, located near Barrington Street and N Marginal Road, were originally expected to be suspended for three weeks as of March 19 in response to the COVID-19 outbreak. Reports state that at least 1,100 of the 1,800 employees would be released as a result. The closure has since been extended indefinitely due to continued concerns regarding the spread of COVID-19. This event is closed.

Headline: United Kingdom: Woolwich Ferry to end services in East London until the new year
Details: Services on the free Woolwich Ferry across the River Thames in East London are due to terminate on 6 October until the new year. The Woolwich Ferry links Woolwich and North Woolwich, (near London City Airport), for which a ferry service has been in operation since 1308. The boats are being replaced with more environmental vessels, and the service temporarily discontinued while new berths are built. The final crossings will be made at 19:45 local time on 6 October. Travellers who use the ferry crossing regularly will need to consider alternative routes from 7 October. Note any height and weight restrictions on alternative bridge crossings as necessary.

Headline: Karachi Port   Operations are reportedly resuming following apparent hazmat incident. Event closed.
Details:
Pakistani media sources report that operations are resuming at the Port of Karachi following a purported hazmat incident in the nearby Keamari area earlier this week. The Pakistan State Oil (PSO) corporation and several private oil companies had closed storage terminals at the port to ensure the safety of workers, triggering reports of shortages and subsequent panic-buying by Karachi residents on February 19. Local schools that had been closed the previous three days have also reopened, with most factories and commercial establishments resuming operations as well. However, local news outlets said that residents were still practicing precautionary measures due to lingering air quality concerns, notably wearing face masks.

There were conflicting reports regarding the nature of the situation, with some sources suggesting that a gas leak in Keamari left 14 people dead and caused some 500 others to fall ill since February 16. However, others attributed the incident to soybean dust that was dispersed during the unloading of a docked ship, causing allergic reactions, while local scientists blamed the casualties on the release of a chemical used to fumigate vessels. The reason for the discrepancy was not immediately clear. Affected individuals complained of chest pains, breathing difficulties, and burning eyes, and came from areas including Jackson Market, Railway Colony, Majeed Colony, Shireen Jinnah Colony, and Sikanderabad. In addition to the human toll and disruptions to operations at oil terminals, dozens of people staged a protest on February 18 over the failure of authorities to detect and correct the problem. This risk event is closed.

Headline: Security Increased Nationwide for All Saints and All Souls Day on 11/1, 11/2; No Confirmed Threats
Details:
On Monday, the Philippine National Police (PNP) said that it was on full alert status for All Saints Day (Undas) and All Souls Day on Friday, November 1 and Saturday, November 2. More than 35,000 police officers have been deployed across the country in order to ensure public safety. The PNP has said that they are not aware of any direct threats to the holidays. A  red alert  will be declared from Wednesday, October 30, which will result in a tightening of security at transport hubs, malls, and cemeteries and will remain in place until Sunday, November 3. The  red alert  for ports and seaports will be active through Tuesday, November 5. The Manila International Airport Authority (MIAA) has advised travelers to arrive at airports at least two hours in advance due to expected delays.

Assessment: All Saints Day and All Souls Day are Christian religious holidays where around 15 million Filipinos visit over 4,600 cemeteries and memorial parks to honor their ancestors and the saints. While the PNP has said that they are not aware of specific threats, there is still a moderate risk of terrorism in the country and Christian religious holidays have been targeted by Islamist militants in the past. There is also heightened concern that militant groups, many of whom have pledged allegiance to the Islamic State, will attempt to carry out attacks in response to the recent death of Islamic State leader Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi. Resilience360 customers are advised to exercise a high degree of caution during the upcoming holidays and should expect an increased security presence, which could lead to transit delays.

Headline: Protests and Clashes in Hong Kong around the New Year a Sign That Unrest Is Likely to Continue
Details:
On Wednesday, protesters gathered for an approved march from Victoria Park in Causeway Bay to Chater Garden in Central. Organizers claimed that over one million people participated in the march, while police said that attendance was around 60,000. Violence took place just a few hours after the march started, with some protesters vandalizing a HSBC branch in Wan Chai. Police responded to the scene and clashed with protesters, using pepper spray and tear gas to disperse those in the area. A Starbucks store was also vandalized in Tin Hau. The march was ordered to end at around 5:30 PM but thousands refused to return home, and later blocked roads, vandalized buildings, and threw objects in multiple areas, including Wan Chai, Central, and Causeway Bay. Police used tear gas, water cannons, and pepper spray. Around 400 people were arrested, with the majority detained in a single police operation near SOGO in Causeway Bay.

Assessment: The large turnout on New Year s Day and the violent clashes that followed shortly after is a clear sign that unrest is likely to continue for at least the near future. The level of violence is still lower than what was seen in October and early November, where protesters held multiple days of disruptive actions, first in early October with the National Day protests and the face mask ban, and then in November with the citywide strike and takeover of universities. There was a brief lull in demonstrations in the immediate lead up and aftermath of the local district council elections in late November, but protest activity began to increase again in December, with shopping centers targeted and central and southern Kowloon (Tsim Sha Tsui, Yau Ma Tei, and Mong Kok), along with northern Hong Kong Island, seeing disruptive demonstrations and violent clashes. Overall, the protests since December have been more geographically contained when compared to those in October and early November, making the disruptions easier to predict and less widespread, although this may not hold true in the future, as the movement has shown that it is adaptable and can change tactics quickly. Customers should continue to exercise a heightened level of caution at all times, as protests may be called with little notice in advance, and all demonstration activity should be avoided due to the risk of clashes.

Headline: China to Allow Nepal to Access Ports, but Lack of Sufficient Infrastructure Will Slow Progress
Details:
On Friday, Nepal s government announced that China will allow access in the future to four sea ports in Tianjin, Shenzhen, Lianyungang, and Zhanjiang, as well as land ports located in Lanzhou in Gansu Province, and Xigatse and Lhasa in the Tibet Autonomous Region. The date for when the agreement would be signed between Nepal and China was not specified. Nepal s government said that it would increase connectivity with the Asian market and reduce cargo transit times between Nepal and countries like Japan and South Korea. 
 
	 
		Assessment: Nepal has been seeking increased access to China in order to reduce its dependence on India for nearly all critical goods. This dependence was highlighted by a blockade along Nepal s southern border with India in late 2015 that resulted in severe shortages of basic products like fuel. While the agreement regarding land and sea port access is a long-term positive development, Nepal currently lacks the road infrastructure to fully take advantage of significant amounts of overland trade from China. If such infrastructure is developed, it could result in a diversification of Nepal s trade sources, but it appears that the country will remain dependent on trade from India for the near future.

Headline: Container terminals close gates in Genoa following bridge collapse; to reopen on August 16
Details:
Transportation and logistics in and around the port city of Genoa have been paralyzed since midday on August 14 after the central span of the Morandi Bridge, a flyover bridge supporting the A10 highway, collapsed onto rail tracks and warehouses. Container terminals at the Port of Genoa, located about 5 kilometers from the bridge, have preemptively closed their gates on August 14, preventing trucks from entering the gates to load or unload containers. Vessel operations were said to continue as usual, and gates are expected to reopen by August 16. 

Road and rail traffic throughout the city of Genoa has already been significantly compromised since August 14. With only one bypass available via the SS1 road and bridge construction works likely taking months before completion, congestion, delays and additional fees will likely affect road, rail and ocean freight transportation from and to Genoa over the coming months. Customers should be mindful of the following transportation impacts when planning shipments to, from or through the Genoa area: 

1.	Cross-terminal movements between the major container terminals VTE and SECH in Genoa, which are linked by the Morandi Bridge, are likely to suffer delays. This is expected to affect export containers in transit, which may miss cut-off times on vessel services. 

2.	Container movements between Genoa and industrial centers such as Torino and Milan in Italy, as well as the French border near Menton, is likely  to experience extended delays as trucks are re-routed via smaller, congested connection roads towards the A12 highway to the north or the A10 highway to the west. 

3.	As rail tracks are likely to remain closed in the short term, potential alternative modes of transportation such as intermodal rail traffic from the Port of Genoa to Milan will also be affected by the bridge collapse. Since containers from Milan are usually connected to Germany through the important Rhine Alpes Rail Corridor via Switzerland, rail exports from factories located in the port area of Genoa are expected to face delays and congestions. Factories in the area include the Ilva steel mill that supplies hot-rolled steel to automotive, packaging and energy customers. 

Customers are advised to monitor recovery efforts in the area and consider the aforementioned impacts to transportation when planning cargo movement in the area.

Headline: UPDATE 1 - US Embassy Issued a Weather Alert for Typhoon Noul
Details:
On Thursday, the US Embassy in Hanoi issued the following Weather Alert:



“Location:   Central Provinces Quang Binh, Quang Tri, Thua Thien – Hue, and Danang City



Event: Typhoon Noul will land in the central provinces as early as 9 a.m. local time on Friday, September 18, 2020.



The U.S. Embassy in Hanoi and Consulate General in Ho Chi Minh City alert U.S. citizens to Tropical Storm No. 5, also known as Typhoon Noul. The storm is currently east/southeast of Danang, Vietnam and expected to make landfall near Hue Friday, September 18 or Saturday, September 19. Wind speeds of 80 mph/130 kph are predicted. Vietnamese authorities are instructing maritime vessels to return to port and for residents to prepare for heavy rains, winds, and flooding of low-lying areas, with the possibility of some evacuations. Northern and central localities should expect heavy rains of up to 300 mm a day. Rainfall of 180 mm a day is considered heavy. From Thursday afternoon to Friday, central provinces from Quang Tri to Thua Thien-Hue may be hit by heavy rains of 300-400 mm a day. Mountainous areas could be affected by landslides while urban areas face heavy flooding. We encourage U.S. citizens in the central area of Vietnam to follow the news closely and to take precautions appropriate to their situation.During the approach of a typhoon you should monitor the U.S. Joint Typhoon Warning Center (https://www.metoc.navy.mil/jtwc/jtwc.html) and the Vietnam National Center for Hydro-Meteorological Forecasting (https://kttv.gov.vn/KttvsiteE/en-US/2/index.html) (Tiếng Việt).



Actions to Take:



You should have an emergency plan in place before the approach of a storm. Even areas far from the coastline can experience dangerous winds, tornadoes, mudslides, and floods. Please take precautionary measures to ensure minimal disruption or damage, and have evacuation plans that do not rely on U.S. government assistance. You should also contact friends and family in the United States with updates on your whereabouts.



We strongly recommend that U.S. citizens traveling to or residing in Vietnam enroll in the Department of State’s Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) at www.Travel.State.Gov.  STEP enrollment gives you the latest security updates, and makes it easier for the U.S. embassy or nearest U.S. consulate to contact you in an emergency.  If you don’t have Internet access, enroll directly with the nearest U.S. embassy or consulate.”



The full text of the alert can be viewed here: https://vn.usembassy.gov/weather-alert-typhoon-noul/

Headline: UPDATE 1 - US State Department calls for divestment away from US-listed Chinese equities, reinforcing threat of potential forced delistings
Details: NYSE President Tom Farley, Alibaba Chairman Jack Ma, and Alibaba CEO Daniel Zhang attend the ceremony of ringing the NYSE Opening Bell over long distance at the Water Cube on 11 November 2015 in Beijing, China.Visual China Group via Getty ImagesInternational media reported on 18 August that the US State Department had asked US colleges and universities to adjust their endowment portfolios to reduce their exposure to Chinese assets. The Department cited the possibility of a “wholesale delisting” of mainland Chinese firms due to stricter regulatory requirements. Direct drivers for the recommendation include allegations of fraud and lack of transparency in company operations. According to the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB), in the 18 months preceding July 2020, access to 202 mainland Chinese and Hong Kong SAR public companies’ audit work papers were restricted. The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission further highlighted that among those based in mainland China, at least 11 are Chinese state-owned companies and 49 had denied PCAOB access to conduct its most recent inspections in September 2018. The Washington regulators assess that non-compliance with US accounting standards – including providing access to such documentation – exposes investors to potential accounting fraud, such as in the recent case involving Luckin Coffee, when investors lost almost all the money invested in a 2019 flotation after the company reported materially incorrect disclosure of its financial performance. The timing of the delisting threat also suggests that it is part of a wider political objective to reduce Chinese exposure taken by US asset managers. Prior to the announcement, the two countries had negotiated audit disclosure using a 2013 Memorandum of Understanding on Enforcement and Cooperation. The recent move comes in the context of Washington targeting Chinese companies across multiple fronts, including human rights, national security, and Chinese Communist Party (CPC) affiliations, irrespective of their listing status. A 6 August announcement by a working group under President Donald Trump’s administration ordered the tightening of disclosure requirements for Chinese companies listed on US stock exchanges. Under the proposed changes, the principal audit firms (or co-auditors) of currently US-listed Chinese companies would have until 1 January 2022 to submit detailed documentation of their auditing process to the PCAOB, without which the firms will face delisting. This executive action is related to the recent Holding Foreign Companies Accountable (HFCA) Act bill, which was introduced on a bipartisan basis and set a compliance deadline of 1 January 2023. The bill passed the Senate in a unanimous vote on 20 May and is currently awaiting review by the House Committee on Financial Services.Chinese companies, particularly state-owned enterprises, are unlikely to comply with additional disclosure requirements from the US, increasing the likelihood of at least some companies delisting from US exchanges in the coming year. China’s Revised Securities Law, which was implemented on 1 March 2020, blocks accounting firms from sharing securities-related information abroad without the approval of the China Securities Regulatory Commission. Beyond one-year outlook, higher US regulatory hurdles will discourage Chinese initial public offering (IPOs), while national security-based and other measures are likely to prevent or hinder Chinese industrial investments in the US. State-owned enterprises face a particularly high risk, given the HFCA bill’s provision mandating the disclosure of details of CPC affiliation and ownership. If the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) issues new rules mandating more stringent disclosure requirements – as is likely – or if the HFCA bill becomes law, the majority of US-listed Chinese companies are more likely to choose to delist from US exchanges than to comply with the new rules, instead favouring domestic financial centres such as Shanghai, Shenzhen, and Hong Kong SAR in addition to possible listings on other international markets such as London, Singapore, or Tokyo. Beijing has signalled its intent to grow domestic exchanges, with the trend towards greater domestic focus already indicated by local investors welcoming recent sizeable secondary listings and share sales by Alibaba, JD.com, and others in Hong Kong.Indicators of changing risk environmentIncreasing riskUS announcements of sanctions against Chinese firms engaged in the construction of land features in the South China Sea would open further avenues of US regulatory targeting and increase the likelihood of Chinese delisting from US exchanges.Chinese retaliatory responses such as blocking business permits, raiding offices, or stronger enforcement of tax, environmental, or employment regulatory compliance against US companies would further deteriorate bilateral relations. Decreasing risk An election of a Democratic administration in the US November presidential election might delay US targeting of Chinese companies based on national security or human rights justifications, as a new administration and Congress would be prone to act on other domestic priorities first. However, the overwhelming bipartisan Congressional consensus makes the eventual outlook on further financial disclosure requirements unlikely to change, and even if the Congressional focus changes in 2021, the SEC appears likely to tighten its requirements. © 2020, IHS Markit Inc. Headline: UPDATE - Australia: Police continue negotiating with two armed individuals in apartment building in Auchenflower, Brisbane
Details: Local updates have confirmed that police are continuing negotiations with two armed individuals at an apartment building in Auchenflower, Brisbane, on Monday afternoon. No injuries have been reported after a shot was fired in the direction of the police officers. Due to the ongoing operation, Coronation Drive remains closed in both directions between Sylvan Road and Park Road while Dunmore Terrace between Chasely Street and Lang Parade is partially shut. This has resulted in heavy inbound delays from Toowong and also outbound traffic from the city and the Riverside Expressway. In addition, Queensland Traffic Metro has confirmed that the Brisbane Riverwalk is closed to pedestrians and cyclists, while bus services operating in the local area require diversions. Ferry services are suspended between Milton and Toowong. Travellers are advised to bypass the immediate area and expect disruption within the Auchenflower suburb of Brisbane. Follow any commands of the police officers if you encounter their operation.

Headline: DAILY BRIEF: Export disruption, cargo delays, and cruises diversion likely...
Details: Risks: Labour strikesSectors or assets affected: Marine; Cargo; Agriculture; TourismOn 27 November 2018, Chile's Finance Minister Felipe Larrain called on for a swift resolution of a workers' strike at the port of Valparaiso that has been ongoing for 11 days. Workers are demanding higher salaries and better working conditions and have paralysed operations. This has forced at least 14 cargo vessels, and three cruise ships to divert to the nearby port of San Antonio, also in Valparaiso region. This has generated increased congestion in San Antonio, which is receiving an additional 500 cargo trucks a day, while ships have to wait for hours to dock. According to port operators' estimates, at least 20,000 containers have been diverted, and losses account for at least USD3.5 million. In 2013â14, three weeks of nationwide port strikes caused losses of approximately USD300 million. The port sector being crucial for Chile's economy, the government has implemented negotiating tables to deactivate the strike.Significance: The strike is likely to continue for several days, as no advances in the negotiations have been reported, causing ground and maritime cargo delays in San Antonio and Valparaiso. Disruption will increase as public-sector unions are also on indefinite strike over minimum-wage demands, likely delaying customs operations. Fruit exports, which use mainly the ports of San Antonio and Valparaiso, will be specifically affected, as the export season begins next week (early December). The diversion of cruises will also undermine Valparaiso's tourism industry, due to a reduction in tourists coming into the city. There is a risk of solidarity strikes in other ports, as members of the Port Union (Union Portuaria) in Antofagasta and Bio Bio regions have supported the strike (but have not announced any action). Statements by union leaders of other ports that they will join the strike will indicate increased risk of nationwide disruption. The strike continuing for longer than a week will indicate significant losses of fruit to be exported, as it is a perishable product, making exporters miss international trade commitments. Headline: Government instability: Opposition crackdown, expansion of Chinese presence...
Details: On 29 January, the European Union closed the consultation window for member states to offer opinions on the removal of Cambodia from the ""Everything but Arms"" (EBA) preferential trade scheme that permits duty- and quota-free exports of all products except armaments. The European Union is now likely to initiate Cambodia's removal from the scheme. This process would take approximately 12 months and probably substantially affect Cambodia's textiles and clothing industry, which represented 68% of the country's exports in 2016, 46% of which was imported by European countries, according to the latest Word Bank data. These negative developments in Cambodia-EU relations occur in the context of growing Chinese investment and positive ties. Specifically, from 9 to 12 January, three Chinese naval vessels docked at Sihanoukville port, stoking international concerns that Chinese firm Tianjin Union Development Group's USD3.8-billion development project in neighbouring Koh Kong province would create a civilian port that would also be open to Chinese military assets.Unlike following the EU's re-imposition of rice tariffs in January, Cambodia would not be able to replace EU demand with Chinese imports for other sectors that currently benefit from the EBA. The move would nonetheless be supported by Cambodia's political opposition, including exiled leader Sam Rainsy. Importantly, garment workers in Phnom Penh have been supportive of the opposition and would most probably organise strikes, disrupting road transport, if their industry is threatened. An indicator of Prime Minister Hun Sen attempting to mitigate the risks of removal from the EBA to economic growth and political stability would be the announcement of policies facilitating tourism from China or investment in non-garment manufacturing and infrastructure. Despite being unlikely in the six-month outlook, another indicator of increasing distance between Cambodia and the European Union, likely to manifest in preferential regulation for Chinese firms, would be a change to the constitution (which currently bans foreign military bases). If proposed by Hun Sen, this would probably pass and formally facilitate a growing Chinese military presence, specifically naval assets at ports in the Gulf of Thailand.                    Content provided by IHS Markit Foresight © 2019

Headline: Valparaiso terminal workers reject compensation agreement, increasing...
Details: Risks: Labour strikes; Protests and riotsSectors or assets affected: Marine; Cargo; Property; AgricultureOn 19 December, Valparaiso port contractor workers rejected a preliminary agreement mediated by the government to call off a 34-day strike over working conditions and bonuses. The agreement offered them soft loans and other benefits totalling CLP1.37 million (USD1,980), lower than the CLP2 million bonus workers demanded. Confrontations between demonstrators and the police at the port neighbourhood, Colon Avenue, and the city centre, involved protesters erecting barricades using burning tyres, and throwing sticks, stones, and Molotov cocktails at the police, who responded using tear gas and water cannons. Some demonstrators broke windows of nearby property and stores, and looted the offices of maritime company Ultraport. At the union headquarters, approximately 25 individuals threw blunt objects and Molotov cocktails from the roof, which led to the police breaking into the premises and arresting 16 people. Valparaiso's union is calling workers at other ports to join the strike. According to the company Empresa Portuaria de Valparaiso (EPV), over USD4.9 million in losses have been incurred as a result of this dispute.Significance: There is a high risk of nationwide strike action Chilean ports, with unions at other ports joining in. Port workers at 10 other terminals throughout the country (Bio Bio, Caldera, Coronel, Iquique, Lirquen, Penco, San Antonio, San Vicente, Talcahuano, and Ventanas) have already carried out partial stoppages in solidarity, mainly during the night shifts, indicating growing likelihood of escalation. Broadening strike action at Chile's ports would cause severe export disruptions and delays to maritime cargo. In 2013â14, three-weeks' long strikes across Chilean ports caused losses totalling approximately USD300 million. The agriculture sector would be particularly affected, as this is the middle of their export season. Fruit exports in December have already declined by 95% compared to the same period in 2017, according to media reports. Should the government present a bill improving compensation and working conditions for contractor workers, this would indicate improved likelihood of resolution and declining labour strike risk at Chilean ports. Headline: US Consulate Issued Weather Alert for Cyclone Forecast to Hit Tamil Nadu, Kerala Starting Wednesday
Details:
On Tuesday, the US Consulate General in Chennai issued the following Weather Alert:



“Location:   South Tamil Nadu coast



Event:   A well-marked low-pressure area in the southeast Bay of Bengal and adjoining areas of the South Andaman Sea and Equatorial Indian Ocean is expected to develop into a cyclonic storm approaching south Tamil Nadu and south Kerala by December 2, 2020.  According to official local weather sources, such as the Regional Specialized Meteorological Centre for Tropical Cyclones Over North Indian Ocean (http://www.rsmcnewdelhi.imd.gov.in/index.php?lang=en), heavy rains may begin as early as December 1, 2020. Heavy to extremely heavy rains are expected between Thanjavur and Kanyakumari, in the State of Tamil Nadu, from December 1 through December 3, 2020.  Other regions across southern India can expect heavy rainfall and possible flooding as a result of this storm. Internet service, landline phone, and cell phone capabilities may be affected.   



Consulate Operations:  The U.S. Consulate General Chennai is currently scheduled to operate as normal.   



Actions to Take: 



Monitor local media for weather updates. 



Seek secure shelter. 



Have evacuation plans that do not rely on U.S. government assistance. 



Notify friends and family of your safety.”

Hurricane Florence is currently approximately 900 miles from the Wilmington area and is moving west-northwest at 16 miles per hour. The storm has maximum sustained winds of 130 miles per hour. Headline: Hong Kong - Medical workers have ended their five-day strike. Incident closed.
Details: Media sources reported that medical staff have ended their five-day strike across Hong Kong that began on Monday, February 3. The strike was called to pressure city officials to completely close the territory's border with mainland China over fears that the Novel coronavirus (2019-nCoV) will continue to spread in Hong Kong. Workers also demanded protective equipment, sufficient isolation wards, surgical masks, and assurance that staff will not be penalized for taking part in the labor action. Approximately 2,700 people participated during the first day of the strike and around 7,000 participated on the second day of the strike. Reports indicate that hundreds of people gathered at the Hospital Authority headquarters. On Monday, February 3, a number of surgeries had to be postponed. There were no details regarding whether further labor action will be carried out as the outbreak continues. This incident is closed.

Headline: Authorities Warn that ELN Could be Planning New Offensive in Northern and Eastern Departments
Details:
On October 7th, National Liberation Army (ELN) insurgents killed two police officers in a grenade attack in a rural locality in the northern department of Cesar. Two days later, Colombian authorities announced that they had obtained intelligence indicating that the rebel group was planning to launch a new offensive in the country s northern and eastern departments. While few details have been publicly divulged, the purported offensive has been likened to   Plan Pistola ,  a campaign of targeted police killings that a separate paramilitary group carried out last year. Police officers have been placed on high alert, and elements of the Colombian Army have been deployed to rural police stations, which are considered the most likely targets. Resilience360 advises travelers in Colombia to take security precautions and practice strong situational awareness, especially when in the vicinity of police stations. Any suspicious activity or items should be reported to local authorities. 

 
	 Recent Developments  
	 
	On Sunday, October 7th, two police officers were fatally ambushed on a road that links the municipalities of San Alberto and La Mata, in the northern department of Cesar. The two officers had been tasked with conducting routine inspections of public transportation vehicles, and were riding on a single motorcycle at the time of the attack. Unidentified assailants threw a hand grenade at the vehicle, and then opened fire on the wounded officers with rifles before fleeing the scene. Both officers succumbed to their injuries. Authorities subsequently attributed the attack to the ELN. The following day, President Iv n Duque held a press conference and stated that Bogot  would not resume peace talks with the ELN should the group continue to carry out similar attacks. 
	 
	On Tuesday, October 9th, Colombian authorities announced that they had obtained intelligence indicating that the ELN was planning to launch a new offensive in the country s northern and eastern departments. Colonel Iv n Calixto, commander of the Magdalena Medio Police in the northwestern department of Antioquia, told reporters that the plot had been discovered through telephone intercepts. Authorities have likened the scheme to   Plan Pistola ,  an offensive carried out by the Clan del Golfo paramilitary group in mid-2017, which entailed a wave of attacks against police officers across the country. Although few additional details have been made public at this time, Colonel Calixto stated that security measures were being bolstered throughout the region, and that authorities were particularly concerned about the southern portion of Bol var Department, which borders Antioquia to the northeast. The Colombian Army announced that it would provide additional support to police stations in rural areas, which are considered to be the most likely targets. 
	 
	 Background  
	 
	The most recent round of peace talks between Bogot  and the ELN concluded on August 1st, without any major progress. Since President Duque took office on August 7th, his administration has maintained a much more hard-line stance than his predecessor. Duque has repeatedly stated that negotiations will only be resumed if the ELN releases all of its captives, ceases all criminal activity, and declares a unilateral ceasefire. While the insurgents have thus far failed to comply with these preconditions, the ELN made one concession in early September by releasing three police officers, one soldier, and two civilian contractors that the group had kidnapped the previous month. Nevertheless, the ELN continues to hold multiple captives. On October 10th, the rebels released a proof-of-life video of an engineer that they abducted from a rural locality in the northeastern department of Arauca in March of this year. Historically, the ELN has engaged in kidnapping both to raise funds through ransom payments, and to utilize abductees as bargaining chips. 
	 
	As mentioned above, the   Plan Pistola   offensive was an assassination campaign that was carried out last year by the Clan del Golfo, a right-wing paramilitary group and staunch adversary of the ELN. It entailed a wave of small-scale attacks across ten departments, which killed at least 11 police officers and injured over 30 more. Officers were targeted at police stations, security checkpoints, and while conducting routine patrols. Furthermore, some officers were targeted while off duty, during their commutes or at locations such as barbershops. Attacks were carried out with small arms, grenades, and improvised explosive devices (IEDs). While most incidents occurred in small towns and rural localities, some attacks transpired in larger cities such as Cartagena, and several plots were foiled in Bogot  and Medell n.  
	 Assessment  
	 
	Due to the scant details that have been made public so far, it currently remains unclear to what extent the ELN s purported offensive might resemble   Plan Pistola .  As news of the ELN s intentions has been made public, and Colombian security forces have already begun to take preventive measures, it is possible that the guerillas could opt to delay, modify, or even abort the plan. Any renewed ELN offensive could also potentially entail an uptick in attacks against fuel pipelines and other energy infrastructure. The guerillas have historically favored this tactic, as such attacks have proven to be a low-risk and low-cost means of both generating publicity and inflicting financial losses. 
	 
	There are currently no signs to suggest that the diplomatic impasse between Bogot  and the ELN will be overcome in the near future. Any large-scale offensive by the ELN would likely prompt a strong military response. Some local commentators have suggested that such a development might cause the Duque administration to fully abandon the pursuit of a negotiated settlement with the rebels. 
	 
	Resilience360 advises customers with interests in Colombia, especially in Bol var and other departments across the northern and eastern portions of the country, to stay abreast of ongoing developments. The ELN has not historically engaged in indiscriminate attacks against civilian targets of opportunity. Nevertheless, attacks directed against security forces have resulted in injuries and deaths of civilian bystanders, and the group continues to occasionally target civilians in kidnappings. 
	 
	Due to the high level of risk posed by insurgent activity and violent crime, Resilience360 advises customers to avoid all travel to the departments of Arauca, Norte de Santander, Cauca, Choc , and Nari o. Travelers visiting other parts of the country are advised to take heightened security precautions, especially in rural areas where police coverage may be severely deficient. While the level of risk posed by the ELN will likely be the greatest in rural areas, the possibility of an attack in one of the nation s large cities cannot be ruled out entirely. The ELN demonstrated its continued ability to strike in urban areas when it detonated an IED in downtown Bogot  in February of 2017. Travelers are advised to maintain a heightened sense of situational awareness when in the vicinity of police stations, security checkpoints, or military installations. Any atypical behavior or suspicious vehicles, packages, or objects should be promptly reported to local authorities.

Headline: 90 miles E of Nanning - Mangkhut now a depression, to dissipate in next 15 hours. Incident closed.
Details:
Mangkhut has weakened to a tropical depression and is expected to dissipate within the next 15 hours. The storm recently made landfall in Guangdong Province after previously affecting the Philippines.

Residents in low-lying areas of Macau and Hong Kong were advised to evacuate to temporary shelters, while flooding was reported in many coastal areas in Hong Kong, with associated structural damage. Cleanup operations are underway on Monday, and some operations are returning to normal. The most impacted areas of Hong Kong included Tsim Sha Tsui, Ha Fa Cheun, Sai Kung, and Chai Wan. The Ting Kau Bridge was closed and a crane collapsed in the Tai Kok Tsui area. Flooding was also reported in the inner harbor area of Macau. Reports indicate that at least 300 people were injured in Hong Kong, at least 15 people were injured in Macau, and at at least two people were killed in Guangdong. The Hong Kong Observatory issued a Number 10 Southeast Gale or Storm Signal.

State media reports that over 2.45 million people were evacuated in Guangdong. Flight disruptions were reported at Hong Kong Airport (HKG) and Macau International Airport (MFM), and some disruptions persist into Monday. Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport (CAN) temporarily canceled all flights. Rail services in Guangdong and Guangxi provinces, already disrupted for the passage of Tropical Storm Barijat, were expected to remain out of operation until at least until Monday. In addition, ferry services and MTR bus and rail services in Hong Kong were temporarily disrupted until further notice.

In the Philippines, the typhoon caused flooding across multiple parts of Luzon. More than 151,000 residents were evacuated. At least 59 people were killed in storm-related incidents, including landslides. Tuguegarao Airport (TUG) suffered significant damage, and was forced to close.

Residual disruptions are possible as the storm weakens. This incident is closed.

Headline: Reports of COVID-19 Outbreak Inside US Embassy Reflect Kingdom’s Trouble Containing Virus
Details:
On Wednesday, the New York Times, citing accounts from nine current and one former US official, reported that the American Embassy in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, has experienced an outbreak of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). According to the report, an estimated 50 embassy employees, mostly foreigners, either tested positive for or are believed to have contracted COVID-19. One of them, reportedly a Sudanese driver, died, while 32 others have recovered. The condition of the remaining 17 was not clear. The outbreak reportedly happened last month and purportedly stemmed from a birthday barbecue; more than 20 embassy staffers were quarantined soon after the gathering. On June 27, the US Embassy in Riyadh issued a Security Alert informing citizens that the Department of State (DoS) has authorized the voluntary departure of non-emergency American personnel and family members from Washington’s diplomatic missions in Saudi Arabia due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The measure is said to leave the bulk of embassy staff in place, though officials can still take further action and issue an “ordered departure,” which would require most employees to evacuate, mirroring similar steps taken by the United States embassies in Lebanon and Iraq earlier in the pandemic. As of Thursday, Saudi Arabia had recorded 197,608 confirmed COVID-19 infections and 1,752 deaths attributed to the virus.



Assessment: If confirmed, the development would highlight the difficulty that Riyadh and many of its regional counterparts have had in controlling the spread of COVID-19. Indeed, daily incidence remains high in Saudi Arabia, with the Kingdom reporting some 4,000 new coronavirus cases every day, while the Gulf region in general remains a global hotspot for COVID-19, with Bahrain (#1), Qatar (#2), Oman (#4), Kuwait (#6), and Saudi Arabia (#9) representing five of the top nine countries in the world in terms of per capita incidence as of July 1. Yet, the Saudi government has relaxed most coronavirus restrictions and allowed all economic and commercial activities to resume, a decision that embassy employees in Riyadh have predicted will lead to a spike in cases throughout July. Given signs that Saudi Arabia may already be nearing its capacity to treat coronavirus patients, including a recent statement from the US Embassy that it has received reports of American citizens having difficulty accessing care in the Kingdom, a large influx of new cases could overwhelm the country’s healthcare system, leading to a shortage of hospital beds and likely greater exposure and deaths. The public is advised to stay apprised of associated health developments in this regard, practice good hygiene measures, and heed all official guidance and directives.

Headline: UPDATE 1 - Baloch separatist attack on state exploration company convoy underlines growing threat to commercial transport in southern Pakistan
Details: The Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) – one of several separatist groups operating in Pakistan’s southwestern province of Balochistan – on 20 October claimed that its fighters had killed 61 Pakistani soldiers in 20 attacks from July–August 2020. The BLF is part of an umbrella group of separatists – the Baloch National Freedom Movement (Baloch Raji Ajohi Sangar: BRAS) – which claimed the 15 October attack against a convoy of the state-run Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL) employees traveling to Karachi from Gwadar. At least seven soldiers and seven private security guards were confirmed as having been killed in the ambush. Significance: Although the BLF’s claims are likely exaggerated, they reflect a broad increase in the frequency and sophistication of Baloch separatist activity, which has likely been driven by growing co-ordination between the disparate separatist groups through BRAS and with counterpart Sindhi separatist groups (see Pakistan: 14 August 2020: Co-ordination between Pakistani ethno-nationalist separatist groups likely to increase terrorism threat for Chinese expatriates in Sindh). The OGDCL convoy attack, moreover, underlines that Pakistani state and Chinese commercial activity are primary targets for Baloch separatists, second only to security forces. However, Baloch separatists have had limited success in causing damage to fixed assets with recent high-profile attacks, such as the June 2020 assault against the Pakistan Stock Exchange in Karachi, in which meaningful damage to buildings was minimal. We therefore anticipate that separatist attacks will predominantly target assets and individuals in transit over the next year, rather than project sites or secured locations. Government and military-run commercial companies such as OGDCL and the Frontier Works Organization, and all Chinese companies, face a particularly high risk of being targeted in ambushes by militants using small-arms and rocket-propelled grenades (RPGs) or roadside improvised explosive device (IED) attacks, particularly along the Makran Coastal Highway connecting Balochistan and Sindh provinces. Headline_Details: UPDATE 1 - Baloch separatist attack on state exploration company convoy underlines growing threat to commercial transport in southern Pakistan The Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) – one of several separatist groups operating in Pakistan’s southwestern province of Balochistan – on 20 October claimed that its fighters had killed 61 Pakistani soldiers in 20 attacks from July–August 2020. The BLF is part of an umbrella group of separatists – the Baloch National Freedom Movement (Baloch Raji Ajohi Sangar: BRAS) – which claimed the 15 October attack against a convoy of the state-run Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL) employees traveling to Karachi from Gwadar. At least seven soldiers and seven private security guards were confirmed as having been killed in the ambush. Significance: Although the BLF’s claims are likely exaggerated, they reflect a broad increase in the frequency and sophistication of Baloch separatist activity, which has likely been driven by growing co-ordination between the disparate separatist groups through BRAS and with counterpart Sindhi separatist groups (see Pakistan: 14 August 2020: Co-ordination between Pakistani ethno-nationalist separatist groups likely to increase terrorism threat for Chinese expatriates in Sindh). The OGDCL convoy attack, moreover, underlines that Pakistani state and Chinese commercial activity are primary targets for Baloch separatists, second only to security forces. However, Baloch separatists have had limited success in causing damage to fixed assets with recent high-profile attacks, such as the June 2020 assault against the Pakistan Stock Exchange in Karachi, in which meaningful damage to buildings was minimal. We therefore anticipate that separatist attacks will predominantly target assets and individuals in transit over the next year, rather than project sites or secured locations. Government and military-run commercial companies such as OGDCL and the Frontier Works Organization, and all Chinese companies, face a particularly high risk of being targeted in ambushes by militants using small-arms and rocket-propelled grenades (RPGs) or roadside improvised explosive device (IED) attacks, particularly along the Makran Coastal Highway connecting Balochistan and Sindh provinces. Headline: UPDATE 17 - India imposes additional checks on imports from ASEAN to avoid rerouting Chinese goods
Details: Updated industry sources indicate on August 6 that New Delhi is considering measures to prevent trade partners in Southeast Asia from re-routing Chinese goods to India with little added value amid the continued tensions with its neighboring country. According to sources, the Indian customs will implement more frequent checks at ports of entry for goods coming from many Asian countries. Items include base metals, electronic components for laptops and mobile phones, furniture, leather goods, toys, rubber, textiles, air conditioners and televisions. India’s trade ministry had also issued a notice to restrict inbound shipments of televisions by requiring importers to get a special license in order to restrict Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam and Singapore with which India has a free trade agreement. India is also worried about heavy trade flows from South Korea. India has been conducting 100 percent physical examination and assessment for imports from China, Hong Kong, and Macau after bilateral tensions increased in recent months. This has disrupted the flow of regular inbound shipments and caused congestion at express terminals and impacting the processing of all shipments.

Headline: DAILY BRIEF: Forestry contractors in Chile's Araucania region are...
Details: Risks: TerrorismSectors or assets affected: Forestry; Agriculture; Cargo; Property; ElectricityOn Friday (26 April), regional business lobby Multigremial de la Araucania released a report revealing that Mapuche indigenous-related incidents increased by 503% in JanuaryâMarch 2019 in Chile's southern Araucania region, compared with the same period in 2018 (136 reported cases versus 27). In the neighbouring Bio-bio, Los Rios, and Los Lagos regions, also hotspots of rural violence over Mapuches' land restitution claims, the number of cases moved from 6 to 11, 4 to 2, and 3 to zero, respectively. According to the report, most cases in Araucania were arson attacks (36), followed by land occupations (32). On 22 April, the extremist group Coordinadora Arauco Malleco (CAM) claimed responsibility for setting alight six machines and attempting to burn another eight at the premises of the Agroforestal Pumalal firm on the border between Temuco and Lautaro. It was the first major attack since authorities lifted a two-month state of exception in the area on 6 April that had been declared to prevent the expansion of forest fires. Significance: The risk of arson attacks against forestry and agricultural assets in Araucania and neighbouring regions will remain high over the coming months. Hotspots in Araucania are Victoria, Ercilla, Collipulli, and, to a lesser extent, Lumaco, Temuco, and Angol. The hotspots in Bio-bio are Canete, Tirua, and Contulmo. Traditional targets are warehouses, machinery and vehicles belonging to forestry and agricultural firms, as well as cargo in transit, mainly on Route 5 and rural roads. Forestry contractors are increasingly targets, having already lost 408 machines, a total of USD70 million since January 2014, according to sources in the sector. Additionally, several companies have been forced to downsize or close. Electricity towers have also been occasional targets since 2016. An indicator of the government advancing its security strategy will be the passing of a short version of its proposed anti-terrorism law, as announced on 22 April, focused on increasing prerogatives of intelligence services. An indicator of reduced attacks will be if the government declares a state of exception in the region until the end of the year, as demanded by the private sector; however, this is unlikely. Headline: Security Forces Stage Early Morning Raid at ELN Safe House in Cartagena; Explosives Seized
Details:
In the early hours of Thursday, security forces carried out a raid at a private residence in the port city of Cartagena, located in the northern department of Bol var. Authorities stated that the dwelling, situated in the southeastern district of Nelson Mandela, was being utilized as a safe house by an urban cell of the National Liberation Army (ELN). One suspect was taken into custody. There were no reports of shots fired. Security forces seized three firearms and 16  packets  of explosives. At this time, no further details regarding the type or quantity of the explosives have been divulged to the public. 
	 
	Assessment: Although the vast majority of ELN attacks take place in Colombia s rural municipalities, the group has demonstrated its continued ability to strike within cities as well. In early 2017, ELN insurgents detonated a bomb in downtown Bogot  that wounded 23 police officers and two civilians, and claimed the life of one policeman. The ELN has historically eschewed mass casualty attacks against civilian targets of opportunity, and generally directs attacks against security forces. Nevertheless, innocent bystanders have been injured and killed during such incidents on multiple occasions in the past. At this time, local authorities have not suggested that the seizure of the explosives signifies any broader increase in the overall level of risk across Cartagena. Nevertheless, the potential for an attack cannot be ruled out entirely. Resilience360 advises travelers in Cartagena to practice strong situational awareness, especially when in the vicinity of police stations, security checkpoints, or military installations. Any atypical behavior or suspicious vehicles, packages, or objects should be promptly reported to local authorities.

Headline: Upper Texas Coast   Recovery efforts are underway in the region; impacts remain. Incident closed.
Details:
While flood waters continue to recede across the eastern coast of Texas, relief and recovery efforts are underway in the region. As a result of flooding caused by the passing of storm Imelda, a total of five people were killed. On Friday, September 20, two bodies were discovered in the Beaumont area, and one was discovered in Houston. There are reports that flood waters have begun to recede in the area, and although rain is in the forecast for the weekend September 28, favorable weather is also predicted. Officials are continuing to survey flooded areas with regard to search and rescue efforts. Governor Greg Abbott declared a state of disaster in 13 counties in response to the severe flooding. The proclamation was for the following counties: Brazoria, Chambers, Galveston, Hardin, Harris, Jasper, Jefferson, Liberty, Matagorda, Montgomery, Newton, Orange, and San Jacinto. There are no immediate reports regarding the current status for each individual county.

The most substantial flooding was reported in Chambers County, specifically in Winnie. In Harris County, the most significant was in Houston, and in Jefferson County, the largest reported flooding was in Beaumont. As of September 25, the only counties under active flood warnings are Jasper, Jefferson and Hardin. Evacuations were issued for residents in Hardin and Jefferson counties. Several other counties were under shelter-in-place orders during the storm and subsequent flooding.

At least ten more inches of rain fell on September 19, with some areas receiving over 15 inches in total. Over three days of rain, the area received at least 50 inches in some locations. A number of chemical and refinery facilities were shut down in the area, including the TC Energy pipeline. The pipeline, which extends from Cushing, Oklahoma to Nederland, Texas, was restarted on Friday, September, 20. Several roadways in the area were deemed impassable due to high water, which may still be present in certain parts.

The following areas were impacted the most by the storm: 

- Chambers County: In Winnie, at least 200 homes were inundated with water and an entire hospital was evacuated. Initial estimates indicated some 800 homes were damaged in the entire county and approximately 400 people were rescued. Although it was closed during the storm, a stretch of I-10 between Beaumont and Winne has since been reopened. There are, however, reports of water on the freeway and only one lane is open.

- Harris County: In Houston, over 1,700 people were rescued, 323 vehicles were reported stranded, and a building collapsed leading to the injury of three people. In Spring, over 100 people were rescued and at least 60 people were rescued in Huffman. Hundreds of homes were inundated in the Humble and Kingwood areas.

- Jefferson County: The County received roughly 40 inches of rain over a 72-hour period. The Green Pond Gulley Levee was at risk of collapse due to deteriorating conditions exacerbated by rainfall. As a result, county officials ordered multiple evacuations as a precaution. The levee is currently in a stable condition. In Beaumont, over 250 high water rescues were performed.

- Galveston County: All Island Transit services were suspended, including fixed routes, Dial-A-Ride, and rubber wheel trolleys. 
As the post-storm process continues, authorities have stated that around 7,000 national flood insurance claims have been made. Expect residual disruptions as water, debris and other associated impacts continue to affect the region. This incident is closed.

Headline: Recovery Under Way Following Weekend Storm Packing Strong Winds and Rain
Details:
Extensive damage was reported following a storm with heavy winds that swept over Malta during the weekend. Coastal areas and the northeast of the country were among the hardest-hit locations, though no injuries were initially reported. During the severe weather, authorities evacuated 14 people from Sliema and a dozen from Vittoriosa. The storm brought strong waves that damaged or destroyed many stone walls and waterfront businesses have been working to clean up debris and make any needed repairs. Damage to an undersea water main between Malta and Gozo will be repaired as seas calm, with the supply reportedly unaffected. Boats were also damaged during the storm, which packed hurricane-strength gusts in excess of 80 miles per hour while bringing nearly two inches of rain, more than half of the country s rainfall so far this month. Roadways had been partially or fully blocked in many locations due to downed trees. 
 
	Assessment: The exceptional storm was driven by two contrasting pressure systems in the region converging and driving strong winds in the highly varied barometric occurrence. Prime Minister Joseph Muscat said the storm was the worst since October 1982. The government is assessing storm damage and may seek financial assistance from the European Union, Muscat noted. Although there was not extensive damage to critical infrastructure, damage such as toppled power lines and weakened walls highlighted the need for upgrading aging infrastructure. Winds are expected to pick up again on Wednesday and Saturday, though not nearing the level of intensity as occurred last weekend. Resilience360 customers are advised to remain aware of potentially weakened structures and vegetation as storm damage assessments continue, to exercise caution in the event of further inclement conditions, and to heed the guidance of local authorities in an emergency.

Headline: New measures implemented at Port of Salalah amid COVID-19 outbreak
Details:
Media sources reported that additional measures are implemented on March 18 at the Port of Salalah. 
- All ships and their agents are obliged to submit the IMO Declaration of Health to the Harbour Master as well as the attached ‘Coronavirus questionnaire’.
- Both documents should be signed and stamped by the Captain. Both documents need to be uploaded in the Port management system by the ship’s agent for approval of the vessel called by the Harbour Master.
- In case of a sick person on board, the vessel will not be allowed to enter the port and the patient involved will be screened by a Port Health team at anchorage.
- In case of recently arrived crew on board the ship (within the last 16 days), the Harbour Master will decide, based upon the submitted facts, whether pilot boarding and port entry are allowed.
- No disembarkation of ship’s crew is allowed during the ship’s call, including the anchorage.
- In case of needed emergency shore leave or crew change, pre-approval is needed from the Harbour Master, Immigration and Port Health. For Harbour Master approval, this request must be sent to the Port Control email address as mentioned hereunder. Approval is given by email.
- Any concerned staff interacting with the ship’s crew should follow up on the official advice from the Ministry of Health and the World Health Organization on personal protection.
- Port Control should be contacted in case of any suspicious situation regarding the Coronavirus in the port area or onboard a ship so that appropriate measures can be taken in close cooperation with the Port Health team.

Headline: Hong Kong District Council Elections Likely to Take Place on 11/24; Risk of Unrest Remains
Details:
On Thursday, it was reported that Chinese Vice-Premier Han Zheng, who leads Beijing s top task force on affairs relating to Hong Kong, said that the central government wanted the upcoming district council elections for Sunday, November 24, to take place as scheduled. The statements were made during a meeting in Shenzhen on November 15. Nearly all 31,000 police officers in Hong Kong will be deployed for the election and armed officers will be guarding all of the 600 polling stations. Voting will begin at 7:30 AM and polls will close at 10:30 PM, with the counting of ballots taking place immediately after.

Assessment: The situation in Hong Kong has been relatively calm since Wednesday, particularly compared to recent weeks, although there have still been minor transportation disruptions and scuffles during lunchtime protests. Police also continue to stand off with a small group of protesters at Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU), although there have not been any recent clashes or attempts to storm the campus. The relative calm may be in response to threats that the district council polls could be delayed if there was still mass unrest. So far, there have not been any calls for demonstrations to take place on Sunday, although the decentralized nature of the protest movement ensures a persistent risk of unrest. Some protesters have called on others to hold off on any actions that could jeopardize the polls, while others have emphasized the need to not be arrested due to the risk that they would not be able to vote. Protesters are in favor of the polls being held, as it gives them an opportunity to demonstrate what they feel is popular support among local residents. In the unlikely event that Sunday s polls are delayed or canceled, there is a high chance of mass unrest. An unfavorable outcome for protesters or allegations of election fraud could also result in protests. Customers are advised to expect a heightened security presence and continue to avoid all areas where demonstrations are taking place due to the high risk of violence and exercise caution around polling stations on Sunday. A heightened level of situational awareness should be exercised at all times, as protests could take place spontaneously in multiple areas.

Headline: UPDATE 2 - Australia’s proposed legislation on agreements between states/territories and foreign governments indicates increased likelihood of state contract cancellation
Details: The Australian Foreign Relations (State and Territory Arrangements) Act 2020 was introduced to parliament on 3 September, which would empower the federal government to cancel any “written arrangement, agreement, contract, understanding or undertaking” between Australian states and territories and foreign governments if these are assessed as being inconsistent with Australian foreign policy. Prime Minister Scott Morrison announced the legislation on 27 August, stating that the bill would ensure governments at the sub-national level remain consistent with the national interest. Australian Foreign Minister and Senator Marise Payne during the opening of Senate business on 14 May 2020 in Canberra, Australia.Sam Mooy/Getty ImagesTheForeign Relations Bill would apply to all foreign arrangements regardless of whether they are already in operation, indicating that the law would be retroactive. The proposed law does not cover commercial entities such as foreign state-owned companies but is directed at government entities including national and subnational governments, departments, agencies and universities. The bill includes the establishment of a public register where state/territory entities would be required to disclose all existing foreign arrangements to the federal government ahead of a review by the foreign minister. If the foreign minister considers that an arrangement is inconsistent with Australia’s foreign policy, then he or she would have the power to terminate it. Arrangements likely to be terminated under the new law include a 2019 trade deal between the Victorian and Chinese governments that gives Victoria access to funding under China’s Belt and Road Initiative. Sub-national government entities would have to notify the federal government of any prospective foreign arrangements, with “core” foreign arrangements – which include arrangements with foreign countries, their national governments, and related departments and agencies – requiring approval from the foreign minister in order to commence negotiations or enter the arrangement.Although the proposed legislation is not explicitly directed at a particular foreign government, arrangements involving Chinese government entities are most likely to be terminated. Concerns about Chinese influence in Australian politics and strategic assets has increased in recent years (see Australia: 25 January 2018: Australian political interference laws likely to heighten scrutiny of foreign entities with Australian subsidiaries within three months), and in June the Australian government proposed new rules tightening government scrutiny over foreign investments on national security grounds that also appeared to target China (see Australia: 8 June 2020: Proposed changes to Australia’s foreign investment rules likely to target Chinese investors, increasing risk of forced divestments). Relations between Australia and China have also deteriorated significantly since April, when the Australian government called for an independent inquiry into the origins of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), which prompted a strong rebuttal from China. Subsequently, China simultaneously imposed tariffs of 80% on Australian barley as part of an anti-dumping investigation and suspended imports of Australian beef due to regulatory issues in May (see Australia, China: 15 May 2020: Australia unlikely to retaliate against Chinese suspension of beef imports, decreasing the likelihood of extended measures). In August the Chinese government launched an anti-dumping investigation into Australian wine imports. IHS Markit assesses that the proposed bill is highly likely to pass in parliament given strong bipartisan support for a more cautious approach towards China. The opposition Labor Party has signalled that it would support the legislation but said it should be “workable”, indicating that it will probably seek amendments to the clause covering universities. In particular, Labor is likely to scrutinise the impact on science and research. Nevertheless, the bill is likely to pass largely in its current form. The Labor Party at the federal level has grown increasingly wary of arrangements with China; the party has shifted from being “open-minded” about China’s Belt and Road Initiative in 2017 to opposing it. Although the bill does not currently cover arrangements with foreign state-owned companies, on 30 August Labor leader Anthony Albanese said that the 2015 sale of the port of Darwin to a company linked to the Chinese government, which Labor has strongly criticised, should be part of the discussion around the foreign relations bill. A legislation committee inquiry report is due by 5 November 2020 and the proposal will probably be legislated by January 2021.Indicators of changing risk environmentIncreasing riskThe Australian government using the Foreign Relations Bill to retroactively terminate subnational-foreign arrangements would indicate further deterioration of the two countries’ bilateral relationship. This would encourage Chinese retaliatory measures, potentially including further trade restrictions and the targeting of Australian nationals in China.If the bill is expanded to include commercial arrangements between an Australian state/ territory entity and state-owned foreign companies, then this would increase state contract alteration risks for commercial contracts in Australia.Decreasing riskAlthough unlikely, amendments to the proposed Foreign Relations Bill to reduce the extent of its retroactive clauses would mitigate state contract alteration risks and reduce the likelihood of a further deterioration in relations between the federal government and China. © 2020, IHS Markit Inc. Headline: Hurricane Isaias to Impact Florida Coast this Weekend Before Moving up the Eastern Seaboard
Details:
Hurricane Isaias is continuing to strengthen as it moves through the Bahamas towards the east Florida coast. The storm is currently a Category 1 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson wind scale, with winds of at least 75 miles per hour. Strengthening is expected beginning Friday night and the storm may increase to a Category 2 hurricane. The current forecast shows Isaias skirting the east coast of Florida beginning Saturday night before moving up the East Coast. Landfall is currently forecast sometime on Monday near the South Carolina-North Carolina border. Isaias will then weaken into a tropical storm and is expected to continue moving up the coast, potentially impacting the Northeast coast. Some uncertainty in the track of the storm remains and its possible the storm makes landfall along the upper east coast of Florida late Sunday in addition to the expected landfall in the Carolinas. The National Hurricane Center (NHC) has issued a hurricane warning for portions of the central and southern Atlantic Florida coasts. A state of emergency has been issued for the entire eastern Florida coast as well as for the states of North Carolina and Virginia. 



Assessment: As of this writing, the only evacuations issued are on Ocracoke Island in North Carolina. Evacuations remain a possibility for the coast of Florida as the storm continues to move closer to land and the hurricane track evolves. Airport closures and flight delays also remain a possibility both along the eastern coast of Florida, as well as up the rest of the East Coast as the storm moves up the coastline. Portions of Florida and the Carolinas are forecast to see upwards of five inches of rain and flash flooding is possible along the entire east coast of the United States. Similarly, port closures remain a possibility but as of this writing, none have been issued. Several ports in Florida, South Carolina, North Carolina, and Virginia have been set to Port Condition Whiskey. This means that ports remain open to all commercial and cargo operations but commercial vessels greater than 500 gross tons should begin making plans to depart the port. The strong winds from Isaias are likely to cause widespread power outages across the eastern seaboard. Some outages may be prolonged for multiple days depending on other impacts caused by the storm. Those with interests along the U.S. East Coast are advised to continue monitoring the situation closely. The public should use extreme caution in storm conditions and heed all weather warnings and instructions from local authorities.

Headline: More Than 1,800 Tons of Hazardous Materials Illegally Dumped at Port of Tanjung Pelepas in Johor
Details:
On Sunday, Malaysian environmental authorities announced that 1,864 tons of electric arc furnace dust (EAFD) was recovered after being illegally dumped at the Port of Tanjung Pelepas in the state of Johor, just west of Singapore. EAFD is a hazardous material that is created during steel production, and contains such compounds as cadmium, chromium, iron, lead, and zinc. The material, held in 110 containers, had arrived from Romania and was reportedly bound for Indonesia. It had been falsely labeled as concentrated zinc in customs forms. 



Assessment: Authorities had discovered the material on June 3, and it is the biggest find of its kind in Malaysian history. Officials are making preparations to facilitate the return of the material to Romania and are requesting an INTERPOL (International Criminal Police Organization) investigation. Malaysia has stopped at least 28 instances of attempted illegal waste importation so far in 2020. Attempts at illegally shipping certain hazardous wastes are likely to increase as additional countries continue to ban imports or add further restrictions to waste that is accepted. While officials gave no indication that any of the EAFD discovered last month leaked into the surrounding environment, there is the potential for illegally dumped materials to have negative health or environmental consequences.

Headline: Police seize EUR 500 million of cocaine from container at the Port of Genoa
Details: International media sources indicated that on January 31, Italian police seized 2 metric tons of cocaine (worth EUR 500 million, USD 568 million) that were discovered in 60 bags hidden within a container at the Port of Genoa. The container departed from Colombia the week before and was destined for Barcelona after transiting through Genoa. Italian police swapped the cocaine with salt and a GPS tracker before the container continued to Barcelona, allowing Spanish police to arrest the final recipient. The seizure occurred with the cooperation of Colombian and Spanish police and and was the largest drug seizure in Italy in 25 years. Police have commented that the Port of Genoa is suspected to be increasingly utilized for illegal drug trafficking into Europe.
