Headline: Flood-Related Disruptions, Warnings to Linger Despite Improving Weather, Death Toll at Seven
Details:
Flood warnings remained in effect across North Carolina on Friday after a weather system tied to Tropical Storm Eta brought more than nine inches of rainfall to parts of the state on November 11-12. The National Weather Service extended a flash flood warning for the central counties of Alamance, Chatham, Durham, Johnston, Orange, and Wake until 3:45 PM local time on November 13, while local authorities have advised that several rivers, including the Cape Fear, Haw, Neuse, and Tar, will crest between flood stage and major flood stage over the weekend. In addition to rising water levels, multiple stretches of highway and surface streets remain closed or impassable due to flooding. Affected highways of note include Interstate 95, with the northbound lanes closed near mile marker 102 in Johnston County, about 30 miles southeast of Raleigh, until at least 5:00 PM local time on Friday. Another part of I-95 was closed near Wilson but has since reopened, as have parts of Interstate 85 near Charlotte. To view up-to-date road conditions, one can consult the following webpage maintained by the North Carolina Department of Transportation: https://www.drivenc.gov/#incidents.



Five counties declared states of emergency on Thursday due to the deluge: Alexander, Burke, Catawba, Iredell, and Yadkin. Among the areas hardest hit was Alexander County, about 65 miles northwest of Charlotte, where three people died and 31 others were rescued when floodwaters from a nearby river inundated a campsite and swept away recreational vehicles and those inside. Elsewhere in Alexander County, another person died in a car accident that was attributed to a bridge washout, while a child reportedly drowned in a swollen creek in Wake County near Raleigh. At the time of this writing, the death toll from the rainfall-induced flooding stood at seven, with two others missing. Additionally, hundreds of other people were evacuated or rescued statewide, including 143 students from the Charlotte Corvian Community School, while more than 16,400 homes and businesses lost electricity. Dozens of schools delayed the start of classes or shifted to virtual learning only on Thursday due to the inclement weather, while others in the eastern part of the state closed early once the rainfall began. The weather system, a combination of tropical moisture from Eta and a cold front, also affected parts of South Carolina and Virginia. In the former, several people had to be rescued from flooded homes in York County, while southeastern Virginia saw intense rainfall and flooding as well; flood warnings were still in place on Friday.



Assessment: Conditions improved across the southeastern U.S. on Friday and drier weather is forecast throughout the region into next week, presumably facilitating recovery and clean-up efforts. Indeed, power appeared to have been restored to the vast majority of affected customers by Friday morning; however, as noted above, the threat of flooding and associated disruptions will persist in the coming days. With swollen rivers projected to crest on Saturday, water levels are unlikely to recede before Sunday, especially from low-lying roads and neighborhoods. As such, with further residential flooding and road closures almost certain over the weekend, the public should allow additional time for overland travel and exercise caution when driving, taking care not to drive around barricades or on flooded roads, particularly those covered by moving water.

Headline: Booms Placed After Oil from Decommissioned Pipeline Leaked into Sea at Port Dickson
Details:
Officials on Wednesday confirmed that a black substance discovered in monsoon storm drains in the Kampung Gelam area of Port Dickson, south of Kuala Lumpur, on Sunday was crude oil. The oil leaked from decommissioned pipelines connected to a refinery in the area after the pipes were punctured during construction work. Repair work to the pipes was expected to be completed on Wednesday.



Assessment: Some of the oil from the leak flowed into the nearby sea. Authorities have placed booms in the area to stop additional flow into the ocean. Following the repairs to the broken section of pipeline, work will be carried out to flush remaining crude oil from the pipes. Sand will be used to replace contaminated earth near the leak. Officials have not yet reported how much oil actually leaked or made it into the ocean. While there has been no immediate indication that this was a major spill, disruptions are possible in the area while cleanup operations are ongoing.

Headline: Hong Kong Protests Become More Violent and Less Predictable, Requiring a Higher Level of Caution
Details:
On Friday, protests continued across Hong Kong, with violent clashes taking place in the Mong Kok area of Kowloon and the Sheung Shui area of the New Territories in the evening. Protesters left the Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), which had been a flashpoint of clashes with police earlier in the week, but some reportedly regrouped at Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU) and others said they were planning to carry out different actions. Friday marked the fifth consecutive day where general strikes were called from the morning, although the morning disruptions were much less severe when compared to earlier in the week. Individuals across Hong Kong also continued the daily action of walking out and occupying the streets during lunch, although there were no reports of major clashes, which took place earlier in the week as well.

The day before, Chinese President Xi Jinping issued another statement supporting Hong Kong Chief Executive Carrie Lam and called the protests a trampling of the rule of law and a blatant challenge to the one country, two systems arrangement. The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission, which is a government body tasked with advising the U.S. Congress, also recommended that if Beijing intervened militarily, Hong Kong s special economic status should be suspended. The recommendation is non-binding and there were no reports that such a plan was in place.

Assessment: Protests have entered a more violent and less predictable phase since Monday, with Hong Kong seeing daily general strikes that have resulted in widespread clashes and transportation disruptions. Protesters were generally satisfied with the disruptions seen in Monday s action, which led them to call for daily strikes through Friday. The lower impact of Friday s general strike could be indicative of slowing momentum for the actions, although it could also just be a temporary pause as protesters regroup. The actions over the past week have also seen a notable shift in tactics that have made the demonstrations less predictable. Protesters have started to use  blossom everywhere  tactics, which involve impromptu gatherings in the protesters  own local neighborhoods. The objective is to divide the attention of the police force and is also in response to the government shutting down the MTR system more quickly during protests, which was used in the previous  be water  tactics that saw protesters spread from location to location by train. Flash mob tactics, which involve the locations of demonstrations being announced just an hour or two before they start, are also becoming more popular among protesters. These developments in the protest movement make demonstrations more difficult to plan for in advance and necessitate a higher level of situational awareness being observed at all times. Some areas that have seen prolonged actions by protesters, such as PolyU and CUHK, should be avoided.

The increased levels of violence over the past week, which included a protester being shot, a person being set on fire, and a man dying after being hit by a brick have raised concerns that the Chinese military could decide to intervene and restore order. However, this is an extreme step that would be an absolute last resort if it was clear that the government and police had lost control of the situation, as it would likely have severe economic and political ramifications. The Hong Kong government still has a number of other options available, such as imposing additional restrictions under the Emergency Regulations Ordinance (ERO), which could include curfews, greater powers for police, or telecommunications restrictions, that would likely be exercised before a military intervention took place. It is still important to note that the situation remains very fluid and conditions could change quickly, and all political and protest-related developments should be closely monitored.

Headline: Teachers in Seven Washington School Districts are on Strike; Strikes Authorized in Other Districts
Details:
Negotiations are being held between teachers  unions and school districts across Washington in an attempt to avoid strikes over salary increases. Teachers in southwestern Washington have commenced strikes in Evergreen, Vancouver, Ridgefield, Hockinson, Washougal, Battle Ground, and Longview school districts. The start of the school year in these districts has been delayed, impacting approximately 78,000 students. Teachers in Seattle are among other districts in the state who have authorized union representatives to call a strike if agreements are not reached by the start of the school year. Classes are scheduled to begin for Seattle Public Schools on Wednesday, September 5. Teachers and school districts are negotiating over the level of wage increases after the state legislature approved an additional $1 billion for educators  salaries this year.   
 
	Assessment: Negotiations between unions and school districts are being held at the local level. This has reportedly limited the resources available during bargaining. Strikes have already begun in several school districts where state mediators were unable to meet with the two sides because they were in negotiations elsewhere. The Washington Public Employment Relations Commission (PERC) has reportedly received 27 requests for a mediator since July 1, of which 20 cases are still active. PERC indicated that all non-teacher-related disputes are currently on hold for the time being. Resilience360 customers are advised to anticipate strike-related disruptions while negotiations continue.

Headline: Disruptions Reported to DHL and FedEx Shipping from China to India Amid Customs Inspections
Details:
Media sources have reported that some customers of shipping company DHL’s India subsidiary received notices on Thursday that the company has suspended its pick-up of packages being imported to India from China, including shipments from Hong Kong and Macao. The suspension is expected to remain in place for ten days and comes due to a backlog of shipments at Indian ports caused by increased customs inspections of products arriving from China. The DHL notice reportedly details delays at all ports in India, while media reports have previously mentioned increased inspections at the Port of Chennai and have more recently specified additional delays to Chinese imports at Indira Gandhi International Airport (DEL) in Delhi, Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose International Airport (CCU) in Kolkata, and Mumbai’s Jawaharlal Nehru Port. Media reports and posts on social media have also indicated a temporary suspension of FedEx shipping from China to India.



Assessment: The reported suspensions by DHL and FedEx come following reports earlier in the week of significantly more thorough customs inspections of good entering India from China in the aftermath of the June 15 border clash between Indian and Chinese troops. According to Indian media, customs officers have received instructions to open all containers arriving from China and individually inspect every item inside. Normally, only around 30 percent of imported products arriving in India are physically inspected. The ostensible reason given for the increased checks is that drugs have recently been intercepted in packages from China arriving in Chennai, but it is far more likely that the measures are intended as economic retaliation against China following the earlier clash. Indian officials have, however, denied that additional customs inspections have been ordered, whether officially or otherwise. The resulting shipping delays from the inspections are likely to impact supply chains, especially if the situation persists for an extended period of time. Individuals and businesses are advised to expect associated delays and disruptions to shipping while tensions between India and China remain elevated.

Headline: UPDATE: Workers in the steel industry conclude one-day strike; negotiations to resume on March 16
Details: On March 12, updated media sources report that steel workers with labor union IG Metall have concluded a warning strike across northwestern Germany after the employer’s association had unilaterally called off the next rounds of talks, citing the sickness of its chief negotiator as the reason. Steelworkers previously went on strike in February across the region. IG Metall is demanding a 6 percent wage increase for its 72,000 workers from the steel industry in Germany’s northwest. The next round of talks is now planned for March 16. The following plants were affected: Arcelor Mittal in Bremen, ThyssenKrupp Steel in Eichen and Ferndorf, Deutsche Edelstahlwerke in Geiswald, Peiner Träger GmbH in Peine and Georgsmarienhütte GmbH in Georgsmarienhütte. Many production plants located in the Ruhr area were also expected to go on strike, including Thyssen-Krupp, ArcelorMittal, Salzgitter, Krupp Mannesmann and Baosteel Tailored Blanks.

Headline: UPDATE: Philippines customs sets temporary guidelines to mitigate congestion
Details: Updated sources on March 8 indicate that the Bureau of Customs (BOC) of the Philippines has issued a temporary guideline regarding with the return of empty containers at the port of Manila (POM) and the Manila International Container Port (MICP) to prevent congestion. According to the new guideline, importers, truckers, brokers and other port stakeholders are temporarily banned from returning empty containers to the premises of the POM and the MICP until further notice by the BOC. However, empty containers with Special Permit to Load (SPTL) issued by the BOC will be allowed to enter to the designated areas for POM and MICP. The empty containers covered by SPTL must be moved to their designated areas within a 72-hour period before its scheduled date and time of their loading to carry vessels for re-exportation overseas. Customers with shipments to Manila are advised to follow the new guidelines by engaging with local agents to avoid delays in cargo unloading and loading process.

Headline: Weather warnings issued as Tropical Storm Nangka moves towards the SAR
Details: The Hong Kong Observatory has issued weather warnings as Tropical Storm Nangka tracks closer to the special administrative region (SAR). The Hong Kong Observatory will consider issuing the No 8 typhoon signal before dawn on 13 October. Strong winds and heavy rain are forecast as Nangka intensifies, while gradually moving closer to China’s southern coast. Earlier today, a No 3 typhoon warning signal was issued, which indicates winds with mean speeds of 41 to 62km/h are expected. At 19:00 local time on Monday, Nangka was estimated to be about 470km south of Hong Kong and expected to move west or west-northwest at about 22km/h in the general direction of Hainan Island.

Headline: Ongoing Tensions Sustain the Risk of Clashes at Weekend Protests in Europe over Racial Justice
Details:
Protest activity in recent weeks related to the Black Lives Matter movement and associated local grievances in several European countries is planned to continue through the coming weekend. Hotspots of recent protest activity with flare-ups around demonstrations, such as in London and Paris, are likely to remain so. Police in Paris have prohibited three demonstrations planned for Saturday, though gatherings are likely to occur regardless of the prohibition, raising the potential for confrontations and clashes with authorities. Potentially adding to tensions, the French government walked back plans to prohibit chokeholds by police until a replacement method is found. Additional clashes between opposing groups in London may occur, while police may take swift action to quell unruly behavior. London authorities have arrested nearly 230 people in connection to protests in recent weeks. Some prominent German politicians have rejected alleged systemic racism among police forces, and disputes over calls for reform can further demonstration activity in the near term. As well as central squares, government buildings, and US diplomatic facilities in several European countries, protests and associated escalations have frequently occurred around controversial statues and other symbols. Sites connected with colonial history have been common targets of condemnation. 



Assessment: The bulk of demonstrators have been peaceful, though clashes with counter-protesters and police remain a risk. Authorities continue to be challenged by allowing peaceful protest while trying to deter actions that could result in unrest, as well as the ongoing difficulty of large crowds developing while COVID-19 restrictions on gatherings remain in effect. Scrutiny over policing methods and accusations of systemic racism are likely to prompt additional demonstrations by officers, and discontent among officers could results in actions such as increased sick calls, as has occurred in limited instances in the United States. Recent protests over alleged police violence and racial inequalities have also drawn attention to the lack of official data held by countries such as France and Germany, due to policies against the collection of ethnicity in demographic data, that could underscore disparities. With mobilizations continuing over the coming days, it is advised to avoid protest activity as a precaution and to anticipate potential disruption in proximity to demonstrations.

Headline: Container ship drifted through Port of Livorno
Details: Industry sources reported that on January 24, 2019, at 1.35 p.m. container vessel ""Maersk Sheerness"" broke lose from its moorings at the Lucca Quay in the port of Livorno in ENE winds of 35 knots and broke out a bollard. The ship drifted to the opposite dock, the Massa quay and hit another berthed container ship, the ""Chacabuco"", with its stern. The container ship managed to get back to its berth with the help of three tugs, but nevertheless broke lose again, breaking out another bollard, this time at the bow. Eventually the wind dropped and the ship could finally be secured at its berth again at 3.20 p.m. The ship left the port again on January 25 at 9 a.m., bound to Genova, where it was expected in the evening hours.

Headline: American Airlines Flight Attendants to Picket at 15 Airports Across the US on Sunday, November 18
Details:
On Sunday, November 18, American Airlines flight attendants represented by the Association of Professional Flight Attendants (APFA) plan to demonstrate at 15 airports across the United States. The demonstrations will entail picketing and are scheduled to occur from 11:00 AM to 1:30 PM local time at each of the specified airports. The action has been called to commemorate the 25 th  anniversary of a strike by the airline s flight attendants, and to protest against what the union alleges are problems with American Airlines  scheduling system, an unfair sickness policy, and contract and seniority violations. 
 
	Demonstrations are scheduled for the following airports: Logan International Airport (BOS), Charlotte Douglas International Airport (CLT), Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA), Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW), Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR), John F Kennedy International Airport (JFK), Miami International Airport (MIA), O Hare International Airport (ORD), Pittsburgh International Airport (ORD), Philadelphia International Airport (PHL), Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX), Raleigh-Durham International Airport (RDU), San Francisco International Airport (SFO), and St. Louis Lambert International Airport (STL). 
 
	Assessment: According to media reports, only flight attendants who are not scheduled to be working during these hours will be participating in the demonstrations. As such, it is unlikely that the demonstrations will result in significant disruptions to American Airlines  operations. Details were not immediately available regarding expected participation at individual actions. Air travelers are advised to contact their airline for any flight-specific information, and should also anticipate the possibility of increased congestion at impacted airports.

Headline: Protest Activity Easing but Continues Around Catalonia as Businesses Call for Resolution of Conflict
Details:
Protests that erupted last week over the sentencing of Catalan politicians have largely scaled back following the peak of mass protests last Friday driven by the conclusion of multiday marches into Barcelona and a general strike that day. Between Monday, October 14, and Sunday, October 20, about US $3.4 million of damage occurred during unruly protests in Barcelona, the city announced on Wednesday. The protests damaged or destroyed 1,044 containers such as trash and recycling bins, burned 57 trees, and damaged nearly 7,900 feet of asphalt. Nearly 2,100 municipal police patrols drove up overtime costs, in addition to overtime for firefighters. Two cruise ships were diverted from the Port of Barcelona during the wave of protests last week. Recent protests have concentrated around government buildings, with some participants marching from university or other student locations. During a gathering of several hundred Catalan business leaders on Wednesday in Barcelona, participants called on the regional and national leadership to find solutions leading to a conclusion of the latest conflict.

Assessment: While protest activity has eased around Catalonia compared to sustained disruptive activity in the week prior, smaller demonstrations continue to be held and have the potential for similar scenes of clashes and other unruly behavior. Upcoming weekend demonstration activity is likely to draw a larger turnout than weekday protests of recent days. About 200 protesters have been detained during the spate of protests, though there has been controversy about the relatively low number of people who have been charged by local law enforcement compared to the scenes of violence and property damage, typically involving smaller groups on the sidelines or separate from larger protests. Many of those engaged in scenes of unrest have been youths, frequently seemingly aligned with anarchist-style positions as well as people supporting Catalan independence who are angry over perceived oppression and police violence. Law enforcement officers have employed equipment such as rubber bullets and baton charges in responding to some protests, and some violent groups amidst the protests have focused on confrontations with National Police deployed in Catalonia. According to the Spanish interior ministry, about 13 percent of arrested protesters were foreigners. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has resisted calls by from some right-wing politicians for Madrid to impose central control over the autonomous region, while warning that efforts to breach Spanish law will be met with  a firm and decisive response.  With protest activity expected to continue in Catalonia at least sporadically in the buildup to the national general election on November 10, it is advised to continue monitoring associated developments for potential disruptive actions and to avoid all protest activity due to the risk of further outbreaks of violence.

Headline: Singapore port authorities revise detailed guidelines for crew changes amid COVID-19 outbreak
Details:
Media sources report that the port authorities of Singapore will be implementing detailed guidelines for crew changes due to the recent cases of crew members who are tested positive for COVID-19 upon arrival in Singapore. The new measures will include the need for the signing-on crew to self-isolate for the 14 days before departing for Singapore, ship-owners, managers, and agents ensuring accurate COVID-19 Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) tests, and direct transfers to the ship upon arrival in Singapore.
With immediate effect, the authorities will give priority to applications from Singapore registered ships and applications for sign-off crew only (i.e. without signing-on new crew). For all other cases, the authorities will consider the following circumstances for crew change applications:

(a) the crew has served his/her maximum time on board and no further extension of the employment contract is granted by the flag State; or
(b) compassionate grounds e.g. death of an immediate family member; or
(c) the crew is no longer medically fit to work onboard the ship.

Headline: US Consulate General Issues Health Alert Regarding New CDC Designation
Details:
On Tuesday, the United States Consulate General in Istanbul issued an updated Health Alert for US citizens in Turkey regarding COVID-19. The message reads:



“The Department of State has issued a Global Level 4 Health Advisory advising U.S. citizens to avoid all international travel due to the global impact of COVID-19.



The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) issued a Level 3 COVID-19 Health Notice for Turkey warning travelers to avoid all nonessential travel to Turkey. Travelers returning to the United States from Turkey should stay home for 14 days after returning from travel, monitor their health, and practice social distancing.



U.S. citizens who are considering returning to the United States are urged to work with their airlines to make travel arrangements while flights are still available.  Travelers should be prepared for additional travel restrictions to be put into effect with little or no advance notice.



Country-Specific Information



• Turkey has confirmed cases of COVID-19 within its borders.

• For current information go to the Turkish Ministry of Health COVID-19 web page.



Entry and Exit Requirements:



• Starting March 27, Turkish Airlines is suspending all international commercial routes, except to New York JFK, Washington Dulles, Hong Kong, Addis Ababa, and Moscow.   

• The Government of Turkey has suspended passenger flights to/from Algeria, Angola, Austria, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Belgium, Cameroon, Canada, Chad, Colombia, Cote d’Ivoire, Czech Republic, Cyprus, Denmark, Djibouti, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Egypt, Equatorial Guinea, Finland, France, Georgia, Germany, Guatemala, Hungary, India, Iran, Iraq, Ireland, Italy, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Kenya, Kosovo, Kuwait, Latvia, Lebanon, Mainland China, Mauritania, Moldova, Mongolia, Montenegro, Morocco, Nepal, Netherlands, Niger, North Macedonia, Norway, Oman, Panama, Peru, Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Saudi Arabia, Slovenia, South Korea, Spain, Sri Lanka, Sudan, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, Tunisia, Ukraine, United Arab Emirates, United Kingdom and Uzbekistan.

• Foreign citizens are not permitted to transit or enter Turkey if they were physically present in these countries, as well as Greece and Bulgaria, in the last 14 days.

• Turkish citizens who were in these countries in the past 14 days are allowed to enter Turkey but are subject to a quarantine requirement.

• Additionally, Turkish Airlines and other carriers are constantly updating their flight schedules, some of which are more restrictive than government bans. For an updated list of cancelled Turkish Airline flights visit Turkish Airlines website.

• Passenger crossings are not permitted at Turkish land borders with Bulgaria, Greece, Iran, and Iraq; nor at the Sarp border crossing with Georgia, nor at the Dilucu land border.

• Passenger sea crossings between Greece and Turkey are also closed.

Turkish Ministry of Health officials screen travelers at airports and maritime ports, as well as some land crossings, using thermal cameras.

To date, travelers do not need any specific health documentation to enter/exit Turkey.



Quarantine Information:



• If an individual presents with COVID-19 symptoms, Turkish Ministry of Health guidelines are to send that person to a designated hospital for testing and possible observation under quarantine for 14 days.

• All museums and archaeological sites closed March 19.

• All primary, middle and high schools (public and private) closed on March 16 and will begin online/distance learning the week of March 23.

• All universities closed on March 16 for three weeks.

• Also closed: theaters, cinemas, exhibition centers, concert halls, wedding halls, restaurants/cafes offering live music, casinos, pubs, taverns, coffee houses, cafes, cafeterias, hookah cafes, internet cafes, all kinds of indoor playgrounds (including inside shopping malls and restaurants), tea gardens, clubhouses, amusement parks, swimming pools, barber shops, hair salons, Turkish baths, saunas, hot springs, massage parlors, spas, and sports centers.



Local Resources:



• Dial 184 within Turkey to access the Turkish Ministry of Health COVID-19 Telephone Hotline (Turkish/English/Arabic)

• Turkish Ministry of Health COVID-19 web page.

• Turkish Airlines Press Releases

• Turkish General Directorate of Civil Aviation



Other links:



• COVID-19 crisis page on travel.state.gov

• CDC page on COVID-19

• F.A.Q. About Presidential Proclamation — Travel From Europe on travel.state.gov

• Turkey Country Information and Travel Advisory page”



Assessment: At the time of this writing, Turkey’s COVID-19 case tally stood at 1,529, with 37 deaths. Despite being one of the last countries in the Middle East and North Africa to record a positive coronavirus infection, Turkey is now the third- and second-most affected country in the region in terms of cases and deaths, respectively. The rapid spread of the virus can likely be attributed to several factors, including a slow response by the government, a lack of public compliance with restrictions and prevention measures, and the country’s proximity to other coronavirus “hotspots,” notably Iran, as well as its reputation as a global hub for international travel. It has been reported that the Turkish government has thus far focused primarily on testing individuals who recently arrived from abroad, which could also be a reason for the high number of cases; however, the imposition of a ban on individuals over the age of 65 and those with chronic health problems from leaving their homes on March 21 suggests that tighter movement restrictions, potentially including general lockdowns and/or curfews, could be forthcoming. In the meantime, further spread of COVID-19 should be anticipated in Turkey in the near future, with clients advised to practice diligent handwashing, avoid individuals exhibiting outward signs of illness, and refrain from touching one’s eyes, nose, or mouth with unwashed hands.

Headline: Crackdown on opposition, expansion of Chinese presence likely to accelerate...
Details: Risks: Government instability; Regulatory burden; Labour strikesSectors or assets affected: AllOn 29 January, the European Union closed the consultation window for member states to offer opinions on the removal of Cambodia from the ""Everything but Arms"" (EBA) preferential trade scheme that permits duty- and quota-free exports of all products except arms and armaments. The European Union is now likely to initiate Cambodia's removal from the scheme. This process would take approximately 12 months and probably substantially affect Cambodia's textiles and clothing industry, which represented 68% of the country's exports in 2016, 46% of which was imported by European countries, according to the latest Word Bank data. These negative developments in Cambodia-EU relations occur in the context of growing Chinese investment and positive ties. Specifically, from 9 to 12 January, three Chinese naval vessels docked at Sihanoukville port, stoking international concerns that Chinese firm Tianjin Union Development Group's USD3.8-billion development project in neighbouring Koh Kong province would create a civilian port that would also be open to Chinese military assets. Significance: Unlike following the EU's re-imposition of rice tariffs in January, Cambodia would not be able to replace EU demand with Chinese imports for other sectors that currently benefit from the EBA. The move would nonetheless be supported by Cambodia's political opposition, including exiled leader Sam Rainsy. Importantly, garment workers in Phnom Penh have been supportive of the opposition and would most probably organise strikes, disrupting road transport, if their industry is threatened. An indicator of Prime Minister Hun Sen attempting to mitigate the risks of removal from the EBA to economic growth and political stability would be the announcement of policies facilitating tourism from China or investment in non-garment manufacturing and infrastructure. Despite being unlikely in the six-month outlook, another indicator of increasing distance between Cambodia and the European Union, likely to manifest in preferential regulation for Chinese firms, would be a change to the constitution (which currently bans foreign military bases). If proposed by Hun Sen, this would probably pass and formally facilitate a growing Chinese military presence, specifically naval assets at ports in the Gulf of Thailand. This process would take approximately 12 months and probably substantially affect Cambodia's textiles and clothing industry, which represented 68% of the country's exports in 2016, 46% of which was imported by European countries, according to the latest Word Bank data. These negative developments in Cambodia-EU relations occur in the context of growing Chinese investment and positive ties. Specifically, from 9 to 12 January, three Chinese naval vessels docked at Sihanoukville port, stoking international concerns that Chinese firm Tianjin Union Development Group's USD3.8-billion development project in neighbouring Koh Kong province would create a civilian port that would also be open to Chinese military assets. Significance: Unlike following the EU's re-imposition of rice tariffs in January, Cambodia would not be able to replace EU demand with Chinese imports for other sectors that currently benefit from the EBA. The move would nonetheless be supported by Cambodia's political opposition, including exiled leader Sam Rainsy. Importantly, garment workers in Phnom Penh have been supportive of the opposition and would most probably organise strikes, disrupting road transport, if their industry is threatened. An indicator of Prime Minister Hun Sen attempting to mitigate the risks of removal from the EBA to economic growth and political stability would be the announcement of policies facilitating tourism from China or investment in non-garment manufacturing and infrastructure. Despite being unlikely in the six-month outlook, another indicator of increasing distance between Cambodia and the European Union, likely to manifest in preferential regulation for Chinese firms, would be a change to the constitution (which currently bans foreign military bases). If proposed by Hun Sen, this would probably pass and formally facilitate a growing Chinese military presence, specifically naval assets at ports in the Gulf of Thailand. Headline: Hundreds Arrested Following September 20-21 Protests; Further Demonstrations Possible
Details:
On Monday, media sources reported that Egyptian authorities have arrested some 400 people following a rash of anti-government protests that broke out in several cities on September 20-21. Among those detained was Mahienour El-Masry, a prominent human rights activist and lawyer who was taken into custody in Cairo late Sunday. According to reports, authorities, including plain-clothes police officers, have been stopping individuals in Cairo and checking social media content on their cell phones. Meanwhile, the internet monitoring group Netblocks says it has recorded disruptions affecting social media platforms and news sites since September 22, with some suggesting that Arabic-language editions of international media have been blocked. The moves come after a few thousand people heeded online protest calls by a self-exiled Egyptian businessman who has accused Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi and the military of corruption. Demonstrations were reported in several cities and towns on September 20 and September 21, notably in Cairo, Alexandria, Giza, Damietta, Suez, Port Said, and El-Mahalla El-Kubra, with activists demanding that President Sisi step down. Clashes ensued when police attempted to disperse the gatherings with tear gas and rubber bullets. Unconfirmed reports indicated that several people were injured. In addition to skirmishes, which were most pronounced in Suez on September 21, protest-related traffic disruptions were also reported over the weekend.

Assessment: Compared to the Arab Spring protests in 2011 and the demonstrations against late Islamist President Mohamed Morsi in 2013, the September 20-21 gatherings were smaller and appeared to be spontaneous and devoid of central leadership. Thus, while some have described the protests as the most significant challenge to Sisi s rule to date, the movement does not seem to have gained significant traction at this time. Still, given the overall rarity of protest activity in Egypt due to strict government action against unauthorized gatherings, the fact that the demonstrations materialized at all is somewhat surprising and evidence of simmering public discontent over various grievances, notably alleged government corruption, perceived authoritarianism, and bleak economic prospects. As such, the possibility of future protests cannot be ruled out in the coming days; the aforementioned exiled businessman has called for a million-man march in Egypt on Friday, September 27. Resilience360 advises customers in Egypt to avoid any public gatherings that may crop up due to the potential for violence, particularly unruly crowd behavior and aggressive crowd dispersal methods by police.

Headline: Irrespective of Panamanian government’s decision on suspension of labour contracts, strikes and protests likely from early 2021 - UPDATE 1
Details: Panama’s Minister of Labour and Labour Development Doris Zapata on 27 November said that 96,066 labour contracts out of a total of 282,000 suspended because of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19)-virus pandemic have been reactivated. Legislation suspending contracts and reducing the working day was passed in March, with the National Assembly in July extending the measure until 31 December. After this date, workers must return to their jobs under the same conditions as before the suspension; if they do not, companies will have to dismiss them, paying the corresponding severance. Business organisations such as the Federation of Commercial Associations (Federación de Cámaras de Comercio: Fedecámaras) have strongly lobbied in favour of extending the measure into 2021, as around 85% of small and medium-sized companies have said that they are likely to be forced to reopen with fewer staff, while only 8% have said that they have sufficient funding to cover workers’ severance pay. Unions oppose any extension on the grounds that affected workers have been without adequate income for the past eight months (the government funds only USD100 per month through the Panama Solidario welfare payment) and are in expectation of either the restoration of full wages or severance pay.Significance: Irrespective of the government’s decision on the future of contract suspensions, strikes and protests are likely from the first few months of 2021. In the event of an extension, unions will press for early contract reactivation, and many companies are unlikely to be able to either restore full salaries or fund severance pay. The government has stated that it is open to extending the suspension for sectors most affected by the lockdowns and is currently in discussions with business and labour sectors. If, as is likely, the National Union of Workers of Construction and Similar Industries (El Sindicato único nacional de trabajadores de la industria de la construcción y similares: SUNTRACS) rejects an agreement, there would be a high likelihood of protest roadblocks lasting for weeks at a time, causing disruption to cargo and resulting in vandalism near Colón port and Panama City. Even if an agreement regarding suspension is reached with unions, protest risks are likely to be high from early 2021. Durban and surrounding communities, including KwaMashu, Inanda and Ntuzuma, have been badly affected. Disaster teams and officials are currently assessing the damage. In Durban, a temporary bridge has additionally collapsed and caused rubble to block storm water drains, further exacerbating the problem and preventing rainwater from draining.

Headline: UPDATE - Australia: Firefighters to remain on the scene of large fire in Campbellfield, Melbourne over the coming days
Details: Updated reports say that firefighters are still on the scene of a large fire that broke out in an industrial warehouse located along Thornycroft Street in Campbellfield, Melbourne on Friday morning. Operations at the warehouse had been suspended prior to the blaze as the company, Bradbury Industrial Services, had been stockpiling an illegal amount of chemicals. The Environment Protection Authority has said that there were more than 400,000 litres of hazardous materials on site. More than 175 firefighters have been on the scene of the blaze throughout the day in an attempt to contain it. A number of nearby businesses have been evacuated as a precaution. At the time of reporting, firefighters have contained the blaze to the premises, however it is still burning due to the volume of fuel that was inside. Smoke from the fire is still impacting the locality and the authorities have urged residents in the immediate area to limit time spent outdoors due to the chemicals that could be in the air. Environmental experts are monitoring pollution levels. Firefighters have said that they are likely to remain on the scene for several days to ensure that the fire is safely extinguished. Localised disruption is ensuing.

Headline: UPDATE 10 - Jakarta & West Java – Flooding has subsided in Sukabumi and Central Jakarta; no major rain expected.
Details:
Updated Report:

Media sources are reporting that the flooding in Sukabumi and Central Jakarta has subsided and that the Emergency Response status was revoked on Monday. No major rains are expected throughout today. Aid is still being distributed to those impacted in the area.

Previous Updates:

Sources reported that heavy rainfall caused flooding in multiple locations across Jakarta Province and West Java Province. The Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) expects heavy rain to fall throughout Jakarta and West Java Province through Wednesday, September 30. As a result, local government agencies continue to expect associated disruptions and damages to take place in the most affected areas. Flood relief efforts continue throughout the region, with local government delivering food parcels and structural assistants.

Sources reported that all missing persons in Sukabumi District in West Java Province have been found, but three were killed. Twenty other people in Sukabumi were injured. Emergency services have called off search and rescue missions in the area. At least 34 shelters have been set up in Central Jakarta for residents within the most severely impacted areas. Impacted areas include Tanah Abang, Benhil, Petamburan, and Karet Tengsin, as well as residential areas near the Ciliwung River such as Kartini and Pasar Baru In addition, the Central Jakarta City Government has ordered the dredging of waterways, as well as the repair of several supporting infrastructures. 

At least 210 families have been displaced in Sukabumi. The Pabrik PT. Aqua Golden Mississippi factory in Bogor, West Java has been reopened after flash flooding caused the facility to close for several days. The Ciliwung River has reportedly overflown near Kebon Pala, causing inundation in several areas. In addition, the Cianten River also overflowed which caused severe inundation in the Cibunian Village, Pamijahan District.

Headline: Snap General Election and Trial of Catalan Separatists Driving Protests in Coming Months
Details:
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has called a snap general election for Sunday, April 28, after defeat in the legislature. The decision follows on large protests over the relationship between Catalonia and Madrid, and disagreements between political factions in congress. Adding to debate in Spain is the recent start of the trial of Catalan separatist officials for their roles in a prohibited independence referendum. Beyond debate over independence and levels of autonomy for Catalonia, snap elections will draw an array of issues to the forefront and mobilize demonstrations in Spain. Rising far-right support heightens the potential for protests associated with the Vox party as well as other political candidates and officials who may express controversial positions. Demonstrations are likely to be frequent through the springtime, with some causing disruptions and resulting in restive behavior. 

 
	 Recent Developments  
 
	On Friday, February 15, Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez announced that an early nationwide general election will be held on April 28. Sanchez has been in office less than a year with a minority government. His call for a new election followed the failure Wednesday of his 2019 budget bill to advance in congress. Parties voting against Sanchez and the budget of his Socialist Party (PSOE) included the conservative Popular Party (PP), center-right Ciudadanos (Citizens), and pro-independence factions from Catalonia. Support from Catalan lawmakers had been offered in exchange for concessions regarding Catalan officials facing criminal charges for their involvement in the 2017 Illegal independence referendum. Sanchez s openness to negotiating with Catalonian separatists short of considering an independence vote spurred a protest in Madrid on Sunday, February 10, that drew about 45,000 participants to Plaza de Colon. The protest was organized by the PP, Ciudadanos, and the far-right Vox party, and was held without serious incident. No agreement was reached between Sanchez and Catalan lawmakers prior to the prime minister s legislative defeat. 
 
	The vote Wednesday proceeded the opening of the trial of a dozen Catalan separatists at the Supreme Court in Madrid on Tuesday. The trial is expected to last about three months. Among some 500 witnesses are former Prime Minister Mariano Rajoy, Catalan Parliament Speaker Roger Torrent, and Barcelona Mayor Ada Colau. The arrests, transfers, and other developments related to the criminal charges against Catalan separatist leaders have consistently prompted protests by their supporters. Thousands of people protested around Barcelona on Wednesday as the separatists  trial opened, with about 6,000 people gathering in Pla a de Catalunya while some protesters blocked highways and set piles of tires on fire. Further demonstrations are planned in Catalonia on Saturday, February 16, with at least thousands likely to turn out for weekend mobilizations. 
 
	 Background  
 
	Catalonian independence has been a highly divisive issue for years, though it has not been characterized by the same levels of violence and terrorism as previous decades of Basque separatism. Pro-independence supporters in Catalonia regularly mobilize to push for their demands, with exceptionally large demonstrations capable of attracting more than 100,000 participants, with smaller demonstrations across the region. Pro-unity demonstrations within Catalonia are less frequent and typically not reaching the same participation levels, though the October 2017 independence referendum mobilized supporters of both sides. While Madrid has typically seen the largest pro-unity demonstrations, the 2017 referendum spurred demonstrations in cities and towns across the country. 
 
	Although Spain has held three general elections in less than four years, the failure of a government budget bill in congress is only the second such instance since 1975, when fascist dictator Francisco Franco died. Sanchez came to power in June 2018 following the vote of no confidence that ejected former Prime Minister Rajoy. In 2016, Spain held a general election triggered by the failure for any parties to form a government following elections in 2015, the first such instance in Spanish history. Rajoy was able to reclaim the office of the prime minister in 2016 following the PSOE s decision to abstain from voting on the formation of a new government   a choice taken to prevent a third election being called amidst political gridlock.  
	 Assessment  
 
	Pro-independence efforts in Catalonia pose a continuing challenge and point of controversy in Spain, and debates over separatism and degrees of autonomy are likely to be prominent in the upcoming election. As parties compete for seats in parliament with an eye to the potential formation of a ruling coalition, given the likely event no single party secures an absolute majority, smaller parties may prove crucial to getting sufficient numbers to be able to form a government. However, as seen in the recent legislative results and protest last weekend, there is a risk of backlash over the consideration of any concessions to Catalonia, even in spite of a refusal to consider a legally recognized referendum. The pro-unity demonstration in Madrid last Sunday was exceptional for the PP leader s appearance with the Vox leader, despite past efforts by the more center-right party to maintain distance from any associations with the growing far-right party. The development could signal that PP may attempt to retake power with the support of Vox, uniting on issues such as the shared opposition to Catalan independence. 
 
	Vox has been gaining support around the country, including winning seats in Andalusia s regional elections in December that resulted in Vox providing the backing for the PP to claim sufficient support to have a ruling coalition. Post-Franco Spain has not previously had a substantial resurgence of far-right parties in the political sphere; however, the small but growing Vox reflects a broader trend in Europe of populist, nationalist platforms gaining support and challenging established parties. Vox is not expected to jump to the head of polls nationally, though it could be seen as a potential junior partner or coalition faction to shore up a ruling majority in parliament. As well as being staunchly opposed to Catalan independence, Vox backs an array of controversial views, including on issues such as immigration and women s rights. 
 
	The far-right Vox has already been the focus of protests, including by anti-fascists and feminists. As the party seeks to gain a stronger national footing in the April election, its events around the country are likely to draw protests. Such demonstrations could result in clashes between opposing groups, clashes with authorities, and other unruly actions such as property damage. Demonstrations regarding Catalan independence, both for and against, also carry the potential for clashes, though such incidents typically involve fringe elements. Developments in the trial of Catalan officials in Madrid will continue to spur both planned and spontaneous demonstrations. Pro-independence organizers in Catalonia have also called sectoral and general strikes in the past to draw attention to their cause and protest grievances. Such labor actions are capable of causing substantial disruption, and often coincide with protest activity seeking to block highways and key roads as well as concentrating outside of government buildings. It is advised to exercise caution and avoid demonstration activity when possible due to the risk of incidents of unrest. Demonstrations are likely to have an increased police presence monitoring developments and localized disruptions are possible. Furthermore, although no specific, credible threat is known at this time, there is an ongoing heightened threat of jihadist terrorism in Spain and around Europe. The risk of extremists targeting crowds of people, including demonstrators, cannot be ruled out. Resilience360 customers are advised to maintain increased situational awareness, particularly in crowded and high-profile locations, and to report suspicious behavior or items to local authorities.

The protest was organized by the PP, Ciudadanos, and the far-right Vox party, and was held without serious incident. No agreement was reached between Sanchez and Catalan lawmakers prior to the prime minister s legislative defeat. 
 
	The vote Wednesday proceeded the opening of the trial of a dozen Catalan separatists at the Supreme Court in Madrid on Tuesday. The trial is expected to last about three months. Among some 500 witnesses are former Prime Minister Mariano Rajoy, Catalan Parliament Speaker Roger Torrent, and Barcelona Mayor Ada Colau. The arrests, transfers, and other developments related to the criminal charges against Catalan separatist leaders have consistently prompted protests by their supporters. Thousands of people protested around Barcelona on Wednesday as the separatists  trial opened, with about 6,000 people gathering in Pla a de Catalunya while some protesters blocked highways and set piles of tires on fire. Further demonstrations are planned in Catalonia on Saturday, February 16, with at least thousands likely to turn out for weekend mobilizations. 
 
	 Background  
 
	Catalonian independence has been a highly divisive issue for years, though it has not been characterized by the same levels of violence and terrorism as previous decades of Basque separatism. Pro-independence supporters in Catalonia regularly mobilize to push for their demands, with exceptionally large demonstrations capable of attracting more than 100,000 participants, with smaller demonstrations across the region. Pro-unity demonstrations within Catalonia are less frequent and typically not reaching the same participation levels, though the October 2017 independence referendum mobilized supporters of both sides. While Madrid has typically seen the largest pro-unity demonstrations, the 2017 referendum spurred demonstrations in cities and towns across the country. 
 
	Although Spain has held three general elections in less than four years, the failure of a government budget bill in congress is only the second such instance since 1975, when fascist dictator Francisco Franco died. Sanchez came to power in June 2018 following the vote of no confidence that ejected former Prime Minister Rajoy. In 2016, Spain held a general election triggered by the failure for any parties to form a government following elections in 2015, the first such instance in Spanish history. Rajoy was able to reclaim the office of the prime minister in 2016 following the PSOE s decision to abstain from voting on the formation of a new government   a choice taken to prevent a third election being called amidst political gridlock.  
	 Assessment  
 
	Pro-independence efforts in Catalonia pose a continuing challenge and point of controversy in Spain, and debates over separatism and degrees of autonomy are likely to be prominent in the upcoming election. As parties compete for seats in parliament with an eye to the potential formation of a ruling coalition, given the likely event no single party secures an absolute majority, smaller parties may prove crucial to getting sufficient numbers to be able to form a government. However, as seen in the recent legislative results and protest last weekend, there is a risk of backlash over the consideration of any concessions to Catalonia, even in spite of a refusal to consider a legally recognized referendum. The pro-unity demonstration in Madrid last Sunday was exceptional for the PP leader s appearance with the Vox leader, despite past efforts by the more center-right party to maintain distance from any associations with the growing far-right party. The development could signal that PP may attempt to retake power with the support of Vox, uniting on issues such as the shared opposition to Catalan independence. 
 
	Vox has been gaining support around the country, including winning seats in Andalusia s regional elections in December that resulted in Vox providing the backing for the PP to claim sufficient support to have a ruling coalition. Post-Franco Spain has not previously had a substantial resurgence of far-right parties in the political sphere; however, the small but growing Vox reflects a broader trend in Europe of populist, nationalist platforms gaining support and challenging established parties. Vox is not expected to jump to the head of polls nationally, though it could be seen as a potential junior partner or coalition faction to shore up a ruling majority in parliament. As well as being staunchly opposed to Catalan independence, Vox backs an array of controversial views, including on issues such as immigration and women s rights. 
 
	The far-right Vox has already been the focus of protests, including by anti-fascists and feminists. As the party seeks to gain a stronger national footing in the April election, its events around the country are likely to draw protests. Such demonstrations could result in clashes between opposing groups, clashes with authorities, and other unruly actions such as property damage. Demonstrations regarding Catalan independence, both for and against, also carry the potential for clashes, though such incidents typically involve fringe elements. Developments in the trial of Catalan officials in Madrid will continue to spur both planned and spontaneous demonstrations. Pro-independence organizers in Catalonia have also called sectoral and general strikes in the past to draw attention to their cause and protest grievances. Such labor actions are capable of causing substantial disruption, and often coincide with protest activity seeking to block highways and key roads as well as concentrating outside of government buildings. It is advised to exercise caution and avoid demonstration activity when possible due to the risk of incidents of unrest. Demonstrations are likely to have an increased police presence monitoring developments and localized disruptions are possible. Furthermore, although no specific, credible threat is known at this time, there is an ongoing heightened threat of jihadist terrorism in Spain and around Europe. The risk of extremists targeting crowds of people, including demonstrators, cannot be ruled out. Resilience360 customers are advised to maintain increased situational awareness, particularly in crowded and high-profile locations, and to report suspicious behavior or items to local authorities.

Headline: Counter-fuel theft campaign leaves 60+ tankers stranded at Mexican ports
Details: Local media sources indicate on January 11 that the counter-fuel theft campaign launched across Mexico has left over 60 tankers stranded outside the country's ports due to inability to unload. There are 31 outside Veracruz, 9 outside Tuxpan, and the remainder outside Altamira, Acapulco, Coatzacoalcos, Lázaro Cárdenas, Manzanillo, Salina Cruz, Tampico, Mazatlán, Guaymas, La Paz, Ensenada, and Campeche. The counter-fuel theft campaign involves the use of trucks as opposed to the previously favored pipelines, which were more theft-prone, yet allowed storage facilities to be quickly replenished at ports. The problem is anticipated to worsen, with more vessels arriving carrying 350,000-400,000 barrels and requiring USD 30,000-50,000 per day for operation. Those involved in the petroleum trade in Mexico should anticipate worsening delays at the ports and should plan accordingly.

Details: Updated industry sources indicate on November 19 that due to the recent factors, such as bad weather, abnormal increases in volume throughput, terminal productivity with additional measures taken to be COVID-19 secure, and transport shortages, carriers are currently experiencing congestion in the berthing plan and container yard for all Marine Terminals at London Gateway Port. Various efforts and actions at the terminals are reportedly ongoing to improve the situation, but the congestion is expected to continue until the end of December. Shipping sources reported that more ocean carriers will impose congestion surcharges on cargo shipped to and from London Gateway due to ongoing congestion issues. Hapag-Lloyd previously announced a surcharge of EUR 175 per TEU for cargo from Far East Asia to London Gateway from November 15. In addition, CMA CGM will impose a surcharge of USD 100 per TEU for cargo from and to Australia and New Zealand from November 30 and from and to the Indian subcontinent, the Middle East, and the Red Sea from November 15.

Headline: US Consulate General in Chennai Issued a Weather Alert About Forecast Tropical Cyclone
Details:
On Monday, the US Consulate General in Chennai issued the following Weather Alert:



“Location:   Puducherry, Tamil Nadu



Event:   A tropical depression in the Bay of Bengal is expected to strengthen into a tropical cyclone (Tropical Cyclone Nivar), making landfall in Tamil Nadu by November 25, 2020. According to local weather sources, such as the Regional Specialized Meteorological Centre for Tropical Cyclones Over North Indian Ocean (http://www.rsmcnewdelhi.imd.gov.in/index.php?lang=en), heavy rains may begin as early as November 24, 2020.  The cyclone is expected to move north and west, along the coast.  There is an increased risk of heavy rainfall, flooding and high winds for both coastal and inland locations.  Internet service, landline phone and cell phone capabilities may be affected.



U.S. Consulate General Chennai staff members have been asked to defer non-essential travel and to make preparations should sheltering-in-place or relocation become necessary.



Consulate Operations:  The U.S. Consulate General Chennai will be closed to the public for visa, U.S. citizen and foreign commercial services on Wednesday, November 25, 2020, due to the effects of likely heavy wind and rain, and is closed on Thursday, November 26, 2020, due to the Thanksgiving holiday.  The Consulate is currently scheduled to re-open to the public on Friday, November 27, 2020.



Actions to Take:



Monitor local media for weather updates.

Seek secure shelter.

Have evacuation plans that do not rely on U.S. government assistance.

Notify friends and family of your safety.”



The full text of the alert can be viewed here: https://in.usembassy.gov/weather-alert-tropical-cyclone-development-november-23-2020/

Headline: US District Court for Central California judge orders halt to offshore fracking
Details: Local media sources indicate on November 14 that a federal judge on the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California ruled the week prior that 38 operators of active leases on the Pacific Outer Continental Shelf must halt offshore hydraulic fracturing until the federal permit-issuing agencies complete an impact review on Santa Barbara, Ventura, and Los Angeles Counties, as well as consult with the Fish and Wildlife Serice, National Marine Fisheries Service, and the California Coastal Commission. The judge also issued an injunction prohibiting two federal agencies from approving plans or permits for the use of well stimulation treatments off the California coast. The injunction comes from an alleged violation of the Endangered Species Act and the Coastal Zone Management Act. Those conducting business with exploratory ventures in the aforementioned California counties should be mindful of the ruling and should plan accordingly.

Headline: Clan del Golfo Announces Unilateral Holiday Ceasefire, Intentions to Bolster its Presence in Cities
Details:
On Saturday, the right-wing Clan del Golfo paramilitary group issued a public communiqu . In the message, the group proclaimed that it would observe a unilateral ceasefire across all of Colombia throughout the holiday season, extending from December 8th, 2018, through January 10th, 2019. However, the militant group also announced that it plans to bolster its presence in all of the country s departmental capitals  from now on.  The message did not contain any specific details regarding particular locations or plans of action. 
	 
	Assessment: Members of Clan del Golfo generally refer to the organization as the  Gaitanista Self-Defense Forces of Colombia  or  AGC.  The paramilitary group is heavily involved in drug trafficking, extortion, and other forms of criminal activity. It remains embroiled in violent turf wars with other gangs and militant groups. In recent years, Clan del Golfo militants have carried out assassination campaigns against police officers, and so-called  armed strikes  that have been intended to paralyze commerce through broad threats of violence levied against the public. In early July of this year, during the final days of the Juan Manuel Santos administration, the former president announced that Clan del Golfo s leaders had agreed to collectively surrender to the government in exchange for reduced sentences. However, the deal never came to fruition, and incumbent President Iv n Duque continues to maintain a more hardline stance in his approach to the country s various subversive militant groups. 
	 
	While the number of Clan del Golfo attacks against security forces has fallen significantly in recent months, it appears highly unlikely that the group plans to demobilize any time in the foreseeable future. Furthermore, if the organization moves forward with its plans to broaden its presence in major cities across the country, new turf wars could potentially arise with local criminal organizations. Resilience360 advises customers with interests in Colombia to stay abreast of associated developments.

Headline: UPDATE 1 - Mainland China strengthens political influence over private enterprises, increasing scope for state-directed management and investment decisions
Details: The General Office of the Chinese Communist Party (CPC) on 17 September released a document entitled “Opinions regarding strengthening of united front work for the private sector economy in the new era”. The proposals seek to strengthen the CPC’s “political guidance”, “communication mechanism”, and “party building” in private-sector enterprises.Mainland China’s Anbang Insurance Group has formally sought banking and insurance regulator approval to be disbanded and liquidated, two years after being placed under state control.Greg Baker/AFP via Getty ImagesThe document indicates that party influence will strengthen in terms of aligning corporate managerial and investment decisions more closely with the CPC’s political goals. The new directive highlighted the need for a private sector that is “reliable and dependable at critical moments”. The proposals seek to “educate and guide” private companies to “adopt Xi Jinping Thought”, as well as to “maintain a high degree of consistency” with the party’s core objectives and to be “politically sensible”. The directive indicates that there will be stronger influence over corporate management, either through party cells or via direct control by local government or regulatory authorities. This is likely to include measures to reflect government directives through increased hiring to support employment, investing in unprofitable but strategically important sectors or countries, and using company resources to support government initiatives. The document also emphasised that “all private enterprises and private economic individuals” would be included under its remit, particularly highlighting Hong Kong SAR and Macao SAR-based businesses that have investments on the mainland. It is highly likely that this approach also will extend to Taiwanese and foreign companies with significant exposure in China, especially those under joint venture (JV) agreements. This is particularly likely to affect businesses closely affiliated with Chinese business federations, members of the National People's Congress, and the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, who will act as enforcers of party decisions. The timing of the policy release indicates concerns over fiscal difficulties – particularly at the local level – and expectations that the private sector should support local authorities in implementing livelihood and stability-promoting measures. The economic impact of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and the global economic downturn has reduced the revenue base for local governments. The Ministry of Finance has reported that, between January and July 2020, national general public budget revenue decreased by 8.7% year on year (y/y) – a larger decrease than expenditure, which fell by 3.2%. The fiscal deficit stood at CNY1.88 trillion (USD278 billion), a CNY640-billion y/y increase. On 29 August, a state-affiliated public account on WeChat named “Banyuetan” highlighted that declining local government revenue has affected economic recovery and improvement in livelihoods, particularly at the “grassroots” (below county) level. Strong CPC influence over private companies would further increase sanction risks from the US and US-allied countries. Article 7 of China’s National Intelligence Law mandates Chinese companies to “support, assist and cooperate in national intelligence work”. A key driver of ongoing US efforts to sanction Chinese companies is national security concerns over the firms’ alleged connections with the Chinese leadership. Prior to the White House’s decision to block social media application TikTok, owned by Chinese company ByteDance, US Secretary of State Mike Pompeo highlighted concerns over the company’s connection to the CPC and the possibility of Chinese government access to data on US citizens. Similar measures were also adopted in India, and are under discussion in US-allied countries such as Australia. (TikTok has denied the US’s claims.) Stronger CPC influence over business decisions will increase the likelihood of additional Chinese companies being placed on US sanctions lists – such as through the Department of Commerce’s Entity List – particularly within sectors that provide civilian and military dual-use technology such as semiconductors, companies emerging as global market leaders in areas such as social media and software development, and industries relevant to national security. Indicators of changing risk environment Increasing risk Indications of further diplomatic disagreement, such as an unsuccessful EU-China investment agreement negotiation or Western governments taking strong positions against China in issues related to human rights or COVID-19 origins, would further increase China’s threat perception and thus accelerate its measures to increase control over its domestic resources. This would also increase the likelihood of localised military conflict in disputed regions, particularly around the Taiwan Strait but also within the South China Sea and regions bordering India. Signals of slowing economic recovery during the coming winter months – including a significant fall in real estate prices, wider fluctuations in exchange rates or a devaluation of the yuan, signs of local governments being unable to pay civil servants, increasing unemployment, or acceleration of growth in food prices – would indicate a likelihood of increased local government pressure seeking to mobilise private-sector resources.Decreasing risk Economic recovery above expectations would indicate positive prospects for improving government revenue. IHS Markit currently projects a 2020 growth rate of 1.69% for China. The election of a Democratic administration in the US November 2020 presidential election might delay US targeting of Chinese companies based on national security or human rights grounds, as a new administration and Congress would be likely to focus first on domestic priorities, thus reducing international pressure on the Chinese government. © 2020, IHS Markit Inc. Headline: Heightened Risk of Protests in Guinea as President Alpha Conde Hints at Possible Third Term
Details:
Over the last few days, tensions have been rising across Guinea over President Alpha Conde s hints at a possible third term in office. Rumors that President Conde may seek to amend the constitution to run for a third term began to swirl last year and gained steam earlier this week after a video began circulating online in which he called on Guinean expatriates to prepare for a referendum. Although Conde has yet to confirm the rumors officially, they have nonetheless sparked a number of protests across the country in recent months, several of which have resulted in clashes with police, injuries, and arrests. The potential for additional protests and unrest is likely to run high over the coming days and weeks, particularly on Saturday, which will also mark the tenth anniversary of the September 28, 2009 massacre, when security forces killed over 150 demonstrators during a rally in Conakry.

Recent Developments

On Monday night, a video emerged on social media in which President Conde called on his supporters to prepare for a referendum. The video was filmed during a meeting with members of the Guinean expatriate community in New York and featured Conde discussing some of the projects he has undertaken during his two terms in office, including the building of the Souapiti Dam. At the end of the nearly 30-minute video, which was allegedly broadcast live, Conde stated,  I ask you to get organized and prepare for a referendum and elections.  No further details on the proposed referendum or election were immediately provided and Conde did not explicitly confirm that he will seek a third term. 

Nonetheless, the video has fueled rumors that Conde may seek to amend the constitution either to remove term limits or simply reset them, allowing him to run for additional terms, and has been met with resistance from opposition parties. The vice president of the main opposition party, the Union of Democratic Forces of Guinea (UFDG), has deemed it a  constitutional coup d etat,  while another opposition party, the Guinea Standing Party (PGD), denounced it as a  provocation  and announced plans to meet with another party to prepare a response. There were also reports of several localized protests in Tougue and Lelouma on Thursday and Friday, but no clashes, injuries, or arrests were immediately indicated.

Background

President Conde was elected into office in 2010 in Guinea s first-ever democratic election since it gained independence from France in 1958. He was re-elected for a second five-year term in 2015 amidst allegations of fraud and vote rigging. His second term is expected to expire in October 2020 and he is currently constitutionally barred from seeking another term in office. Despite the constitutional cap on presidential terms, rumors began to swirl last year that he may seek another term in office, a move that would require either a constitutional referendum or consent from two-thirds of parliament. The rumors first emerged around September 2018, when the head of Guinea s Constitutional Court, Kelefa Sall, was removed from office. Sall was widely considered the last remaining opposition voice on the court and had previously called on Conde to respect the two-term limit. Many opposition activists deemed his removal a critical step to pave the way for constitutional amendments. The rumors resurfaced earlier this year when the Russian ambassador to Guinea issued a speech in support of Conde seeking a third term, and a memo from the foreign affairs minister on potential amendments was leaked online. There have also been reports that billboards and banners have been erected across Conakry calling for a new constitution.

The rumors of a possible third term have sparked a series of localized protests across Guinea over the last year, several of which have resulted in clashes with security forces. Notably in June 2019, at least 28 people were injured in clashes between security forces and opposition activists in the southern city of Nzerekore. Additional protests have been reported in Conakry, Macenta, Coyah, Tanene, Boffa, Siguiri, Kankan, and Faranah, largely in April and May of 2019. While most have been peaceful, a ban on protests has remained in effect since July 2018 and security forces have responded with tear gas and batons during some demonstrations and arrested a number of demonstrators. In addition to launching protests, opposition groups formed a joint coalition earlier this year against any constitutional changes titled the National Front for the Defense of the Constitution (FNDC). The coalition is comprised of opposition parties, unions, and civil society groups.Assessment

The latest video has not only fueled the rumors of a possible third term for Conde, but has also likely further galvanized the opposition movement and could raise the risk of protests and unrest over the coming days and weeks. Protests are most likely to occur in opposition strongholds, such as the Middle Guinea region, as well as parts of Conakry, but could occur anywhere. The demonstrations are likely to take place with little to no warning in an effort to skirt the ban on demonstration and prevent police from breaking them up. Nonetheless, the potential for clashes and unrest is likely to remain high, as security forces have a history of responding with force to any opposition gatherings. 

The risk of protests could be particularly high on Saturday, September 28, which marks the tenth anniversary of the September 2009 massacre. The massacre, which left at last 156 people dead and over 100 women and girls raped and sexually assaulted, occurred as security forces stormed the national stadium in Conakry, where opposition activists were holding a rally against coup leader Moussa Dadis Camara s plans to run for office after he had pledged to step down. Although 13 suspects have been arrested in connection with the massacre, they have yet to go to trial and demonstrations to demand justice for those killed cannot be ruled out. Opposition parties could seek to piggyback on any demonstrations or use it as a rallying cry against Conde and his government s alleged repression. 

Additionally, the risk of protests and unrest could rise if a date for the planned referendum is set or if Conde confirms his plans to seek another term in office. As such, Resilience360 customers with interests in Guinea are advised to monitor developments related to the referendum and maintain a heightened level of vigilance over the coming days and weeks. Particular caution should be exercised near government buildings and public gathering places, especially on Saturday, September 28. Additionally, all protest-related activity, rallies, and large crowds should be avoided due to the potential for violence.
