Headline: UPDATE 1 - Australia unlikely to directly retaliate against mainland China’s targeted measures; foreign policy position also unlikely to change
Details: According to Chinese and international media reports, Chinese traders have received an informal notice from authorities that Australian products in seven categories – barley, sugar, lobster, wine, timber, coal, and copper ore and concentrate – will not be cleared in customs from 6 November. The Chinese government has denied that there are any restrictions on Australian commodities, and the implementation of the notice has yet to be confirmed. Australian exporters have nevertheless already cancelled shipments to China and Chinese traders have cancelled orders.The timing and extent of Chinese action against Australian imports give credibility to recent media reporting that this reflects Chinese government policy and not just buyers’ commercial decisions. China-Australia relations have deteriorated significantly in recent months, particularly after the Australian government called for an independent inquiry into the origins of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) in April. Beginning in May, Chinese authorities imposed a series of restrictions on Australian imports, ostensibly due to alleged breaches of trade practices (resulting in tariffs on barley) or quality issues found during routine product inspections (affecting some shipments of beef, barley, lobster, and timber). On 9 October, there were reports that some Chinese ports had been told not to accept Australian coal. Although coal import quotas are not uncommon, this came days after a meeting between foreign ministers of the recently revived Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad) nations, comprising Australia, India, Japan, and the United States. China has previously labelled the Quad as an “Asian NATO” (see Australia-India-Japan-US:2 October 2020: Future of Australia-India-Japan-US Quad dialogue and maritime security in the Indo-Pacific). Australian Trade Minister Simon Birmingham has accused China of taking “discriminatory action” against Australia in imposing import restrictions. China has repeatedly denied any targeting of Australia, stating that reduced imports were the result of buyers’ decisions.Given its vulnerability to wider Chinese discrimination against Australian imports, the Australian government is unlikely to retaliate. According to the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, China accounted for 32.6% (AUD153.2 billion, or USD111.1 billion) of its total goods and services exports in the financial year ending 2019. According to China’s National Bureau of Statistics, Australia in 2019 only accounted for 1.9% of mainland Chinese exports globally and 3.8% of mainland China’s exports to the Asia-Pacific and Oceania regions. This indicates that, while China has scope to extend restrictions on other Australian imports, Australia is unlikely to respond in reciprocal measures and equivalent degree. Rather, the Australian government will probably increase conciliatory advances towards China, notably through public statements on the importance of the bilateral relationship. The government is also likely to rein in backbenchers, both within the Liberal-National coalition and the Labor Party opposition, who frequently criticise China publicly. In addition, Australia will probably refrain from taking a prominent role in any further international initiatives challenging China, as it did in April when it led an international call for a COVID-19 inquiry. Repeated Chinese import restrictions are unlikely to result in Australian reversal on foreign policy issues challenged by China, however. Although Australia will avoid taking a prominent role in future international initiatives against China, its participation in the ongoing India-Japan-US Malabar naval exercise this month indicates that the Australian government is unlikely to reverse core policies that are at odds with China. This includes Australia’s commitment to the Quad grouping and its stance on issues such as Hong Kong SAR and the South China Sea. Participation in the current Malabar exercise contrasts with the last time Australia took part in 2007: China’s negative response resulted in the government of then-prime minister Kevin Rudd withdrawing from the exercises and accompanying security talks, resulting in the dissolution of the Quad. Nevertheless, given its economic vulnerability vis-à-vis China, Australia will probably seek to adjust its approach to the Quad and other regional defence activities by minimising its profile. Indicators of changing risk environmentIncreasing riskIf November and December 2020 shipments of Australian coal continue to show signs of regulatory targeting indicated by significant congestions in major ports in mainland China, this would further signal worsening bilateral relationships due to Beijing’s evident refusal to lift restrictions on Australian coal during the winter months – traditionally a period of higher power consumption and coal demand.If China imposes import restrictions or heightens regulatory barriers against Australian iron ore, this would indicate a significant worsening of bilateral relations. In 2019, 62% of China’s iron ore imports came from Australia. The economic cost of Chinese targeting of iron ore would likely be disproportionally borne in China’s infrastructure sector, which remains important in its investment-led economic recovery and relies on an inexpensive and stable supply of steel. Targeted measures against iron ore would indicate both a long-term policy shift of trade diversion from Australia to alternative markets for raw materials as well as intent to significantly damage the Australian economy, given that iron ore is Australia’s largest export to China.The passage into law of draft Australian federal legislation affecting foreign, particularly Chinese, commercial interests in Australia – likely in January 2021 (see Australia:8 June 2020: Proposed changes to Australia’s foreign investment rules likely to target Chinese investors, increasing risk of forced divestments and Australia:4 September 2020: Australia’s proposed legislation on agreements between states/territories and foreign governments indicates increased likelihood of state contract cancellation) – would be a further indicator of the trajectory of relations between Australia and China. Any amendments targeting Chinese interests more explicitly would probably result in a further deterioration of relations, increasing the likelihood of further restrictions on Australian goods and services or other targeted measures against Australian assets.Decreasing riskDirect talks between either Australian Prime Minister Scott Morrison and Chinese President Xi Jinping or their respective foreign ministers would increase the likelihood of an improvement in relations.Any delays or a government reversal on passing the draft legislation affecting Chinese interests would slightly decrease the likelihood of further Chinese restrictions on Australian products, as long as Australia avoids further high-profile diplomatic confrontations with China.© 2020, IHS Markit Inc. Headline: Philippines: Tropical Depression Samuel to bring heavy rain to Visayas and Mindanao areas
Details: PAGASA, the national weather bureau, has confirmed that heavy rain will impact Visayas and Mindanao areas from Monday evening as a tropical depression travels towards land. Samuel entered the Philippine Area of Responsibility on Sunday morning and is currently east southeast of Surigao del Sur, with sustained winds of 55kph. The storm has the potential to unleash floods and landslides in Caraga, Davao Oriental and Compostela Valley regions starting Monday. Outer rain bands of the current depression will impact Metro Manila. Travellers are advised to heed to any instructions from the authorities and exercise caution when travelling in adverse weather conditions.

Headline: Germany: Greenpeace target vehicle terminal at Bremerhaven

The loading ramp has also been targeted. Another vessel docked at the terminal is also said to contain hundreds more BMW and Mercedes vehicles. Greenpeace claim that these cars are significantly more harmful to the climate than other cars due to their heavy weight and their large engines. Greenpeace also acknowledge that these vehicles will be showcased at the Frankfurt motor show, although it is not known if Greenpeace will target the show alongside other activist groups.

Headline: ZIM to fine shippers for misdeclared hazardous cargoes
Details: Industry sources indicate on September 3 that Haifa-based ZIM Integrated Shipping Services announced its intent to implement a penalty of USD 12,000 (EUR 10,800) per container for misdeclared or undeclared hazardous cargoes, with a definitive fine quantity unknown as of reporting, and it is unknown when this penalty will come into effect. ZIM will hold the customer on record liable and responsible for costs and consequences related to violations, fines, damages, incidents, claims and corrective measures resulting from cases of shipment of such cargo. The move is similar to that implemented by other cargo shipping lines in the aftermath of the Yantian Express fire.

Headline: US Embassy Issues Weather Alert
Details:
On Thursday, the United States Embassy in Muscat issued a Weather Alert for US citizens in Oman regarding Tropical Cyclone Luban. The alert reads in part: 
 
	 Location: Southern Oman; possible heavy rains and wind. 
 
	Event: Tropical Cyclone Luban continues to strengthen as it moves westward toward the coastal areas of Dhofar governorate and Yemen.  The storm is still not expected to make landfall in Oman, but heavy rain and strong winds are expected to affect Dhofar and Al Wusta governorates beginning October 13.  The Port of Salalah has temporarily suspended operations in anticipation of rough seas and strong winds.  
 
	Assessment: Although southwestern Oman and, to a lesser extent, parts of southern Saudi Arabia are likely to be impacted by the storm, the primary effects will be felt in Yemen, particularly the governorates of al-Mahra and Hadramaut. In addition to rough seas along the coast, the predicted winds and rainfall raise the risk of flash flooding and mudslides in these areas, as well as on the island of Socotra, which Luban is forecast to skirt on Friday. Resilience360 customers should note that heavy rainfall can be dangerous in dry environments such as Yemen, as  wadis , or dry river valleys, can overflow and cause human casualties, as well as damage to poorly-built structures. Power outages and difficult travel conditions should also be anticipated in the coming days. 
 
	To view the Weather Alert in its entirety, please click the following URL:  https://om.usembassy.gov/weather-alert-u-s-embassy-muscat-oman-october-11-2018/

Headline: US Embassy Issued a Weather Alert on Tropical Cyclone Season Preparations
Details:
On Tuesday, the US Embassy in Singapore issued the following Weather Alert:



“Location:  Pacific Ocean and Indian Ocean



Event:  Tropical Cyclone Season in the South Pacific Ocean began November 1, 2020 and ends on April 30, 2021.  The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) recommends that those in tropical cyclone-prone regions begin preparations for the upcoming season now.



Actions to Take:



Visit the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s (NOAA) Climate Prediction Center (https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/) for the 2021 Cyclone forecast.

Visit the Department of State’s Hurricanes, Typhoons, and Cyclones page (https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/international-travel/emergencies/what-can-you-do-crisis-abroad/tropical-storm-season.html).

Have evacuation plans that do not rely on U.S. government assistance. For more information see: https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/international-travel/before-you-go/your-health-abroad/insurance-providers-overseas.html”



The full text of the alert can be viewed here: https://sg.usembassy.gov/weather-alert-u-s-embassy-singapore/

Headline: Tanker damaged and partially submerged following rock strike in Singapore Strait
Details: Maritime media sources indicate that a Saint Kitts & Nevis registered tanker (Name Sea Frontier, IMO 8911126) is partially submerged 2 nautical miles off of Tanjung Penyusop in Malaysia, east of Singapore. The ship is believed to be carrying cargo, but the specific contents are unknown.

Headline: Bush Fires around Sydney Could Impact Water Supplies in New South Wales State
Details:
On Friday, it was reported that firefighters are prioritizing the protection of water infrastructure, such as plants, pumping stations, and pipes from the bush fires that are burning around Sydney, New South Wales (NSW) State. The recent fires have threatened supplies in the Warragamba and in the Blue Mountains areas. Lake Burragorang, which supplies around 80 percent of Sydney s water by way of the Warragamba Dam, has been almost completely encircled by bush fires. Officials have said that critical infrastructure for water supplies has not yet been damaged by the fires.

Assessment: The fires can impact water supplies through two methods, either through direct damage to infrastructure or ash from fires contaminating waterways. Sydney is already under Level 2 water restrictions due to the ongoing drought, which limits the watering of gardens, lawns, and other uses of water. Information about the restrictions can be found here: https://www.sydneywater.com.au/SW/water-the-environment/what-we-re-doing/water-restrictions/index.htm. While there have not been any immediate impacts to overall water supplies due to the fires, customers in NSW are advised to closely monitor the situation, as unexpected damages to infrastructure or contamination of supplies could result in rationing and other disruptions.

Headline: Magnitude 5.3 earthquake reported 17 km west of Nasugbu, Batangas Province
Details:
The United States Geological Survey (USGS) has confirmed that a 5.3 magnitude earthquake has occurred 17 km west of Nasugbu. The quake was reported at a depth of 86 km and no information on structural damage or injuries has been announced. 
USGS (United States Geological Survey) is a scientific agency of the U.S. government which monitors earthquake activity worldwide. USGS earthquake alerts are assessed primarily using the moment magnitude (Mw) scale. However, local magnitude (ML), surface-wave magnitude (Ms) or body-wave magnitude (Mb) may be used in lieu of the Mw scale. All magnitude scales should yield approximately the same value for any given earthquake.

Headline: Malaysian customs to revoke importers' licenses for false declarations
Details: According to sources on March 1, the customs officials of Malaysia have announced that it would use the Customs Act authority to strip off the licenses of any freight forwarders whom are found to import cigarettes, liquor, tiles, plastic waste and tyres under a false declaration. The strict measures were put in place to alleviate illegal smuggling activities especially for the five items. In the past two weeks, licenses of five agents have already been revoked for making false declarations; this includes four cases of importing plastic wastes and another case of cigarettes. The regulatory measures have been enforced at a time when Malaysia is taking serious actions to curb plastic wastes. Around 140 containers of garbage and plastic waste have been stranded at Port Klang while Penang Port had more than 200 containers of similar items.  The new regulation will encourage all shippers to be aware of the real items in the containers through the declaration form.

Headline: UPDATE: Hanwha Total restarts Daesan naptha cracker after workers strike
Details: Updated media reports indicated on June 19 that South Korean petrochemical producer Hanwha Total yesterday restarted its 1.09 million tons per year Daesan-based naphtha cracker. Hanwha Total continued maintenance on the cracker from March 27, amid a workers' strike that ran from March 23 to May 28. The maintenance was supposed to end on May 6, but the restart of the cracker and its derivative units were delayed by the strike and a lack of manpower. Hanwha Total had been preparing to return to normal operations since the strike ended but needed more time than usual to restart the cracker because of the extended shutdown. The producer had also failed several times to restart the cracker since attempts were first made on June 8. Hanwha Total then attempted to restart the unit yesterday and was able to produce on-specification ethylene. It now plans to slowly ramp up operations. Previous media sources indicated on May 8 that a restart of Hanwha Total's Daesan-based cracker continues to be delayed by a labour union strike after workers went on a general strike over a pay increase on March 23 after negotiations with management broke down. Hanhwa Total is a petrochemical company that manufactures building block chemicals that are used to produce other chemicals needed to make various consumer product.

In addition, the four eastern provinces of Chon Buri, Rayong, Chanthaburi and Trat, as well as six southern provinces of Ranong, Phang Nga, Phuket, Krabi, Trang and Satun are under strong wind/waves warnings; small boats have been prohibited from sailing during the next 1-2 days.

Headline: Climate Marches Planned across the Region on 3/15; Largest Actions in Australia and New Zealand

The largest actions appear to be taking place in Australia s Sydney and Melbourne, as well as Auckland in New Zealand. 
 
	 
		Assessment: The protests are under the banner of a Global Climate Strike For Future, which is a part of the Fridays For Future movement that has been active for months. Given the history of past climate demonstrations, the protests on Friday are largely expected to be peaceful, although localized transportation disruptions are likely to occur in areas where large demonstrations are taking place. In addition, they are not packing any clothing that could be construed as the attire of the protesters, for example black clothing.

Headline: Boxship attacked by pirates in Gulf of Guinea
Details: Industry sources reported that perpetrators tried to board the boxship ""Kota Satria"" while the vessel was sailing in the Gulf of Guinea on February 21, 2019. More than four men armed with guns onboard an unlit fast boat attempted to board the vessel. Two of the perpetrators attempted to hook a ladder to ship’s hull. However, they were not successful and slowed down the pursuit. The perpetrators then fired two gunshots toward the ship’s bridge and subsequently to the ship’s accommodation. The master initiated security procedures and contacted the company security officer as well as the company’s armed escort vessel and the Nigerian Navy and carried out evasive maneuver. Consequently, the fast boat aborted the pursuit. There were no injuries to the ship’s crew and no damage to the vessel reported. In addition, no items were stolen. Following the incident, the ship met an armed escort ship and proceeded to the port of Onne where it berthed on February 22 and sailed on February 28, bound to Singapore, ETA March 27.

Headline: U.S. Embassy in Panama City Issues Health Alert Regarding COVID-19
Details:
On Friday, the U.S. Embassy in Panama City issued a Health Alert for American citizens in Panama. The message reads, in part:



“Event: Remembering 9/11 and Announcing Changes to Movement Restrictions Beginning September 14



The American flag is flying at half-staff today. Please take time to watch this video and remember those we lost in the attacks of 9/11.



On August 25, the Government of Panama announced plans to reduce movement restrictions and open up additional economic sectors, starting on September 7. The plan is conditional upon meeting certain criteria regarding the control of the COVID-19 pandemic in Panama.



On September 7 the Government of Panama opened the following economic sectors: Construction and related activities (engineers, architects, project managers, contractors, moving services), Panama Pacifico, Colon Free Zone and other free trade zones, private ship docks and sports fishing, tailor shops, shoe shops, and carwashes will resume operations.



On September 14, the following changes in movement restrictions will be implemented: Gender-based movement restrictions are lifted and ‘salvoconductos’ become null and void, except for those occupations that require movement during curfew hours. Curfew will be from 11pm to 5am, Monday through Saturday. Sundays will remain days of total quarantine.”



The Health Alert can be viewed in its entirety (along with embedded hyperlinks) at the following URL: https://pa.usembassy.gov/health-alert-u-s-embassy-panama-city-panama-september-11-2020/.

Headline: Chinese firm's criminal charges will not trigger arbitrary detainment of US...
Details: Risks: Individuals Sectors or assets affected: US nationals in ChinaOn 29 January, the US Justice Department filed criminal charges against China's Huawei Technologies, its alleged affiliates, and its chief financial officer Meng Wanzhou for alleged bank fraud, wire fraud, and obstruction of justice. Meng will be extradited from Canada if Canadian courts are satisfied that there is sufficient evidence for her to stand trial. Meng and Huawei maintain their innocence. China's foreign ministry spokesman at its US embassy criticised the case as politically motivated but did not threaten ""repercussions"", unlike the Chinese envoy and ambassador to Canada, who have repeatedly issued such threats against Canada. Several Canadian nationals have been detained in China following the arrest of Meng in Vancouver, Canada, in early December 2018. Meanwhile, China's Vice Premier Liu He has arrived in Washington, DC to begin a new round of trade negotiations with US officials led by US Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer. The US and Chinese governments have emphasised that the trade negotiations and the criminal investigation of Huawei are separate issues; the two sides aim to reach a settlement by 1 March that prevents the US's 24 September round of tariffs on USD200 billion-worth of Chinese imports rising from 10% to 25%. China's official news agency, Xinhua, reported on 30 January that the Chinese government intended to pass new legislation relating to foreign investment in its annual National People's Congress in early March. The new rules will prohibit local-level Chinese government officials from 'forcing' the transfer of intellectual property from foreign to local entities engaged in joint ventures; such transfers are a central complaint of the US Trade Representative's office in its Section 301 report.Significance: US nationals are not at increased risk of arbitrary detention in China as long as the 24 September tariffs are maintained at 10%. A breakdown in trade negotiations, however, would increase the risk specifically to current or former US federal officials working in either State, Defense, or intelligence services, and to rights activists or those with links to activists; the risk would not be indiscriminate across US nationals in general. US nationals facing ongoing criminal investigations would also see their cases opportunistically prioritised by Chinese courts. Clear threats of 'repercussions' by Chinese officials in the US would be a secondary indicator of increasing risk to US nationals in China. Headline: Tugboat operators at the Port of Algeciras threaten strike over new regulation
Details: Tugboat operators at the Port of Algeciras in Cadiz have threatened to strike if an upcoming regulatory issue that is perceived to threaten their labor conditions is not resolved. Regulation 352/2017 of the European Union, which is set to go into effect on March 24, permits tugboats carrying international flags to operate in EU ports. France and Germany have already passed resolutions to restrict the flags of their ports, thereby protecting labor standards, but Spain has not. A specific timeline for the threatened strike is not yet known.

Headline: Congestion issues persist at Aomi container terminal in the Port of Tokyo - UPDATE 1
Details: Intelligence obtained by Everstream Analytics confirms that circumstances driving congestion at Aomi terminal in the Port of Tokyo (described below) persist. Previously on April 14, sources indicated that truckers continue to face waiting times to pick-up and deliver containers of more than 8 hours at the Aomi Terminal. Due to the congestion at the terminal, regardless of the availability of berth, vessels often need to wait on the water in the bay until terminals are ready to unload containers or entirely omit the port call. Headline: Residual Disruptions Possible as Post-Luban Cleanup Efforts Commence
Details:
On Monday, Omani media sources reported that cleanup efforts have begun after Tropical Cyclone Luban affected life in the sultanate over the weekend. According to local authorities, the storm caused heavy rainfall in Dhofar and Al Wusta governorates, particularly in the eastern and western portions of the former. In addition to a man who was found dead from the storm on Sunday, overland travel complications were reported in some areas after debris damaged local roadways. Additionally, authorities responded to minor power and telecommunication outages and quickly restored service to the majority of affected customers. All schools in Salalah and eastern Dhofar governorate were slated to resume on Monday. Meanwhile, in neighboring Yemen, where Luban made landfall, 50 families were in need of evacuation on Monday after their homes were flooded in Ghaida, al-Mahra governorate. Local authorities have also ordered the temporary closure of schools and government offices amid widespread power outages across Ghaida. 
 
	Assessment: While Luban weakened to a tropical depression on Sunday, periods of heavy rainfall were forecast to continue in parts of southwestern Oman and eastern Yemen until Monday morning. As such, the possibility of further disruptions, along with possible complications to cleanup efforts, cannot be ruled out in the coming days. Resilience360 customers in Oman and Yemen should stay abreast of local weather forecasts and enact security and financial contingency plans as necessary.

Headline: UPDATE 1 - US legal seizures of Venezuelan oil and fuel tankers increasingly likely, but US naval blockade remains improbable
Details: A US Texas court authorised on 31 August the selling of Iranian fuel that had been seized from vessels on their way to Venezuela. The event follows the US government’s confirmation on 13 August that it had seized through court procedures four vessels at sea, allegedly carrying Iranian fuel that were heading towards Venezuela; the vessels were diverted voluntarily to Houston to comply with the US authorities’ request and were not military intercepted. The United States also reported that another five Iranian-flagged tankers carrying Iranian fuel refused to comply and reached port in Venezuela on 24 May. The US Department of the Treasury had imposed sanctions on cargo transporting Venezuelan oil to Cuba, including on six oil tankers from PDVSA, in December 2019. The US has also blacklisted other vessels and shipping companies that facilitated oil exports in the past two years for PDVSA, including Russia’s Rosneft, which, according to US authorities, managed (before sanctions) 70% of Venezuelan oil sales.Significance: There is a high and rising risk that ships carrying fuel cargo to Venezuela will  face court-ordered seizure because of non-compliance with the US Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctions or as a result of US court orders relating to outstanding debt. Commercial vessels suspected by the US of transporting either Venezuelan oil exports or Iranian fuel heading towards Venezuela will also face similar risks. The rising likelihood of seizures is due to a combination of the US’s increasing pressure on Venezuela ahead of the November US presidential election and Venezuela’s increasing need to import fuel as shortages intensify because of falling refining capacity. The implications for non-compliance to US court orders are likely to include restrictions on conducting US-dollar transactions and accessing the US financial system, as well as restrictions on access to US and allied ports. The risk of a marine blockade, however, or of the US intercepting by force Venezuelan or Iran-flagged vessels, remains low. The deployment of US military ships, including aircraft carriers to the Caribbean, that go beyond those typically deployed for counter-narcotic efforts would suggest an increasing likelihood of the US considering seizing by force or blocking any further Iranian-flagged ships carrying fuel into Venezuela.Risks: Government instability; Regulatory burden; Inter-state war risksSectors or assets affected: Oil © 2020, IHS Markit Inc. Headline: 6 miles E of Kisante - Five killed and 70 injured in earthquake; buildings damaged. Incident closed.
Details: The U.S. Geological Survey reported that a magnitude 6.6 earthquake struck approximately six miles east of Kisante. At least five people died and up to 70 others were injured following the earthquake. The deaths were reported in Magsaysay, in Davao del Sur, Koronadal, in South Cotabato, and Arakan, in Cotabato, while 30 people were injured in Kidapawan City and 13 others were injured in M'lang. Additionally, reports indicate that several buildings sustained damages from the earthquake. The earthquake had a magnitude of 6.8. Multiple buildings were damaged in Davao City and Digos City, including the Felcris Centrale mall in Davao City and the Cor Jesu College building in Digos City. Two aftershocks were reported in the region, one with a magnitude of 5.0 and the other with a magnitude of 5.8. There were no reports of tsunami warnings. An unspecified number of people were evacuated from public buildings in Davao City, including the University of Mindanao, the Department of Agriculture in Region 11, and the San Pedro Hospital. This incident is closed.

Headline: UPDATE 2 - Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership signals a political achievement for mainland China, likely streamlining intra-Asian trade once ratified
Details: Member countries of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership sign the agreement at the virtual summit on 15 November 2020NHAC NGUYEN / Contributor/Getty ImagesFifteen Asian countries on 15 November signed the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP). The member countries include Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam – which together comprise the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) – as well as Australia, China, Japan, New Zealand, and South Korea. Once ratified, RCEP will form the world’s biggest trade agreement with a consumer market of 2.2 billion and a combined GDP of USD26.2 trillion, accounting for nearly 30% of global GDP. It requires nine member countries for ratification, of which six will be ASEAN members.Once ratified, RCEP is very likely to streamline and strengthen intra-Asian trade. The 15 RCEP members have several existing free trade agreements (FTAs) among themselves. RCEP will consolidate these arrangements and unify their various “rules of origin” provisions, seeking to streamline supply chains among member countries. Despite prolonged negotiations since 2012, the impetus to conclude RCEP stemmed from supply chain disruption caused by the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) virus pandemic and was facilitated by India’s exit in late 2019. The streamlining will strengthen intra-Asian trade. Asian Development Bank calculations in 2018 showed that about 60% of Asian trade is already conducted within Asia, compared with about 40% in North America and 65% in the European Union. However, RCEP’s impact is likely to be limited. On tariff reduction, several RCEP members are also signatories of the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP), a cross-continental free trade agreement that already seeks tariff elimination on 99% of traded goods. RCEP has a prolonged timeline ranging from 15 to 20 years for various provisions to be enacted. It differs from the TPP in that it does not include standards for environmental or labour protections, allowing for divergent regimes to continue among RCEP member countries.RCEP is a significant political achievement for the mainland Chinese leadership, but its economic benefits are likely to be limited over the next two years. The timing of RCEP’s signing suggests that China’s leadership is seeking to telegraph a political achievement ahead of the country’s 2022 leadership transition. The Chinese government also intends the agreement to be the basis for future trade negotiations, particularly the proposed China-Japan-South Korea trilateral FTA, which China is seeking to establish as an “RCEP-plus” free trade zone. Under RCEP, China will likely seek to expand exports to ASEAN countries, which would probably worsen ASEAN’s trade balance with China given RCEP’s mandate to introduce tariff reductions. Together with longstanding territorial disputes, domestic opposition against RCEP is likely. ASEAN countries reported a USD62-billion trade deficit in merchandise trade with mainland China in 2018, compared with RCEP’s 14 members’ USD147.2-billion trade surplus. Furthermore, two-thirds of China’s total trade with RCEP members are with US-allied countries, which are likely to experience deteriorating bilateral relations with China and therefore are more exposed to economic disputes. Furthermore, RCEP’s inclusion of e-commerce, intellectual property, and technological cooperation is likely in the one- to two-year outlook to favour market access in areas where China has a competitive advantage. These include advanced manufacturing, internet platforms, and telecommunication technology. However, this will almost certainly face a regional trend of higher taxation and investment barriers in these industries (see Asia-Pacific: 16 November: Asia-Pacific perceptions of mainland China and Asia-Pacific: 2 April 2019: IMF managing director urges co-ordinated approach to taxing technology multinationals in emerging markets; response appears slow-moving).RCEP consolidates and improves ASEAN’s existing free trade agreements with its so-called ASEAN+1 dialogue partners. Although all RCEP countries signed up to a common trade and investment liberalisation goal, the agreement – as with ASEAN’s existing FTAs – allows each member flexibility on timeline. RCEP resembles the ASEAN Economic Community (AEC) agreement, effective since 2015, that allowed the relatively less developed economies of Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, and Vietnam to liberalise at a slower speed than the other six ASEAN member states. Individual ASEAN countries have taken advantage of this RCEP provision by complying with trade facilitation, trade in goods and services, and investment rules. ASEAN countries have different approaches to investment and trade in services, with some adopting a ‘positive’ list – whereby only sectors that are listed will be open to competition from other RCEP members – while others have adopted a ‘negative’ listPositive list membersNegative list membersCambodiaBruneiLaosIndonesiaMyanmarMalaysiaThe PhilippinesSingaporeThailandVietnamSource: IHS Markit© 2020 IHS MarkitAustralia and Japan will likely co-operate in future RCEP negotiations to counter-balance China, including by encouraging India to rejoin the group. Despite growing economic distrust towards China, it is very likely that the scope for increasing diversification through RCEP motivated Australia and Japan to conclude negotiations. For Japan, RCEP meets a key demand of maintaining high import tariffs on five agriculture products while also providing tariff-free export on 86% of its goods that go to China (up from a current 8%). Australia and Japan probably also assess that there is potential to counter-balance China in future negotiations, given increased bilateral co-ordination via the Supply Chain Resilience Initiative (SCRI; see Australia-Japan-India: 27 August 2020: Domestic considerations signal strong intent to advance Australia-Japan-India supply chain initiative, but protracted negotiations will likely culminate in 2021). Both countries will likely encourage India’s return to the group, which specifically has a provision in the current RCEP agreement. However, India is unlikely to join, given its large trade deficit with China – which reached about USD60 billion in 2019 – and its demand to reduce tariffs in dairy and e-commerce sectors, given trade associations’ concerns about domestic markets being flooded with Chinese goods (see India: 5 November 2019: India’s withdrawal from Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership reflects domestic opposition; pending ratification likely to boost intra-Asia trade).Indicators of changing risk environmentIncreasing riskMost countries have yet to offer a timeline for ratifying RCEP. Any delay in doing so would negate its economic impact and increase scope for renegotiations.The attendance of senior members from the incoming US administration under President-elect Joe Biden in 2021’s key Asian economic forums, such as the East Asia Summit, would signal stronger US interest in Asia-Pacific economic multilateral platforms compared with the Trump administration, potentially diluting US-allied Asian countries’ focus on RCEP.Although Australia's opposition Labor party supports RCEP, if it uses the deal’s profile to increase pressure on the government to confront China on ongoing economic disagreements, then this would delay a domestic ratification of RCEP but not yet threaten Australia’s exit.Decreasing riskThe ASEAN Secretariat currently functions as a temporary secretariat for RCEP. The establishment of a separate RCEP secretariat would indicate that the new grouping is making progress in implementing the agreement.Progress by China on developing a joint code of conduct with South China Sea claimants, particularly with the Philippines and Vietnam, would signal Chinese intent to prioritise economic and trade over issues of territorial disputes.Guaranteed exemptions for India to avoid tariff reductions in critical sectors would encourage that country to rejoin negotiations, but it would remain unlikely to ratify the agreement under the current administration of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, incumbent until 2024. © 2020, IHS Markit Inc. Both countries will likely encourage India’s return to the group, which specifically has a provision in the current RCEP agreement. However, India is unlikely to join, given its large trade deficit with China – which reached about USD60 billion in 2019 – and its demand to reduce tariffs in dairy and e-commerce sectors, given trade associations’ concerns about domestic markets being flooded with Chinese goods (see India: 5 November 2019: India’s withdrawal from Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership reflects domestic opposition; pending ratification likely to boost intra-Asia trade).Indicators of changing risk environmentIncreasing riskMost countries have yet to offer a timeline for ratifying RCEP. Headline: UPDATE - Australia: Fatalities reported due to ongoing bushfires in New South Wales and Queensland; over 125 fires burning
Details: Australian authorities have confirmed that four people have died as a result of the ongoing bushfires in New South Wales (NSW) and Queensland. Firefighters are continuing to battle over 125 fires in both of the states, 70 in Queensland and more than 55 in NSW. On Thursday, a coalition of former fire chiefs accused the government of ignoring their warnings about climate change and its potential to exacerbate fire emergencies. Residents of two Queensland towns were told to leave immediately as bushfires in the areas worsened, while NSW authorities warned fire conditions could deteriorate as the weekend approached. The most significant blazes burning as of midday Thursday are at Noosa North Shore on the Sunshine Coast, Woodgate and Black Snake. A 16 year old boy has been arrested by police for deliberately starting a fire. The alleged arson has destroyed 14 homes around the town of Yeppoon, 650km (400 miles) north of Brisbane, Queensland.

Headline: Chinese Authorities Arrest At Least Ten Hong Kong Activists Believed to Be Fleeing to Taiwan
Details:
On Thursday, media sources indicated that Chinese authorities have arrested at least ten people believed to be Hong Kong activists fleeing to Taiwan via speedboat to seek political asylum. According to reports, China’s coast guard intercepted the vessel off the coast of the southern province of Guangdong on August 23. Among the detainees were two people who had previously been arrested on charges related to last year's anti-government protests, one of which is regarded as a prominent pro-democracy activist. It was not immediately clear what charges have been levied against those in custody, though they are reportedly thought to include unlawfully crossing the border. If convicted, the detainees could face one year in jail before being deported to Hong Kong.



Assessment: Regional media outlets report that many members of the pro-democracy movement have begun fleeing Hong Kong in fear over the new national security law that took effect June 30, many to Taiwan, which has set up an office to help those from Hong Kong seeking to emigrate. The application of the national security law, which criminalizes and imposes strict penalties for offenses against the government, potentially including acts previously protected by the Basic Law, such as freedom of speech and assembly, has seen a wave of arrests of activists in recent weeks. Together, the developments seemingly reduce the likelihood of a resumption of major protest activity in the foreseeable future; however, it also perpetuates uncertainty among private sector organizations operating in the territory, particularly over what could be interpreted as a violation of the national security law.

Headline: Operation Brock initiated on M20 in Kent
Details: On March 25, authorities initiated Operation Brock on the M20 in Kent as part of the government s plan to manage gridlock in the event of a no-deal Brexit. The system to manage truck and passenger vehicle traffic to and from the Kentish coast, including the port of Dover, is being coordinated with Kent police and local authorities along the motorway. The operation includes the coast-bound side of the M20 between Junctions 8 (Maidstone) and 9 (Ashford) being solely for truck traffic heading to Dover, serving as a holding space for trucks during congestion periods, though truck traffic remained free-flowing Monday. The dedicated 14-mile stretch will enable trucks to move along based on truck congestion levels, while all other traffic moving in both coast- and London-bound directions travels on the London-bound side of the motorway. The London-bound side in the affected stretch is thus divided with barriers for two lanes of traffic to the coast and two lanes of traffic to London. The anticipated duration of Operation Brock was not immediately announced by authorities.

Headline: Annual maintenance schedule for Three Gorges Dam Lock System released
Details:
This week, the intended maintenance schedule for the Three Gorges Dam Lock System has been issued by the Chinese Ministry of Transport. The timelines for the maintenance works were said to be as follows:

-	Three Gorges South Line Ship Lock: The overhaul time of the Three Gorges Ship Lock in 2018 shall begin on February 19 from 08:00 AM and will last for 33 days.
-	Gezhou Dam No. 1 Ship Lock: The overhaul time of the Gezhou Dam No. 1 Lock in 2018 shall begin on February 26 from 08:00 AM and will last for 20 days.

Please note that the approximate average waiting time to pass through the Dam was 15 days during the Three Gorges’ North Ship lock maintenance in 2017, which impacted the transit time to upper Yangtze River areas. Therefore, this maintenance will impact cargo transshipped via Shanghai. In addition, as of December 2017, barge companies, including COSCO, reportedly delayed space confirmation by at least one week due to extreme congestion at the Three Gorges Dam, and imposed a congestion surcharge to cover increasing local costs. Transit times to Shanghai were on average taking 10 days longer. Customers are advised to consider alternative transport modes, including a rail service from Chongqing to Qinzhou for westbound shipments to India and Southeast Asia.

Headline: Port Drivers and Warehouse Workers Stage Three-Day Strike at Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach
Details:
On Monday, port drivers and warehouse workers at the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach commenced a three-day strike. The group Justice for Port Drivers, sponsored by the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, alleges that XPO Logistics and NFI Industries are committing wage theft, exploiting drivers, and discriminating by misclassifying drivers as independent contractors, also known as owner-operators. During the strike, workers are expected to picket conduct leafleting at company facilities, marine terminals, rail yards, and at customer warehouses and distribution centers. 
 
	Assessment: This is the 16 th  strike staged by Justice for Port Drivers in the past five years. The previous strikes resulted in minimal or no impact on cargo flow at the port complex. Port police are reportedly positioned at terminals to ensure operations can continue during these strikes. As of late Monday morning, a spokesperson for the Port of Los Angeles stated that there has been no impact on cargo flow. XPO Logistics also indicated that it does not expect any impact on customers or disruptions to its operations.

Headline: New COVID-19 measures at Port of  Tanjung Priok
Details:
Media sources report that Indonesia’s Ministry of Health has issued new instructions for the crew on vessels calling at the port of Tanjung Priok, as follows:  
1.	Every crew member who will start their task on a ship is required to validate the RDT (Rapid Diagnostic Test) or PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) certificate before joining the ship, minimum 1 day before the ship’s departure. This is to avoid close contact with the crew on the ship if the result is reactive/positive.

2.	If the RDT result is reactive, crew member must do the PCR test, not join the ship and self-isolate for 14 days, or until the PCR result is negative.

3.	If the PCR result is positive, crew member must be treated with the help of the Covid19 Handling Task Force.

4.	If the crew member is already on the ship and just checked the RDT, and the result is reactive, there will be a PCR test for all crew members who have contact, and the ship will be disinfected. Before the PCR result is issued, the ship will be quarantined.
|
5.	To avoid this disease, there are several things that need to be considered, as follows:
a. Using PPE (Personal Protective Equipment) such as masks for officers who have a high risk of contact with sufferers who are asymptomatic.
b. Always keep healthy and clean such as close the nose and mouth when coughing or sneezing, washing hands with soap, not exchanging drinking bottles, maintaining immune condition.
c. If you have a fever, cough, shortness of breath, contact the health officer immediately.
d. The traveler to an infected area is encouraged to pay attention to the spread of this disease, to avoid places where the disease is infected, and to avoid direct contact with people who have a fever, cough, and shortness of breath.

Headline: UPDATE 50 - 51 miles northeast of Richmond - Storm Laura dissipated off the coast of Virginia. Event closed.
Details:
Laura dissipated off the coast of Virginia after making landfall as a Category 4 hurricane. As a tropical storm after weakening from hurricane-force winds, Laura was impacting the Gulf Coast, including severe power outages and at least one tornado touching down in Gueydan, Louisiana, and at least two in Craighead and Forrest City, Arkansas. A total of 16 people were killed, several of whom were affected by carbon monoxide inhalation. Significant damage to buildings was reported, including a partial collapse at St Patrick’s Hospital in Lake Charles. Debris has left many roadways impassable, and thousands of residents remain without power and water.
 
In advance of Hurricane Laura making landfall, hundreds of thousands of people in coastal Louisiana and southeast Texas were given evacuation orders and/or curfews. In addition, the majority of oil production in the Gulf of Mexico was halted, ports were closed, and public transportation disruptions were reported along coastal regions. 
 
Life-threatening storm surge and high tides were also reported along the Gulf Coast. Minor to moderate river flooding has occurred or was forecast in Louisiana, Arkansas, and northern Mississippi. The coastal areas of Louisiana and Texas continue to experience flooding from the rain and storm surge. Expect residual disruptions as cleanup and repair efforts remain ongoing. This event is closed.

Workers at Ghent and Zeebrugge are also affected by the walk outs. It is unclear when the strike action will end. Travellers are advised to monitor local news reports for additional information and contact their transport provider if affected by any of the ship movement at the port.

Headline: Police Fire Tear Gas at Protesters in Mong Kok Area of Hong Kong; May Be a Sign of Lull Ending
Details:
On Sunday, police fired tear gas to disperse around 100 protesters at Langham Place shopping center in the Mong Kok area of Hong Kong. Tear gas and pepper balls were used in other areas of Mong Kok as well to disperse demonstrators, who police said were blocking roads, throwing objects like glass bottles, and committing acts of vandalism. Police said that 27 rounds of tear gas were fired in total. The protests were part of a  shop with you  action held in multiple shopping centers across the city. Police also stormed the New Town Plaza in Sha Tin, where protesters vandalized restaurants operated by Maxim. Clashes between protesters and police were also reported at Telford Plaza in Kowloon Bay. Other gatherings took place at Metroplaza in Kwai Fong, Times Square in Causeway Bay, PopCorn in Tsueng Kwan O, Cityplaza in Tai Koo Shing, and Harbour City in Tsim Sha Tsui. A smoke bomb was also thrown at a bus stop near the Sha Tin Mass Transit Railway (MTR). At least 31 people were arrested during the protests and five people were injured. No major clashes were reported at other demonstrations in the city involving pro-Beijing supporters and social workers.

Earlier in the afternoon, police found a suspicious object in Tsing Yi that resembled an explosive device. The item appeared to be two ten-inch tubes that were bound together with tape and attached by red and black wires. Police said that there were no explosives or chemicals found inside the item, suggesting that was a hoax to divert police attention or cause panic. At least 30 people were evacuated from the vicinity while bomb crews disposed of the device. Police also arrested three people on Saturday in Tuen Mun that were allegedly testing remote detonators for bombs. The specific chemicals the suspects were using were unknown, as the devices had already been detonated.

Assessment: The protests were effectively a repeat of the  shop with you  actions that were held on November 10 at multiple shopping centers across Hong Kong, which also saw clashes and police using tear gas. The clashes on Sunday were the first time tear gas had been fired since violent demonstrations in Kowloon on December 1. The widespread protests on Sunday, while still smaller than many of the actions in October and early November, demonstrate that a sizable minority of protesters still have the motivation and capability to carry out disruptive protests in multiple locations at the same time. The resumption of violent protests could be tied to the Hong Kong government still refusing to make any additional concessions or substantively respond to the outcome of the local district council elections in late November, which further convinces radical protesters that they cannot rely on peaceful or political solutions to achieve their goals. While it remains unclear if Hong Kong will return to the level of violence seen in past months, the protests on Sunday represent a deterioration of the security situation when compared to the past two weeks, and there is a moderate risk of the protests escalating again in the near future. It is also concerning that police have foiled two plots involving remote-detonated explosives within a week, with the other plot involving fully functional explosives being found at a college in Wan Chai ahead of the major protest on December 8. If a bombing were to cause significant casualties among police officers or protesters, the security situation would likely sharply deteriorate. Customers are advised to be hyper aware of their surroundings and avoid all areas where protesters appear to be gathering due to the high risk of clashes.

Headline: US Embassy Issued an Alert Regarding COVID-19 Checkpoints and Testing
Details:
On Wednesday, the US Embassy in Vietnam issued the following alert:



“Location:  Vietnam 



Event:  The U.S. Embassy Hanoi and Consulate General Ho Chi Minh City are providing U.S. citizens with information during the evolving Coronavirus (COVID-19) situation in Vietnam.



According to the Vietnamese Ministry of Health, Vietnam has had 446 confirmed cases of COVID-19 within its borders since the virus first became known.



         369 people have recovered and were released from the hospital.



         77 cases are being isolated for treatment.



After 99 days without any cases of community transmission, Vietnam recently confirmed new cases of community transmission in Da Nang, Quang Nam, and Quang Ngai, which led to the reintroduction of social distancing measures throughout these cities and other regions deemed high-risk.



Update:



Vietnamese media report that several central provinces, including Kon Tum, Lam Dong, Quang Nam, and Thua Thien Hue, have established multiple checkpoints to screen travelers in an effort to detect suspected COVID-19 cases. Given the current COVID-19 situation in Vietnam, other localities may take similar measures without prior notice.



Authorities in both Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City have required some people who have returned from Da Nang to be tested.  The U.S. Embassy Hanoi and Consulate General Ho Chi Minh City encourage U.S. citizens to comply with local authorities.



Hanoi has implemented a city-wide requirement for everyone to wear face masks in public.



U.S. citizens are encouraged to re-evaluate upcoming travel and consider the risk of COVID-19 transmission as well as travel disruptions that may occur as a result of the evolving situation. The Vietnamese Ministry of Transportation announced that all passengers using public means of transport (bus, taxi, trains, planes, ships, etc.) must complete an online health declaration before the trip and minimize contact with othersduring the trip.



We recommend U.S. citizens check the Embassy’s COVID-19 page daily for information.”

Headline: CMA CGM Hit by Ransomware Attack; Cyberattacks on the Rise in the Logistics Industry
Details:
Over the weekend of Saturday, September 27, and Sunday, September 28, the French shipping container liner company CMA CGM was targeted by a ransomware cyberattack. CMA CGM’s website and the websites of some of its subsidiaries were unavailable, except for the group’s corporate website. While initially the company stated that the issues were caused by problems with internal IT infrastructure, the situation was confirmed to be due to a cyberattack through a message on the corporate website’s homepage, as well as through a social media post by the Vice President, Joel Gentil. The Ceva Logistics subsidiary was reportedly unaffected, and the CMA CGM network remained mostly available to customers for booking and operations requests. Booking and operations services were disrupted at several Chinese offices, including Shanghai, Shenzhen, and Guangzhou. Hackers used Ragnar Locker data encryption ransomware in the attack, but external access to CMA CGM applications was purportedly interrupted when the breach was detected, preventing the malware from spreading. The full extent of the breach remains unclear. On Sunday, September 28, the hackers responsible allegedly contacted CMA CGM via email demanding to be contacted through live chat within two days to pay for a decryption key; however the price has not been disclosed. An investigation into how CMA CGM systems became infected is underway.



Assessment: CMA CGM is the world’s fourth-largest shipping container liner. The top three largest shipping liners have all been victims of cyberattacks in recent years, with Maersk in 2017, Cosco in 2018, and Mediterranean Shipping Co in 2020. The 2017 Maersk attack was reportedly collateral damage of the NotPetya cyberattack concentrated on Ukraine, and resulted in 12 days of disrupted activities and approximately $300 million in losses for the company. Logistics companies have purportedly been increasingly targeted in cyberattacks, with multimodal and automotive logistics company GEFCO suffering a breach on September 20 this year. Increased digitization of shipping and port operations are likely to contribute to increased vulnerability of the industry to cyberattacks in the future. It is advised to monitor developments associated with the investigation into the CMA CGM attack, as well as new information regarding the extent of the breach. It is also advised to monitor industry trends related to digitization and cybersecurity measures adopted by corporations in the sector as means of safeguarding internal infrastructure against future attacks.

Headline: Search Efforts Continue After Ship Capsized Off Japan; Cattle Exports from New Zealand Suspended
Details:
Japanese authorities reported on Thursday that a cargo ship, the Gulf Livestock 1, had capsized in the East China Sea, about 115 miles west of Kagoshima Prefecture’s Amami Oshima. The ship sent a distress signal early Wednesday morning local time while in the area of Typhoon Maysak. A single crew member was rescued by the Japan Coast Guard on Wednesday night. As of this writing, no further sign of the ship or wreckage has been discovered.



Assessment: The Gulf Livestock 1 was transporting nearly 6,000 cattle from Napier, New Zealand, to the Port of Jingtang in Tangshan, China. According to the crew member who was rescued, a Filipino national, the ship suffered engine trouble before capsizing under high waves. An additional 42 crew members remain missing, including 38 Filipinos, two Australians, and two New Zealanders. Search and rescue efforts were initially delayed by the ongoing typhoon, but Japanese authorities report that weather has now cleared and operations are continuing. The Gulf Livestock 1 was a 450-foot cargo ship, constructed in 2002 and weighing 11,947 tons. The ship was registered in Panama. Officials in New Zealand have temporarily suspended cattle exports as an investigation into the ship’s situation is conducted.

Headline: Additional Shipping Delays Possible Amid Ongoing Dispute Between Patrick Terminals and Dockworkers
Details:
On Wednesday, an ongoing dispute between dockworkers with the Maritime Union of Australia (MUA) and Patrick Terminals will be brought before the Fair Work Commission. The dispute, centering on pay and working conditions, has led to some delays to shipping, particularly at Sydney’s Port Botany. While the union has acknowledged an overtime ban is in place, it has denied any other industrial action has been carried out recently. One-day strikes that had been planned at Port Botany and Brisbane for this coming Friday have been canceled. Media sources reported on Wednesday morning local time that the MUA had offered to keep current working arrangements with Patrick for the next year in exchange for a 2.5 percent raise for workers.



Assessment: The MUA ended a similar dispute with DP World last Friday, while a resolution with Hutchison Ports is expected soon. According to Patrick, the MUA’s overtime ban has cost it 31 percent of its crane teams at ports across Australia, with Port Botany even more affected. The company has stated that as many as 40 ships and up to 90,000 containers have been delayed from unloading, including medical supplies. The union has denied this, instead saying that there have been only minor delays, which it has attributed to the company canceling several recent night shifts. It is not immediately clear whether the offer made by the MUA on Wednesday will resolve the dispute. It is advised to follow developments should disruptions and delays to shipping continue from the labor dispute or in case of further strike actions.

Headline: Labour strikes: Expansion of hotel workers' strike indicates growing...
Details: On 20 September 2018, striking hotel workers from seven hotels in Chicago agreed to terms with Marriott International, ending a two-week strike. The hotel workers, organised by the UNITE HERE Local 1 union, sought wage increases, year-round health insurance coverage for workers laid-off during slower seasons, pensions, additional sick leave, and more favourable workloads. Hotel workers representing 19 additional Chicago hotels are continuing their strike, begun 7 September against various other international hotel chains operating in the city. On 17 September, UNITE HERE hotel workers in Detroit voted to authorise a strike action against Marriott, seeking similar terms to the Chicago strikers. This follows similar votes by UNITE HERE hotel workers in Boston, Hawaii, Oakland, San Diego, San Francisco, San Jose, and Seattle. Although the strikes have spread nationwide, none of them have been violent or led to damage to properties. Furthermore, none of the individual unions have called for violence.Although most hotel operators have insisted that disruptions have been minimal, there have been various media reports presenting anecdotal evidence of long check-in delays, disruptions to cleaning services, and the closure of hotel restaurants. Furthermore, two political organisations, the Democratic Attorneys General Association and the LGBTQ Health Symposium, cancelled their Chicago events in support of the strikers. Chicago's city-wide hotel strikes, the largest of their kind since 1903, represent the latest in a growing trend of work stoppages, including those involving prisoners, telecommunications workers, and teachers. According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the number of major work stoppages nationwide involving 1,000 workers or more fell from approximately 350 annually in the 1970s to seven in 2017. However, per a report by Jacobin magazine, this number has more than doubled to 16 during 2018. With unemployment at 3.8%, replacing striking workers is difficult for firms. Thus, many of the strikes, as seen in the hotel example above, have been successful in accomplishing their aims and will probably provide an impetus for other employees nationwide in sectors like tourism, telecommunications, fast-food, and education. Most notably, UNITE HERE appears to have prepared well, by increasing dues prior to the action so that they could provide strike wages during the impasse. There is no precedent of notable violence during such strikes and there is no evidence to suggest this will change in the coming months. However, they are likely to last weeks or months, as shown in previous strikes with telecom firms and schools, severely disrupting business operations. Indeed, statements by the hotel union suggested that they were willing to strike months to obtain a favourable resolution to their demands. Any delay in Marriott opening negotiations with hotel workers in cities that have already authorised but not yet commenced striking would increase the likelihood of strikes in these locations, as the hotel chain has already demonstrated a willingness to address strikers' contract demands. Furthermore, shippers/consignees may need to produce declarations confirming ability of facilities to handle cargo, and inbound cargo can proceed as long as the shipper and consignee are aligned for movement. Furthermore, only 33% of customs officers are allowed to operate in Chennai's air & sea ports, so a noticeable customs operational impact is anticipated.

Headline: Operation Brock Initiated on M20 in Kent as Preparation for Possible No-Deal Brexit Congestion
Details:
On Monday, authorities initiated Operation Brock on the M20 in Kent as part of the government s plan to manage gridlock in the event of a no-deal Brexit. The system to manage truck and passenger vehicle traffic to and from the Kentish coast, including the port of Dover, is being coordinated with Kent police and local authorities along the motorway. The operation includes the coast-bound side of the M20 between Junctions 8 (Maidstone) and 9 (Ashford) being solely for truck traffic heading to Dover, serving as a holding space for trucks during congestion periods, though truck traffic remained free-flowing Monday. The dedicated 14-mile stretch will enable trucks to move along based on truck congestion levels, while all other traffic moving in both coast- and London-bound directions travels on the London-bound side of the motorway. The London-bound side in the affected stretch is thus divided with barriers for two lanes of traffic to the coast and two lanes of traffic to London. The anticipated duration of Operation Brock was not immediately announced by authorities. 
 
	Assessment: With a potential Brexit date recently pushed back to at least April 12, questions have been raised about the purpose of continuing with the no-deal contingency scenario at this time. Operation Brock is a replacement of the previous M20 traffic management system called Operation Stack. In the new system, up to 11,000 trucks are expected to be able to fit into the M20 queuing procedure. Should further space be required, the government has backup provisions for directing trucks to the disused Manston airport as well as the coast bound M26. Although government officials have said checks would not be carried out at Dover in the short term following a no-deal Brexit to avoid heavy disruption, the Dover Harbour Board warned last week that an increase of two minutes per vehicle bound for France undergoing checks could result in 17-mile queues. Resilience360 customers are advised to anticipate possible disruptions while Operation Brock remains in effect and to continue monitoring associated developments that may impact cross-Channel traffic and the United Kingdom s planned separation from the European Union.

Headline: South Korean customs seize smuggled North Korean coal
Details: Local media sources reported on March 26 that South Korean customs authorities in Busan detected two illegal imports of North Korean coal on March 7 (12,325 tons) and January 2 (1,590 tons) this year. Three importers - including an agent of a maritime brokerage company - were arrested for disguising the coal as Chinese and Vietnamese coal and violating trade tariffs. Customs authorities have expressed concerns about international sanctions and the U.S. secondary boycott as some of the illegally imported North Korean coal was sold and used domestically and delivered to South Korean steel mills. The United Nations is believed to be investigating North Korean coal being transported through transshipment from Russia including the Port of Kholmsk.

The US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) revealed that the pork arrived in more than 50 shipping containers over the past few weeks and was hidden in containers of ramen noodles and laundry detergent packaging. The CBP believes that these pork products were smuggled with the original Chinese food ingredients covered by English packaging labels that deliberately did not mention that the products contained pork

Headline: Protests against Police Use of Force Devolve into Violent Unrest across Colombia; More Riots Likely
Details:
From Wednesday night through Thursday morning, a wave of protests erupted throughout Colombia. Numerous demonstrations devolved into broader episodes of unrest, entailing arson and/or violent altercations with security forces. The catalyst behind the tumult was the death of 44-year-old law student Javier Ordoñez, which occurred the previous night.



According to Bogotá Police Commander Colonel Alexander Amaya, Tuesday evening’s incident began when Colombian National Police (PNC) officers responded to a group of intoxicated individuals who were arguing in the street in Bogotá’s Villa Luz neighborhood. Amaya claims that some members of the group became aggressive towards police. Officers placed Ordoñez under arrest, and witnesses recorded the incident on video. The recording depicts Ordoñez being pinned to the ground and tased by two police officers. Shortly thereafter, Ordoñez was pronounced dead while in police custody. The video of his arrest was widely circulated on social media the following day. 



A range of activist groups organized protests against police use of force on Wednesday, in cities including Bogotá, Medellín, Barranquilla, and Cali. As nightfall came, crowds at many demonstrations grew increasingly unruly. Rioting ensued in multiple locations, with the worst unrest being reported in Bogotá, particularly in the districts of Bosa, Engativá, Suba, and Kennedy. Demonstrators threw Molotov cocktails at police substations (CAIs) and engaged in widespread vandalism of public property. Security forces responded with tear gas and rubber bullets, and in some cases with live ammunition.



Although estimates regarding casualties have been subject to variation, local news outlets have reported that as many as eight protesters were killed nationwide. Two of the deceased demonstrators were reportedly killed by gunshots in the city of Soacha, which borders Bogotá to the southwest. Bogotá municipal authorities report that 248 protesters were wounded across the capital, including 58 individuals who sustained gunshot wounds. PNC spokesmen have indicated that 114 officers were wounded in the clashes. Media sources report that at least 30 CAIs were destroyed, 25 police motorcycles were damaged, and eight TransMilenio city buses were set on fire. Authorities report that 33 arrests were made in Bogotá, 15 in Madrid, six in Ibagué, three in Mosquera, one in Medellín, and one in Cali. 



Assessment: Defense Minister Carlos Holmes Trujillo held a press conference on Thursday morning. He condemned acts of excessive use of force among law enforcement, but also noted that various social media accounts were actively fomenting unrest and encouraging vandalism throughout the country. Bogotá Mayor Claudia López has claimed that the PNC is in need of major structural reforms, stating that “141 complaints of police abuse so far this year in Bogotá are not isolated cases.” 



Additional street manifestations have been planned across the country for Thursday night. Tensions throughout Bogotá and other large cities across Colombia will almost certainly remain elevated in the coming days and possibly weeks, and the potential for further public demonstrations will remain high. The public is advised to frequently monitor local news outlets, as impromptu bouts of protest activity could potentially crop up with little or no warning. All large crowds should be avoided as much as possible, as even demonstrations that are intended to be peaceful can rapidly escalate and devolve into violent rioting.

Headline: UPDATE 1 - 73 miles W of San Antonio de los Cobres - A magnitude 4.0 earthquake has struck in the area. Event closed.
Details:
The European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre is reporting that a magnitude 4.0 earthquake has struck approximately 73 miles W of San Antonio de los Cobres, Argentina. There were no immediate reports of injuries or major structural damage. Event closed.
EMSC (European Mediterranean Seismological Centre) is a scientific international organization, which aggregates and provides information generated by national seismological agencies worldwide. EMSC presents earthquake data across several magnitude scales including local magnitude (ML), surface-wave magnitude (Ms), body-wave magnitude (Mb), and moment magnitude (Mw). All magnitude scales should yield approximately the same value for any given earthquake.

Headline: Eastern China   Cleanup operations continue after flooding impacted the area. Incident closed.
Details:
Media sources reported that heavy rainfall from the remnants of Tropical Storm Rumbia caused flooding in the eastern provinces of Shandong, Liaoning, Jiangsu, Anhui, and Henan. Flooding was reported in Quanzhou City. At least 32 people were killed since Rumbia made landfall including 14 people killed in Shandong and 12 people killed in Anhui. At least 15 people were missing. One police officer participating in rescue operations was killed in Shouguang and one other police officer went missing. More than 10,000 firefighters were deployed to Shouguang due to the flooding. 

Approximately 140,000 people were displaced, including 102,800 in Shandong Province and 37,800 in Liaoning Province. More than 34,400 homes were damaged, an estimated 110,000 greenhouse farms were damaged, and almost 820,000 acres of cropland was destroyed. The damage to crops in Shouguang caused Shandong to raise produce prices. Flooding reportedly caused economic losses of US$ 1.45 billion in Shandong. Residual disruptions may persist as cleanup operations continue. This incident is closed.

Headline: Fort Wayne, Green Bay, and Hopkins   UNFI workers to resume work; strike over. Incident closed.
Details: Media sources reported that workers at United Natural Foods, Inc. (UNFI) distribution centers in Fort Wayne, Green Bay, and Hopkins are expected to return to work, officially ending their strike that was initiated over perceived unfair labor practices following the expiration of a collective bargaining agreement. The strike started on December 12 with Teamsters Local 414 union at the Fort Wayne UNFI distribution center, located on Investment Dr near Production Rd. Two UNFI distribution centers in Green Bay, Wisconsin and Hopkins, Minnesota joined the strike later to show solitary. The warehouse in Green Bay is located near Joannes Ave and S Broadway and the warehouse in Hopkins is located near Jefferson Ave S and 3rd St. At least 700 Teamsters Local 120 members participated in the strike in Hopkins and 150 Teamsters Local 662 participated in Green Bay. The strike included UNFI drivers, warehouse workers, and maintenance workers. Picket lines were reported at the participating distribution centers during the strike. The workers supply food and related products to grocery stores, and the strike was affecting customers in Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, Kentucky, Michigan, West Virginia, and Kentucky. In the U.S. and Canada, UNFI is the largest wholesale distributor to natural and organic retailers. Domestically, UNFI is the second-largest grocery wholesaler, and supplies and distributes wholesale groceries to over 3,000 owned, franchised and affiliated stores across the U.S., including Whole Foods and Amazon. This incident is closed.

Headline: 900 juice boxes worth USD 6,000 stolen from Dubai warehouse
Details: Local media sources reported on March 19, 2019 that 900 juice boxes worth over Rs 4 lakh (USD 6,000 or EUR 5,100) were stolen from a food catering company's warehouse in Dubai. According to the police report, a warehouse keeper and two transportation workers were arrested after they embezzled the juice boxes between April 2017 and May 2018 from the company's branch. The warehouse keeper allowed the two accomplices to keep a large quantity of juice boxes, when the deliveries were made, instead of depositing them at the warehouse. They sold the juice later. The theft came into limelight after auditor discovered a deficit in their books. During the investigation, the main defendant confessed he agreed to his accomplices' plan of stealing 100 boxes from each delivery.

Headline: UPDATE 8 - Michigan - The safer-at-home order was lifted; businesses and industries reopened. Event closed.
Details:
New Updates: 

Governor Gretchen Whitmer lifted the statewide safer-at-home order on June 1. Numerous businesses and industries were reopened, including retailers on June 4 and restaurants on June 8. A number of restrictions and rules were also rolled back. All regions of the state are in Phase 4 or Phase 5 of the MI Safe Start Plan. This event is closed.

Previous Updates:

Governor Gretchen Whitmer extended and modified an executive order through June 12 requiring all residents to stay at home statewide to slow the spread of COVID-19. This extension includes some modifications to previous restrictions, including easing of restrictions for some industries. It also requires people to wear masks when in enclosed public spaces. 

Manufacturing workers are permitted to return to work. Additionally, landscapers, plant nurseries, and bicycle repair shops are being allowed to resume operation, while other businesses selling non-essential supplies will be allowed to open for curbside pickup and delivery. Restaurants, bars, movie theaters, and gyms remain closed. In addition, some restaurants and bars in the Traverse City and Upper Peninsula regions have been allowed to partially reopen. Retail stores and auto dealerships will be permitted to reopen beginning May 25 for appointments. Non-essential dental, medical, and veterinary procedures will also be allowed to resume.

This relaxing of restrictions in is accordance with a six-phase reopening plan developed by the Michigan Government. The plan will loosen restrictions based on several metrics including the rate of virus spread. The state’s 83 counties have been divided into eight regions, two of which, the Upper Peninsula and Traverse City regions, have passed into the fourth “Improving” phase, while the other six remain in the third “Flattening” phase. The regional divisions are as follows:

- Detroit Region: Genesee County, Lapper County, Livingston County, Macomb County, Monroe County, Oakland County, St. Clair County, Washtenaw County, and Wayne County

- Grand Rapids Region: Clare County, Ionia County, Isabella County, Kent County, Lake County, Mason County, Mecosta County, Montcalm County, Muskegon County, Newaygo County, Oceana County, Ottawa County, and Osceola County
